Disclaimer - This is being written just after the finishing the campaign.
Bastion is an excellent game, and I have no idea what took me so long to jump on this train and play it! Gameplay is excellent, tight responsive combat with exceptional diversity in player weapons and attacks being tossed against a wildly unique plethora of enemies. This freedom allows for great player choice in playstyle, and no matter how weak certain weapons may feel when you first get them, the upgrade system greatly assists and closing any stat disparities by the end of the game, though some (lookin' at you, Carbine) because borderline overpowered by virtue of their upgrades.
The story is excellent - your character, The Kid, is a post-apocalyptic janitor, trying to restore his people's safehold, the Bastion, while encountering the remainder of the world doing the best they can to stop him. Philosophical posturing is the flavor of the over-arching story, and the excellent narration of The Old Man breathes live into gameplay elements in a wildly unique way - I found myself disappointed whenever I accidentally cut the narrator short when jumping from one place to another, causing me to wait those extra ten or fifteen seconds to snap up every second of dialogue before taking the portals to the next sounds.
Of course everyone has spoken about the art style for Bastion, but it really is top-notch. Consistent color palettes and tediously hand-crafted tile sets give nearly every zone a unique flavor. The judicious use of color filtering during 'cut-scenes,' (if you can call them that), starkly emphasize, rather than detract, the mood and tone.
On top of the art is the music and sound direction for the game - again, thematically consistent and spectacularly accurate at helping to convey the message the game is presenting at any given time. Fast-paced and flowing music during combat really help to get the blood flowing, while the haunting melodies during introspective and questioning scenes draw your attention into the game in top form.
Truly, the thematic style of Bastion, both artistically and musically, create an environment that gently coaxes the player, rather than forcing or asking, into full suspension of disbelief. I found myself losing track of time, and truly, a sense of physical reality, as I fell further and further into the world of Bastion.
While secondary content is available after beating the game, it exists on the level of replaying missions for score points on a global leaderboard, or trying to complete more difficult challenges. To the best of my knowledge, completing the game once reveals its main content, and while playability still exists after beating the main story campaign, it is simply a repitition of the story with greater challenge.
My only misgiving's with Bastion are the tile based maps - while fresh and interesting, I sometimes found myself relying a bit too heavily on the rising tiles to direct my movement through the map - I found that the tiles implicitly discouraged exploring the maps because of invisible boundaries. It seemed inconsistent whether one path or another would yield progress in the level, and only by comitting one way for a few minutes could you really be sure where you were going, which always left me wondering whether I had missed any side paths. All in all, a very minor complaint.
Final Verdict - 9/10. If you have the means, I highly recommend playing it. Watching it on youtube or reading a review can only provide a transparent facsimile of what makes Bastion special - its the experience that the game provides via your choices in game that really leave a lasting impact.

Bastion is a very stylized isometric action game in which you play a young character who finds himself awaken shortly after the apocalypse. As you explore, the world fills in around you. Bastion's strengths are three main areas: first, how it tells the story. The actions of the player are narrated by a fantastic voice actor, providing a feeling of having the tale be told as you play it out, which is very unique among games. Secondly, it has an amazing soundtrack, which I don't know exactly how to describe - maybe Electronic Folk? Anyway, it absolutely has one of the best soundtracks of any game I've ever played. Finally, the story itself, which I obviously don't want to spoil in the review, so I'll leave you to that.
There's a fair amount of replayability and challenges to complete if the player is so inclined - I personally chose to play through once and enjoyed it as that. At any rate, the most important thing is this: buy this game, and when you do, buy the soundtrack.

Many people will try and persuade you not to buy Starbound, them complaining that the developers are never going to finish the game because of whatever reason. What don't they realize? Games take a long time to develop! It was a bad move surely for the developers to have published the game on Steam so early on, but this was because they needed funding.
The developers aren't some large company that can pitch out a game every year to make mad money, I'm looking at you Assassin's Creed and Call of Duty, no but instead a smaller company that doesn't have all the resources to pump out a large game in record time. Starbound is honestly a great game and it's a fun game to play, mainly with a group of friends, that has entertained me for many hours in the short time I've had it. There's plenty to explore with the random world generation, plenty to craft, plentry to build, and plenty to do with anything. Many people compare this game to Terraria, but it's not like Terraria unless you focus on a few key aspects. This game goes far beyond the repetition of Terraria where you do the same thing: mine, craft, kill, build. Extremely boring in my eyes, but no this game is more vast where you have quests that are worthwhile, planets that are worth exploration, and simply so much fun to do.
What's the biggest part about this game that I love? We didn't have to wait a long time for this game to be published with all the content. Now many people will question why this is a good thing but hear me out! What's the number one thing that stops people from playing a game? Running out of things to do. Now if a game is permenantly having things being added to it this would solve that problem now wouldn't it? There are many games that I adore then stopped play, which I'll take Fallout 3 which on my PlayStation I use to play every day and all day. It was an amazing game that I didn't stop playing for a long time, but in the end I had stopped. Why? I ran out of things to do. Even with mods a game will get boring in the end, but if something is constantly being improved then we'll never run into this problem.
Summary: Stop complaining about how this game will never be finished. If you want a game that will be finished quickly then go play Call of Duty where you can get a new one every year, then you should be happy. Starbound is an amazing game so just buy it and try it, it's a cheap game and if you don't like it there's always a refund.

This is a great point and click adventure game. The bulk of the story lies in the fleshed-out characters and how they interact both between each other and with the player. When the game says your choices matter -- they really do. And this is not one of these games that you can get yourself screwed because you chose poorly in the early game and didn't realise it. None of the choices particularly screw your situation as much as make it harder or easier, but doable. There are many quick time events during gameplay but they make sense in context and don't annoy you or take you out of the immersion of the cutscenes. I also really like the online feature to see how you did in relation to other players, it really puts things in perspective. Wish it had more detailed stats, but it's alright.
The puzzles are well constructed and make sense in their envoirnment. I managed to beat it without walkthroughs and I'm not a fan of puzzle games. There isn't a single puzzle that once you solve it you go "what? This makes no sense", although I did think of a different solution to a puzzle in early game that wasn't the right solution and I thought mine would be much more intuitive to players than the one presented. It's not a major disappointment for me but I think it's a small flaw in an otherwise really good game.
The graphics aren't really great, but for a 2012 game it still holds up. They're stylized in a way that make you not care much for them. And to be honest you won't be noticing them with such a thrilling story.
The controls I found a little wonky, but I always had this problem with Telltale games. My mouse gets in a weird state of drunkness, I think it takes the game a little time to register the movement and execute it, so it always feels like the mouse is lagging behind. Keyboard controls are okay. As I was playing I thought that maybe they were most likely made for controllers, and I was reminding myself to play with a controller once I got hold of one, but after talking with people that have experienced the game with it, maybe it feels much worse than with mouse and keyboard.
Is this game worth the price? Really, I don't think so. It's a 12-or-so-hour-long game, I don't think it's long enough, even though there is a lot of love, talent and dedication put into it. If you really want it, wait for a sale. I haven't played the DLC yet but I think the same advice would be applied.
Overall, I believe this is a game that everyone should play, even if you don't enjoy puzzle adventure games. The story alone is enough to get you hooked.

*  QUESTS:  Most are just a case of go here kill this, fetch that.
*  ROLE-PLAYING:  There isn't much.  They've taken away the fun karma system that Fallout 3 had.  There isn't really a good/bad path to follow - it's really just a matter of deciding which major faction you chose to follow.
*  MAIN STORY LINE:  I personally didn't find it terribly interesting or engaging and the particular ending that I chose kind of felt like "so that's it?".  Perhaps it would've been more interesting if they had clear cut good/bad npc's and factions  in the game.
*  NPC'S AND THEIR DIALOGUE:  Terrible.  Just terrible.  The speech options are limited compared to fallout 3 and the voices seem dreary as though it's just someone in the background waffling on about nothing.  They either put you to sleep or are just downright irritating.  I'm not sure if it's the volume, sound technology, voice acting or something else but the dialogue just seemed off somehow.  I don't recall having this issue with Fallout 3 and I certainly don't recal having it with the Witcher 3 either.
*  GRINDING:  I felt there was just too much stuff to collect.  It really was quite tedious for much of the game.   The whole walking around slowly while over-encumbered and then painstakingly sifting through dozens and dozens of items with traders wore thin fairly quickly.
* LOAD SCREENS:  Waiting 2 minutes every time you want to enter a building or fast travel?  No thanks.  Witcher 3 did it better.
_..._
Alright so I guess that's about it.  The only positives are that the combat, looting and perks are somewhat fun to deal with.  Other than that, it's a fairly bland, tedious and grindy experience.
By the way, I also played the dlc's - and while there's some decent loot - it's really not too different from the main game.
I can only hope that they address these issues for any future games in the series.

Northgard has beautiful graphics, and offers a refreshing take on the city-building genre. For the first time in a while I decided to buy this game out on a limb, and not research the game or watch any videos on it. I was pleasantly surprised for the first hour and a half. However, I played this game on normal difficulty and quickly reached the end game. I was dissapointed at how quickly I defeated the AI and the lack of freedom when it came to forging an army and expanding my clan. Like Civilization, there are tiles around the map, but there are very strict limits to how many structures you can build in each tile, which I found rather irritating. And after around 2 hours, I found that I had accomplished everything the game had to offer. So for this reason I requested a refund, as I found there to be little to no replayability.
, but if I were you I would wait for the game to drop to £10 or less, as I don't feel it is worth the £15 price-tag. But I am sure this game will be a lot better in the future as there are many features that are yet to be released, due to the fact that this game is in early access. So I would also recommend that you wait until the full release.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Like I said at the beginning, I think Northgard is a very good game, but in it's current stage, I personally don't feel that I can spend £15 on a game this short. And, like previously stated, I am aware that this is in early-access and more will be added to the game. Another point I failed to make was that with strategy games, I wouldn't dream of entering multiplayer. Even the thought of multiplayer slipped my mind when writing the original review. So taking that into thought now, I guess if you are a hardcore fan of strategy games, then this is probably the game for you.
My review was hastily written, and I actually wrote it because I was bored, not because I wanted to bash the game. I didn't expect anyone to even see it let alone upvote it. Not necessarily a knock on the game itself, I just came into it with the wrong expectations. This is very much an eroge visual novel about a ton of girls orbitting one oblivious dude's crotch, even if it does eventually involve giant robots and aliens and other sci-fi stuff. And if the former is your thing, again, this is almost certainly for you. But if you're just curious about the one super hyped up mecha visual novel you'll probably want to save yourself the time and money. While the mecha aspect definitely sees a huge jump in quality once you get to Alternative, you're talking about over 20 hours minimum to get there (I used a walkthrough), and even then it takes it's sweet time getting to (no spoilers) the parts you've actually wanted to see since halfway through the previous game, and would only stand up to average/slightly above average mecha anime or manga.

Some people is left handed and drive/walk/move using arrow keys. Now with this game it is impossible to map movement to arrow keys. According to the official forums this is not a bug. But a feature.
For some left handed people this works as a showstopper. The worst kind of bugs. Making it impossible to play the game. so it is realy a terrible game design.
The Reason I call it a terrible game design is it would be a simple matter to allow rebinding of all functions to all keys. There is likly extra code in the game to prevent rebinding of some keys.
So yes it is probably not a BUG but a bad design choice.
One cold argue about if this is a bug or not, introduced at design time. But that discussion is perhaps more of a academic nature and largely irrelevant. The consequence is still that it is a showstupper for some players.
There exist a workaround - AutoHotkey.
But it should not be needed to use tools like that to fix a REALY BAD game design.
Also it is not everyone that can figure out to use such a workaround, should they need it.
Beside that the game is quite fun to play, But still I will not recommend it, Because of that terrible game design.

Would not recommend to those who are not a fan of the genre. Muv-Luv is a romantic comedy. Don't start it just because you heard Unlimited and Alternative get more intense. The journey should be enjoyed in its entirety, including the tropey Japanese highschool romance parts, otherwise your enjoyment of the work as a whole will suffer.
That being said, I thoroughly enjoyed every minute of this light-hearted, but emotional journey. The art style was off-putting for me at first, but I grew to love it really quickly. This VN is solid all around. It has a good sense of humor and every character in the cast is well-developed and extremely lovable.
Pros:
+Catchy soundtrack
+Solid voice acting
+Great sense of humor
+Excellent light-hearted story that still has plenty of feels
+First half of story (Extra) has a lot of unique, well-developed branches
+Top-tier waifus
+Expressive ahoge
Cons:
-Art style takes some getting used to
-The genre isn't for everyone
-Second half (Unlimited) suffers from copy-paste story branches
-Second half arguably struggles to establish an appropriate tone
Overall, solid 9/10.
Strongly recommend to fans of the genre or anyone looking for a light-hearted story with just the right amount of feels to get you invested without leaving a hole in your soul when you finish.

Many people will try and persuade you not to buy Starbound, them complaining that the developers are never going to finish the game because of whatever reason. What don't they realize? Games take a long time to develop! It was a bad move surely for the developers to have published the game on Steam so early on, but this was because they needed funding.
The developers aren't some large company that can pitch out a game every year to make mad money, I'm looking at you Assassin's Creed and Call of Duty, no but instead a smaller company that doesn't have all the resources to pump out a large game in record time. Starbound is honestly a great game and it's a fun game to play, mainly with a group of friends, that has entertained me for many hours in the short time I've had it. There's plenty to explore with the random world generation, plenty to craft, plentry to build, and plenty to do with anything. Many people compare this game to Terraria, but it's not like Terraria unless you focus on a few key aspects. This game goes far beyond the repetition of Terraria where you do the same thing: mine, craft, kill, build. Extremely boring in my eyes, but no this game is more vast where you have quests that are worthwhile, planets that are worth exploration, and simply so much fun to do.
What's the biggest part about this game that I love? We didn't have to wait a long time for this game to be published with all the content. Now many people will question why this is a good thing but hear me out! What's the number one thing that stops people from playing a game? Running out of things to do. Now if a game is permenantly having things being added to it this would solve that problem now wouldn't it? There are many games that I adore then stopped play, which I'll take Fallout 3 which on my PlayStation I use to play every day and all day. It was an amazing game that I didn't stop playing for a long time, but in the end I had stopped. Why? I ran out of things to do. Even with mods a game will get boring in the end, but if something is constantly being improved then we'll never run into this problem.
Summary: Stop complaining about how this game will never be finished. If you want a game that will be finished quickly then go play Call of Duty where you can get a new one every year, then you should be happy. Starbound is an amazing game so just buy it and try it, it's a cheap game and if you don't like it there's always a refund.

It's an excellent game in development, but there's a but or two.
First of all, this is a free game playable on a web browser. Sadly, I realised that AFTER purchasing it. That's very unfair, that to easily play with your friends, you'd have to pay for the game.
Second of all, a role or two *cough*mayor*cough* is incredibly broken and unfair. It immediately confirms one person as a townie and any following leads and so on go through the mayor only. This reduces the game to only Investigative roles figuring who's who, to Jailor and Bodyguard protecting mayor, to Mayor guessing who's lying and to everyone else? Just standing there, doing nothing. If you're not an investigative role, never mind that, if you're not a town role, you have almost no say as to what happens and who gets lynched, you have no clue why anyone gets lynched, and all you're doing is hoping the Mayor is smart enough not to screw up, while you wait for them to say "Guilty or Innocent".
Meanwhile, Mafia and evil roles are reduced to guessing who is who randomly, rather than going by the leads the townies give out. This makes the game an absolute guesswork, and is all about finding the Jailor, Bodyguard and Investigative roles through pure luck. Town of Salem, the whole design and concept of it, is not that sort of game.
Now, so that this isn't just a mayor rant, the good things.
It's an incredibly addictive brain stimulator. If you're a manipulative person, if you're a lie detector, if you can apply logic and put 2 and 2 together easily, this game is for you. It's all about achieving your goals while deceiving your opponents, while convincing your team mates that you are, in fact, a team mate, it's about revealing leads as to who's who without revealing who you are or how you know that. I mean, assuming there isn't a mayor, of course *grumblegrumble* #NoMayorGames *grumble grumble*
The amount of fun you can have playing different roles, figuring out what's going on, and so forth, it's crazy. The dynamic between the different and numerous roles is amazing, and if you play Ranked Practice and/or Ranked games, you will really be in for a treat, as there is only one confirmed role, and everything else is just a random selection of categories.
While I'm on the topic, you should not judge the game by the "Classic" games. It's a great start point, to figure out how roles work with each other, how to trick people and so forth, but it's not all it is. I suggest keeping the wiki open until you learn what each role does, how they are detected by others, and what categories can be what roles. This will help loads.
Overall, I suggest you try this game (Remember, it's a free game on web browser), but be prepared to lose track of time, each game lasts around 30 minutes (on ranked/ranked practice) and it's very easy to go "Just one more game". There have been rumours that certain roles will be rebalanced as well, so that should help with the Mayor problem.

This game holds a special place in my heart as it was one of the first fps games I ever played back when it came in a box with Armoured Fist 3. I played it to the point that even now, I can regurgitate most of the dialogue from the first mission in a heartbeat.
Graphics wise, it's not very impressive. This also has the added effect of making it harder to see enemies, especially from a distance, which can be a good thing and a bad thing, as it would make you more alert to the movement of pixels on your screen, but also means you'll get shot from somewhere you had thought previously empty. Constant Vigilance, ehe.
Gameplay is fun. You can run and gun if you want to, but it's much more effective to take a position and fire from it, although the A.I will eventually home in on you. Unless you want to take the wimp route and alter your health in the options, you'll only be able to take two hits from any standard weapon the enemies have, so that would factor in to your alertness as well.
Perhaps it's nostalgiac factor is more appealing to me than it's actual content, but I still find myself playing it the odd time and enjoying it. Whether anyone else enjoys it, I don't know.
TL;DR: Old Graphics, Decent Gameplay, Smart A.I, Nostalgiac.

Delta Force, the legendary open world tactical shooter series that pushed "Voxel Space" voxel tech in a time where large open spaces with bumpy terrain were not a common thing. Nothing bad about the game, but unfortunately I can't recommend this version here because of big issues running it on a modern system. I know Windows 10 is not listed under supported OSes, but still, being able to run this only in a window, then for some time not at all, eventually seemingly fixed things by enabling "DirectPlay" option, yet no matter what I do I cannot access the single-player missions anymore.
As said, nothing bad about the game itself, but if you have a modern system, I do not recommend it.

This is a great idle game to add to any arsenal of idle games you may already play.
It is an idle game along the lines of AdVenture Capitalist, but has some complex metagame play when you delve deep. You are able to upgrade not only your own character, but whatever Champion you choose to play alongside you. The game works fine for people who either choose to go the idle-game route, or for those who wish to do active clicking, because champions specialize in one or the other. This is an awesome feature for diverse idle game players, and the abillity to swap champions on the fly means you can change your strategy whenever you want, and aren't forced to stick with one playstyle.
I really enjoyed Midas's currency system - the developer actually allows players to purchase in-game currency using free, earned currency (blue gems). Super uncommon in a lot of f2p games, and when it happens, it takes ages to get it. In this one, after three days, I had nearly $20 worth of in-game currency just by trading in my blue gems. I was able to trade these for significant profit boosts.
I feel the game is slowly becoming very fair and balanced after adjustments were made in the last few months. There has been an event going on for a while which is great for people who don't want to binge these idle games in a weekend (something that they totally were not made for, nor is the demographic for idle games likely people who want to focus on that game for an entire weekend).
For a free game, this game is good; however, it's propelled above and beyond thanks to a system that doesn't force casual players to buy currency if they don't want to, while still enjoying the benefits of that in-game currency if they rack up enough earned gems, this is paired with a game system that truly caters to an idle gamer demographic - one that doesn't force you to babysit it during "prime times" or events. This is one of my favorite idle games on Steam right now.

It should be noted that you can play this game online for free, but buying the game is a neat way to support the makers. That being said Town of Salem provides a unique experience each game (especially with the "all any" mode). Play L4D at your peril! This game is completely addictive – at least it is for me. Shooting zombies is just so much fun, especially when it’s made possible by such a well-crafted game. The premise is very simple: you and three fellow survivors have to make your way from one safe house to another until you are finally rescued. Along the way you have to fight off hordes of slavering zombies. In single player mode the AI is pretty good, although your teammates don’t always behave as you might wish them to during the incredibly hectic campaign finales. There are 4 campaigns with 5 maps to each one. Replay value is good due to the fact that the AI changes the zombie attacks and spawn points with each play, so you never know where the horde is going to come flooding from or where the bosses are lurking. When you get bored with the maps supplied there are loads of 3rd party maps and campaigns available on the web. On top of all this you can even play as one the various types of zombies (on a random basis). Personally I find this less satisfying, but it is worth a go just to get the other perspective. This is a simple but truly great game. L4D2 here I come!

So when going into this game do not expect SupCom, it will leave you dissapointed more than likely.
The game acts and feels like an updated TA.
Differences between TA and PA:
PA has better balance
TA has a second faction without mods
PA has a massive modding community which fixes some of the short comings of the game
PA has planets, not maps.
Pros:
-runs on my laptop running an i5-2550, even with other players in the game.
-System creation allows for some hilarious maps.
-AI isn't 100% garbage at low levels. They actually attack things and build higher tier stuff on easy.

-The game is basically online only, while you can play it offline it runs like a spoiled mule. While this doesn't affect most people, this affects me negatively since I tend to play games at places without wifi a lot like my job(it has wifi but they track steam on it, before you ask I work IT and I might get one or two calls a day that I actually have to leave my office for, most of the time they just turned off the computer.)

Street Fighter 5 is hard to recommend for anyone unfamiliar with fighting games or without others nearby to play with locally / enjoy online play. For those who do enjoy fighting games, SF5 is quite accessible, with relatively easy but impressive combos and non-complex character traits. And it is fundamentally a good and enjoyable game, nothing I say can detract from that.
However, there are issues plaguing both multiplayer and singleplayer. You can judge as to whether they're a deal-breaker - many will not affect players who just want to play friendly matches locally.
If you want to play online ranked, the fuzzy matchmaking will annoy, often pairing up bronze players with consecutive super golds as soon as they get a winning streak against other bronze players. Lag isn't uncommon, and can be extremely bad, turning the gameplay into sweep and shoryuken battles. There is also little character variety in lower ranks, making learning matchups against advanced characters difficult before you're thrown in the deep end.
If you want to play local multiplayer, the lack of support for Dinput can really hurt. Trying to use 2 fightsticks at once can require driver downloads, use of Xbox360 sticks rather than ones designed for PC, and use of a Joy2Key program. It can be frustrating to get some setups to work. Then there are the problems with dlc character unlocking, which I'll detail later.
If you want to play single player, this really isn't the game. I'd argue Guilty Gear Xrd and King of Fighters 13 are more worth getting, as well as Killer Instinct - SF5 is far too expensive for the little it provides. Survival mode is frustrating to say the least, there is no arcade mode, and all of the story modes give no challenge. There is currently no way to simulate a best-of-3 game against any AI.
(Rant ahead)
The worst thing about SF5 for me personally is the pricing. It's too expensive for what it is, and the new dlc characters and story don't really change that, especially as you'll have to pay for these characters with the season pass or lose a ton of fight money (FM).
The system for getting new characters, costumes, colours, and stages is simultaneously daunting and appalling for any completionist.
The problem is that you will never have enough FM, the ingame currency. You can get stacks of fight money for levelling up characters and completing single player modes, but these only pay out once. After that, the only way to get more is to win online ranked matches - at a paltry 50FM per win.
I would argue it's feasible to get almost 1 million FM through general online levelling and doing all modes and up to hard survival on all characters, but the dlc characters (currently 4, with 2 more coming soon) cost 100,000FM each.
Every single character (currently 20) has another costume which costs 40,000FM, and additional colours which altogether cost 47,000FM. Then there are 5 dlc stages, which cost 40,000 to 70,000FM each.
There's no way to unlock everything without spending forever on online ranked (and winning) or spending real money, and you'll need to endure survival mode thrice for every one of those new costumes to get their colours.
You could always get the season pass, for 'just' £25, and get a single stage, 6 characters, and 6 premium costumes, saving you a lot of FM. But Capcom advertised these dlc characters as being acheivable to get with FM, and if there are many more dlc characters that will simply not be the case without missing out on lots of stages.
Worst of all are the new premium costumes. You can't pay FM, you have to pay £3.20 (~5$?). Each costume. For one character. That's just terrible. USF4 had costume packs at ~£16 for a costume for each of the 40-odd characters, at 20 colours per costume, and these packs even go on sale sometimes. Not to mention all the free costumes you get with USF4. SF5 costumes only have 10 colours, and you'll need to unlock 8 of them yourself. The SF5 costumes are higher resolution and have cloth and hair physics, but you'd need to be a diehard fan of a character to consider getting one.
If you can ignore all the cosmetics and just buy the dlc characters, you should be fine on FM and have a commendable will, but I feel that aside from your skill level and online rank, the cosmetics are the only 'progress' you can make, the only unlocks, a show of the FM and character levels you've earned and the survival mode runs you've wasted your time on. It's also fun to have them to play with friends and let them see more variety in designs.
Overall I cannot morally condone supporting SF5 at this moment due to its pricing, especially after the introduction of premium costumes. It's certainly not supporting the players. It feels like you need to pay over 3 times the base game's already high price for everything. Modding costumes and cheating FM feels like the fair option; I cannot be pleased with this game while it has this lust for eventually breaking you down into spending money for something you already deserve, after putting up with the game.
SF5 wasn't F2P, last time I looked.

But I felt as though I was still waiting for something significant to happen by the time it ended. However, that's probably a bit harsh on my part considering I haven't explored all Extra has to offer.
Unlimited, on the other hand, was definitely where I got heavily invested. Perhaps it's because I'm a sucker for giant robots, but that's not the only reason. The writing, art style and characters all kicked it up a notch. Even Takeru, insufferable he might've been, grew into someone who's somewhat admirable. While no tears were shed by the end of the game, the impact to my feels was definitely felt with the force of a TSF wielding a giant sledgehammer.
So yeah, I can now thoroughly accept this is one of the most acclaimed VNs ever, and going through all of this has me just itching to play Alternative to see how it ends. If you consider yourself a fan of visual novels, pick this up and enjoy the ride. Just make sure to grab a box of tissues just in case.

I am a huge fan of strategy games. I still remember when my father brought Civilization on a floppy disk and how he presented me with a CD of Age of Empires and brought me CD with Heroes III when he came from a business trip. I remember the first time when I played with my brother against each other in Starcraft. I remember how I played Warcraft II at school during computer lessons. I perfectly remember my feelings when I played KKnD, Earth 2140 and Red Alert. I thank god that I discovered
in 2004. I reached Top-1000 in 1v1 Europe. I played all custom maps. So I was really happy when Starcraft II was released. I passed all campaigns on Brutal with all achievements. I am Diamond terrain in 1v1. So I can definitely say that my opinion about this game is valuable.
When Starcraft II was released the RTS genre wasn't so popular as it was 5-10 years ago. So after SCII release there are almost no high-quality RTS games. I was happy when I found Northgard in "Upcoming releases". I had no doubts when it came to buying this game yesterday.
I launched the game and started a single scenario. There is no tutorial in the game so I spent the first hour of playing trying to understand what exactly I should to do here. It seems funny but I understood how to build workers only after 20m of gameplay. Anyway, I like the process of cognition. I restarted the scenario about 5 times when I finally realized what I should do.
Northgard is an unusual RTS game. It contains some elements from Settlers, AoE and other popular strategy titles. I liked the resulting mix. There is no micromanagment like in Warcraft or Starcraft. The gameplay is relaxed and unhurried. You have a lot of time to make decisions. I think this feature will make the game popular among players.
You start with 3 peasants and you should develop your settlement by collecting food, gathering wood/stones/iron. The map is hidden so you should train scouts to make it visible. The playing field is divided into regions. Each one could contain some resources or special elements like crypts, altars and monster's den which are usually defended by a group of monsters.
So the main objective in the game is to expand your territory and rise to power to get enough resources to reach one of the victory conditions. There are some of them: destroy all other clans, collect 7k gold, learn all lores, get 1k authority etc.
As I said before I really like the gameplay despite the fact that there is little content. The development of base is interesting until you reveal all the buildings. There is only 1 upgrade for each building and 1 for each unit. There are only 2 enemies + boss unit. Random events are all the same. You lose food, buildings get damaged or monsters come through portals.
The combat system is poor and boring. There is only 2 types of warriors with no micromanagment. There is only 1 game tactic now. You make a stack of 3 warriors and send them attack. If there is a tower you should add a chieftain. You heal them after and recruit new warriors to maximum and send attack again. Repeat until you win... Boring...
When I completed single scenario after 3 hours of gaming against 3 AI on hard I realized that I didn’t want to play this game anymore. Why? Because the next session will be exactly the same as the previous one. There is no replayability yet by the reason of lack of content.
Upd. I have started a new session today and my thoughts were right. I closed the game after 30m playing.
The game is good and seems promising. It looks pretty. I liked the gameplay. I haven't seen any bugs except for 1 game crash :D. I am sure the game will turn into an awesome game in future. But for now, I think the price of 20$ is too high for 3-4 hours of gameplay. I will definitely change my opinion in the future when the campaign or multiplayer will be released and the game will become deeper.
I can't recommend Northgard in its current state.

If you enjoyed Airline Tycoon 1 (like me) you WILL be dissapointed by this game.
When I first played, my enthusiasm faded quite quickly. At first, I chalked it up to unfairly comparing this game to its predecessor so I gave it a chance.  After a few attempts and a few short sessions every couple weeks, culminating to approx 16 hours, I decided it's time to uninstall this piece of trash.
Now that the personal anecdote is out of the way, here is where I think this game fails.
I'm sure most people got turned off by the fact that you have to move around the airport to do things like in a point-and-click adventure game, instead of just looking at spreadsheets from like other "tycoon" games. The first game did that too, but in that one, the airport was a 2D enviornment and everything was easy to find, and it was easy to get to places quickly. Here, however, you move really slow in a full 3D enviornment that makes your video card chug away for no real reason.
Which brings me to my next point, the graphics. Don't get me wrong, I know graphics don't make the game and I am not criticizing about the choice of style. I'm talking about the unessisary details in this game. When all you are really doing is scheduling flights for your planes do you really care about the ammount of bloom in the main terminal? You would if it's causing your middle-end hardware to lag.
The thing this game has going for it (what the other game lacks) is custom designs of the plane's interiors, livery colors, decals. Unfortuantly all those areas are limited, you only have a few color choices, and half of them are the established color schemes of the featured (uncustomizable) airlines. Instead of buying real world planes like the Airbus A320 or the Boeing 737, you instead have to build planes from scratch from a limited set of parts. Another feature this game has is that you can view your plane in flight. All these things are pointless, unless you entertained by the sight of your butt-ugly plane in it's butt-ugly $-sign decals bob up and down in front of a sky backdrop.
Newcomers to the series hate it for its limiting and unconvential style and fans of the first game hate it for dumbing it down. Spend your $20 elsewhere.
EDIT: Airline Tycoon Deluxe is now available on Steam, I recomend you check that out.

This game. This game is so good. It expands on many of the features of the first game and feels more like an actual game, rather than a bunch of maps to select from. In order to unlock new towers, you need to level up by playing through the maps and gaining exp from killing sh*t, which is a great featureso you feel as though you are getting stronger along with your foes (but it's done in a way that you can still get the crap beaten out of your core and lose, despite your shiny new towers), and the devs even added in a perk feature, which I didn't feel was needed until I used it and fell in love with it. You can unlock more perk slots and equip up to 4 at the beginning of each map, and holy crap they're awesome. The perks range from increasing the damage inflicted on enemy weakspots (I always equip that one), to having the core regain 10% of it's max health after each round, to you shooting lightning out of your body or jumping on an enemy and inflicting 2000 damage (Plumber Shoes ftw) or even increasing the amount of damage you inflict by 15% for every enemy near you. These perks are an amazing addition, and are super fun and add a bunch of variety to each game you play (especially on co-op, with each player equipping different perks).
Now if you read that and are thinking, "Hmmm.... Sounds like I'm going to be overpowered.... Especially on co-op," and you couldn't be more WRONG. The game is really tough, as the towers now do less damage than in the first game and you have to play a larger role in combatting the hordes of mobs you will find in this game. One moment you're on top of the world, your maze is obliterating everything, and the next you have a giant Super Heavy blowing up your towers (and yes, certain boss enemies can destroy your towers, but they can be repaired for free after the round) and a huge swarm of walker pups are attacking your core. Something about the constant switch from success to failure makes the game really addicting, and can you keep playing when you could've rage quit earlier, simply because THIS turret layout is going to work, forget the four you built before. This is the one, and thats what keeps you going.
I haven't completed the game's campaign, or come anywhere near unlocking all the perks (I'm only level 12 out of 50 I think), mainly cuz I only play this game for hour bursts when I want to blow off steam after work or whatever (sometimes i binge and play for longer; 6 hours straight was the longest I could go before getting off and that was so I could go to work), and that's exactly what this game is made for. The original was good, but a lot of the maps were too long requiring you to beat 20 or 25 long waves of enemies before completing the map. In this game there are 8 (with all the DLC) regions, each one with about 4 or 5 maps inside of it (which is a lot of content), and each map contains about 10-15 waves which is a lot easier to get through than 20 or 25 in the original. Because of this the maps change often enough to stay interesting and visually appealing (they're all beautifully designed and full of little secrets like playable arcade games), and the graphics are really breath taking as the environments go from clean cities, to rusted out junkyards and train stations, to beautiful, alien forests (and more areas I haven't seen before) which are completely gorgeous on the Unreal engine this game uses.
As you've noticed earlier, I've been comparing this game to the original which I'm assuming you've already played. If not buy both of them and play them now (there's no story in the first game, so if you can only afford one, buy this one). If you were a fan of the original but read negative reviews saying the game is watered down and dumber, that is 100% untrue. Out of the entire game I can find only 1 issue, which is when you upgrade the cannon tower that tower does less than DPS than if you just bought another cannon and put it by the first one. Other than that though, the game is improved in every way. Graphically, the first game was really nice for an indy game with burnt out cities and gorgeous jungles, but this game takes the cake. Gameplay-wise, this game is far superior. It feels like a spectacular molding of excellant FPS gameplay mixed with tower defense and not TD with FPS thrown in as a novelty or vice versa. Story, the second one actually has a story now, told through little entertaining comic strips that are shown as each map loads. I haven't gotten far in the story at all, but so far so good. It's not the focus of the game, but it's nice to see all the playable characters interacting and learn some backstory on the Lumes (the enemies you'll face) and Elysion One. Music: As an owner of the Sanctum 1 soundtrack, I have to admit the first game has better music, but the music in 2 is still very strong and very good. However it is one of those soundtracks you dont notice, which a lot of people consider to be the best type, so it's good.
Overall, I recommend this game to anyone with a PC and a love for gaming. It's that good. It requires the fast reflexes and thinking of a well-made shooter (not COD), but also the calculating logic of a TD, and the creativity of building games. I may not be the most qualified to write this review, as I stated before, I'm not far in the game, but there is just so much content and so far it is all so good I can't help but write this review now, so others will dive into the world of Elysion One and kick more Lume a$$. I'll probably edit this review (if i can) when I complete this game, but as of now I am currently having a love affair with this game.

It's an excellent game in development, but there's a but or two.
First of all, this is a free game playable on a web browser. Sadly, I realised that AFTER purchasing it. That's very unfair, that to easily play with your friends, you'd have to pay for the game.
Second of all, a role or two *cough*mayor*cough* is incredibly broken and unfair. It immediately confirms one person as a townie and any following leads and so on go through the mayor only. This reduces the game to only Investigative roles figuring who's who, to Jailor and Bodyguard protecting mayor, to Mayor guessing who's lying and to everyone else? Just standing there, doing nothing. If you're not an investigative role, never mind that, if you're not a town role, you have almost no say as to what happens and who gets lynched, you have no clue why anyone gets lynched, and all you're doing is hoping the Mayor is smart enough not to screw up, while you wait for them to say "Guilty or Innocent".
Meanwhile, Mafia and evil roles are reduced to guessing who is who randomly, rather than going by the leads the townies give out. This makes the game an absolute guesswork, and is all about finding the Jailor, Bodyguard and Investigative roles through pure luck. Town of Salem, the whole design and concept of it, is not that sort of game.
Now, so that this isn't just a mayor rant, the good things.
It's an incredibly addictive brain stimulator. If you're a manipulative person, if you're a lie detector, if you can apply logic and put 2 and 2 together easily, this game is for you. It's all about achieving your goals while deceiving your opponents, while convincing your team mates that you are, in fact, a team mate, it's about revealing leads as to who's who without revealing who you are or how you know that. I mean, assuming there isn't a mayor, of course *grumblegrumble* #NoMayorGames *grumble grumble*
The amount of fun you can have playing different roles, figuring out what's going on, and so forth, it's crazy. The dynamic between the different and numerous roles is amazing, and if you play Ranked Practice and/or Ranked games, you will really be in for a treat, as there is only one confirmed role, and everything else is just a random selection of categories.
While I'm on the topic, you should not judge the game by the "Classic" games. It's a great start point, to figure out how roles work with each other, how to trick people and so forth, but it's not all it is. I suggest keeping the wiki open until you learn what each role does, how they are detected by others, and what categories can be what roles. This will help loads.
Overall, I suggest you try this game (Remember, it's a free game on web browser), but be prepared to lose track of time, each game lasts around 30 minutes (on ranked/ranked practice) and it's very easy to go "Just one more game". There have been rumours that certain roles will be rebalanced as well, so that should help with the Mayor problem.

It should be noted that you can play this game online for free, but buying the game is a neat way to support the makers. That being said Town of Salem provides a unique experience each game (especially with the "all any" mode). The game itself is based off a real-life game you may have played as a child called "Mafia" and other similar ones. There are three groups roles can be catagorized under which is the basis for the gameplay. As a town member you have to remember many things, find out who to trust, and hang those you know you can't before it's too late. As mafia however the game is deception and boy is that fun too. The third, "independent" sort of faction, called Neutrals. They can range from the Serial Killer, a murderer who must kill all town and mafia, to the Jester, a role who wants to be lynched, not killed, and upon being lynched will be able to kill one person at night. All of these unique roles when combined create a truly tense game where word cannot be held sacred and people can never be trusted.

I've been playing this game for nearly 5 years now, with 80 days under my belt. I believe it is time for me to write a review.  After 5 years of playing this game, I have yet to get bored of it.
This is my opinion is a game with great potential. The game is simple, and attractive, but yet people will disregard and never attempt to play it due to it's 8 bit nature, as sad as it is. I personally love the simplicity of the graphics, it... Makes for a beautiful creation.
This game has a wonderful learning curve, you die and lose everything, but with each new character and each death, you'll be learning something new. With each death, you learn how to avoid a new one, and thus dying is a... Healthy part of the game, people will die on beloved characters, and on occasion quit to this, but almost always find a way to come back to this beautiful game.
This game was designed with a co-op aspect to it, but with the addition to pets, this was completely disregarded, and thus I propose Deca revitalize the old co-op aspect of this game and make some real ENDGAME content that will truly require a good group of skilled players, with communication to take down. This will help make the game more enjoyable for the players who have put the time in to master the easier parts of the game.
I have yet to be brought into the hype train of DECA, and hope in time they will be able to satisfy me. I hope they listen to the community unlike kabam and listen to all of our amazing ideas, which lie barren due to Kabam's era. There were many genius ideas for dungeons and classes, as well as quality of life improvements which could greatly help to re-vitalize the game. Although you asked for suggestions for ideas to give to this game, I truly cannot, as you already have a wonderful community at your hands giving out quality suggestions. When some time has passed and ideas are being implented, I can then contribute some of the many ideas that could easily improve the quality of life for this game and the overall enjoyment, which I have widely debated about with friends to make for excellent content.
All in all. This game is easily enjoyable and doesn't require a beefy computer, all it takes is a few hours, and you can easily get hooked. I would personally recommend this game. With some love from Deca I expect to see old players and new players coming in, rather than going out. Best of luck to you DECA.
On a final note, I do believe that the vault challenge is not as rewarding as it should be... A single vault?
along with this vault, we should also receive the mystery gift ontop of this, and yet, that probably still wont be enough to justify this event, although simple, this is more beneficial to you than anything, and this we deserve a better reward than such. And the free vault for a person who logged on during a single given day? That should have been two days, to account for timezones. I ended up sleeping til 5 PM that day, although playing til, let's just say a rather late, or rather early hour of the day. Not even sure if I qualified to enter for this raffle. Carrying on with this point, I am rather upset with these "social events" , not going to lie. At least with the vault challenge, everyone has a chance to win. I do agree that more thought could have gone into the events as well, when I first logged on to see that the "free gift" was 500 fame at first, I was rather upset, as fame is not something most people have due to pets. Honestly I also believe that the lucky box could have gotten away with being more rewarding with less attempts, as to not benefit the fame trainers, possibly make the box have a few attempts free of charge, and either you score or you dont. I'm going to end this review here, as it is going nowhere now.
Hopefully DECA can improve over time and add stuff that can impress me and give the community a solid image of them. So far they have done well with attempting to remove spam bots and staying on top of duping, but this MotMG has been a let down for me, but I wont let that get me down just yet.
I wish the best of luck to you, DECA games. Sorry for this not being a quality review, I may make an actual review over the course of time and have it be a quality review.

Fallout 4, while not completely bad, is a huge letdown from Fallout 3.
I'm going to go into detail of what's wrong with it:
*  GRAPHICS:  Looks slightly cartoonish and plasticy which significantly reduces realism and immersion.  Also the facial animations and lip-syncing are a joke in comparison to the Witcher 3.
*  QUESTS:  Most are just a case of go here kill this, fetch that.
*  ROLE-PLAYING:  There isn't much.  They've taken away the fun karma system that Fallout 3 had.  There isn't really a good/bad path to follow - it's really just a matter of deciding which major faction you chose to follow.
*  MAIN STORY LINE:  I personally didn't find it terribly interesting or engaging and the particular ending that I chose kind of felt like "so that's it?".  Perhaps it would've been more interesting if they had clear cut good/bad npc's and factions  in the game.
*  NPC'S AND THEIR DIALOGUE:  Terrible.  Just terrible.  The speech options are limited compared to fallout 3 and the voices seem dreary as though it's just someone in the background waffling on about nothing.  They either put you to sleep or are just downright irritating.  I'm not sure if it's the volume, sound technology, voice acting or something else but the dialogue just seemed off somehow.  I don't recall having this issue with Fallout 3 and I certainly don't recal having it with the Witcher 3 either.
*  GRINDING:  I felt there was just too much stuff to collect.  It really was quite tedious for much of the game.   The whole walking around slowly while over-encumbered and then painstakingly sifting through dozens and dozens of items with traders wore thin fairly quickly.
* LOAD SCREENS:  Waiting 2 minutes every time you want to enter a building or fast travel?  No thanks.  Witcher 3 did it better.
_..._
Alright so I guess that's about it.  The only positives are that the combat, looting and perks are somewhat fun to deal with.  Other than that, it's a fairly bland, tedious and grindy experience.
By the way, I also played the dlc's - and while there's some decent loot - it's really not too different from the main game.
I can only hope that they address these issues for any future games in the series.

I will give this warning to people reading this review. Only RTS fans will really understand and enjoy this type of game. Also if you are the type of person who really enjoys a story in their game then go elsewhere, there's basically no story in this game whatsoever.
Essentially what Planetary Annihilation: TITANS is is it's an RTS game where giant sentient robots reawaken and fight each other to death because that's all they know to do. The difference between this game and other RTS like Supreme Commander is unlike those games, PA doesn't have a unit cap, so you can very well spam 1000+ suicide bots to blow up the enemy base. The only problem I've noticed with this is that really high numbers of units tend to lag the game.
Another thing this game does differently is it offers 4 theaters of war: land, sea, air, and space. Because of this you can develop multiple strategies and avenues of attacks against your enemy. If they have a bunch of anti-air defense, then spam land or sea units. If they have a bunch of land defense, then spam air and orbital units. Or you can go the Zerg Rush route and just build 100+ of any unit and completely overwhelm the enemy.
But what if you encounter an enemy that's incredibly entrenched, and even Zerg rushing them won't work? That's when we get into Planetary Annihilation. In the game, we have 2 (3 with TITANS) ways of achieving this. The first way to do this is to find some moon or other small planet, build several giant engines on it, and
The second way to destroy a planet is to first establish a base on a Metal Planet (you can tell what they are by, well, them looking like a giant Death Star). Then, you have to build five Structures called Catalysts on specified areas of the planet. Once you do that, you then have a fully functioning Death Star and can use it's death-laser to annihilate planets at your will. With TITANS, the third way to do it is to build the Titan called the Ragnarok. It's basically a giant drill that drills into the planet's core and detonates a nuke at the center, blowing it up. A word of advice though,
Now that I've covered the major positive points of the game, here are some of the problems with it people (including me) have.
For one, the AI is pretty much dumb as rocks. The game encourages you to build massive armies to attack the enemy with, but all the AI does is pretty much build a 5 man squad of various units and sends them to attack every 10 minutes. It scales up with difficulty though, plus there's user mods that add in better AI as well.
Second, the story in this game is pretty much non-existant. The only hint we really ever get are the 4 various factions in the game, which really only determines your color, it doesn't effect gameplay at all like in Supreme Commander. This can irk some people who really like games with a engrossing story in them. However I feel the base game is varied enough that I can still enjoy it even without much of a story.
Another thing I'd like to add on a more meta level is this game apparently came out earlier and had a lot less stuff than it did in TITANS, which irked some people off who bought the first game. I can understand that but I do have a solution for people who don't own any version yet: just buy this version. Also, I'd recommend getting it on sale. I mean I like RTS games but $40 is ridiculous for a game with no story whatsoever. I got this on sale for $6.
So in conclusion, I believe this game can still be pretty entertaining even without a story in it.

I got this game on sale for $6 and its the best $6 I have ever spent, This game is basically SupCom on Steroids. But to be fair not graphics-wise, although the planets and terrain look good the units themselves are alright. Sort of in a cartoonish way but not so that you feel like your playing minecraft. But the diversity of units? super weapons? planet to planet travelling? 3D fighting around the planets(With Day/Night cycles for added effect - These Planets Orbit Suns You Know!) and a whole host of different planets (Arctic, Barren, Tropical, Lava/Rocky, Deathstar(yes deathstar planets) Moons, Oceanic.. e.c.t... ?? Well what do you get? An adrenaline pumped RTS that will keep you on your toes as you try to micro-manage whole planets against foe(s). And yes there are cons as with every game, It lacks a story/campaign, Galactic War is basically a back to back Skirmish Mode - but you get *Tech* upgrades per skirmish to unlock more stuff to keep it interesting - And its always a 1v1/1v2/1v3... ect, so that gets stale.. but none the less this game is all sorts of fun, Vehicles/Bots/Ait/Naval/Orbital/Titan units ! and some of those have basic and then advanced units - Tech upgrading is good too, In a normal game(Not Galactic War) You tech up by building, So you start off with your Commander, he builds a factory(Land/Bot/Air) and can build Land/Bot/Air builders(Yes air builders! very good and fast!) and then they build advanced factories - to produce advanced builders, and then they build the best buildings. so all in all teching is actually relatively good, because building those buildings takes alot of energy and metal so you need a good economy to effectively build them(if you just tried to do it at the start you would just slow yourself down way too much) so it works out in a nice way but like I said you have to be on your toes and micro manage the hell out of everything, 10/10 would buy it

I know this is only a 26 minute review, but hear me out...please. I get not everyone may run into these issues...but I am, constantly, so this is my personal review.
The game is super simplistic, in a phone app kinda way. It plays at your desktop resolution and has ZERO UI upscaling or tinkering....so, 1080 is fine, but I'm at 4K...so the UI is microscopic. It's also basically unplayable at this point (which is why I only have 26 minutes played). The mouse will NOT allow you to place buildings (yes in green zones and yes, I have the required resources) 90% of the time...even if you click 40 bazillion times...anywhere in your village zone. You have to keep clicking Build and selecting the building you want over and over around 7 times before it will let you place the building. It acted like my mouse was out of range or the batteries were dying...but then i remembered it's a new mouse, and therefor...new batteries...and I sit right next to my tower. You can't drag select any units because the drag select box is limited/locked to the size of a nickle (limited on purpose or glitched, IDK). The buildings are just placeholders and really serve no purpose( call me old school, but I like every building to do something or produce it's own unit/tech....like C&C). You just build them and the constantly open unit box (no way to close...seriously)in the bottom right corner lights up new things to produce as you build things....when you can, because it's nigh impossible to place buildings to unlock units. I really wanted to like this game...but damn, it's broken as crap and about as simplistic as a mobile app. Also, the story mode isn't even available....just skirmish. I get it's in early access...but I can't review it properly if it is unplayable. The first enemy showed up and decimated half my stuff because i could't produce warriors.....because i could't build the damn training hut. In its current state, the game should not have been released in such an unplayable state.

Muv-Luv, what i can say that everybody already said? I would like to make a little background of myself just for people understand where i come from, i watch a lot of animes, read literally hungred mangas as well as read some LN, of course read some VN, but Muv-Luv tought me the feeling of being devasteded, bear in mind that i didnt play Alternative yet, i just finished Unlimited and came rushing to write this review, so yeah, lets begin.
Muv-Luv Extra i'll be clear, its mediocre, not because it is different from Unlimited and Alternative, but the characters and writting are weird, you see, they diverge a lot, sometimes it looks like the writer knows that he is writting to a VN, other times it looks like he is writting a novel, and what is the problem? Inconsistency with the character, there are sometimes in some routes that the main character starts to think like a romantic novel, using methaphor for what he is doing, really cheesy lines, when the character is more immature and sarcastic, but that is not the only problem, there are a lot of inconsistency with the story, as well as the motivation of some characters, they're not compeling enough. You see, it is not that bad, it is just ok harem shoujo VN, if you read VN or even watch animes offen, you'll know the background of at least one character just 15 minutes in to the game, and it isnt that good but i digress, you have your share of laughts and thats it, if it wasnt for contextualize a little of Unlimited i have to be honest, i would just recommend if you didnt have something to read.
Now lets go to the meat and potatos of Muv-Luv, Unlimited, my God, it didnt even look like the same game, the main character it is way more flesh out as well as the other characters, but the thing about the main character that makes him compeling is the difference between his perspective to the character in Unlimited, he seems immature, and using this adjetive to him, could be a shot in the foot, but it was really well written because the character is self-conscious, and that makes him relatable and not annoying, he can understand something, yet not accepting, not just that, you know something has a good writting when the character is something in the beginning, and at the end he is another. Talking about the story, it is more well paced, but when they need you to feel something, it is so effective, it is a great work of writting and music, makes ou anxious, or feel bad for it, you feel like Takeru in every moment, there wasnt a single moment that i didnt care, and i give props to that. Everytime i was sad reading, because some lines made me think about that world and how sad it was, i'll not get in to the specifics, even if you can read in the resume, but the more you think about that world and what they're going through, it is just sad, even if they are used to it and they are ok with it, just the setting it is so well placed that makes me, again, sad. And i think one of the most compeling aspect of Unlimited is the mistery, you dont know whats going on, whats this or that, and this is always in the back of your mind, this makes you want to read more and more to find out. I have to said, when i was at the final act and i realize what was going to happenning, i got depressed, i got sad, i felt the feels, because i was so invested in every character, the major ones, the small ones, everyone i cared a little at least, and see things going at that direction and let me spare some of your time to just say, the final act was the bread and butter of written in Unlimited, every word was carefully placed, because almost every single line it was a punch in the guts that i got, i'm used to it but i have to say, it was something special, and then, when you think you are depressed enough, seeing the credits, and then there is a after credits scene, you know that they put that there to kick you while you are still in the ground, it is impactful, and if you have a normal heart, my friend, if you didnt cried until then, you're going to shed a tear.

Burnout Paradise is a blast. I have no idea how long it had been collecting dust on my Steam shelf but I sincerely regret not giving it a go sooner.
As a Burnout game, I think the expectation is for vehicle destruction to be the highlight of the experience. I was personally more impressed with the unbelievable sense of speed that this game accomplishes. Typically when I see the absolutely maddening speed found in the first 10 minutes of Paradise, it comes with one of two tradeoffs. Either a) the vehicle movement is actually so fast that you literally are incapable of reacting in time to obstacles or b) the handling becomes so weak by the time you reach top speed that you have to either slow down or crash. Burnout Paradise makes you feel like you’re going 300 miles an hour at all times but never - not even for a moment - out of control. I don’t have any game design experience so I don’t know the tricks for how they achieved this, but let me tell you it’s the most fun I’ve had in an arcade racing game. Ever.
If I had a complaint it would be the “late game” content. Honestly, the issue I’m about to describe should really be a big deal, but I had SO much fun with the hours of wacky racing that I just don’t care. The game is not difficult, from my first time launching the game until I stopped playing I was steadily and relatively effortlessly progressing. I collected lots of cars, got the upgraded versions of all of them, drove like a mad-man through alleys and twisting hills, wrecked more rivals than I can count, and loved every minute of it. Then I hit a wall. It wasn’t the kind of wall that makes you think “Oh wow, the AI finally caught up and I need to start trying”. No, this was the wall where I could have a FLAWLESS race but literally never see the person in first. I had some theories that I missed something or need a different car, but at this point I had gotten something like 10 hours of awesome racing and I was satisfied.
So yes, I think there may be an issue with late game content (or else I just missed something) but it really didn’t matter because I got more than I ever expected out of Burnout Paradise and I would recommend it to any of my friends.

Sold as a simulation but has practically zero depth and you can easily go around the whole game in a few hours. There are only 4 airlines to choose from, which are rigid and uncustumizable. The aircraft customization options themselves are laughable; only 8 aircraft to choose from regardless of any realism (the concorde becomes a short haul, high passenger, profitable aircraft) with very limited options. The indoor cabin design is a joke: the developers wouldn't bother to make the different indoor environment for the different aircraft, so the inside of your jumbo jet is the same as that of your small propeller airliner. Furthermore you just choose preset items for the whole aircraft and can't for example have multiple class aircraft, but this doesnt change anything anyway since the price for all tickets is always the same.
Also personel management is ridiculous: you hire people with the skills they come with and you can't train them further, so your only way to improve your staff is to fire them and get new ones. You can only assign one set of staff to an aircraft, so basically it's the same pilot flying that airplane 24/7 for a whole month. Call the worker's syndicate!!! For those of you who are politically minded it's also nice to notice here that the game is stereotipically sexist: all pilots are males and all flight attendants female.
The main part of the game and where you will spend the most time with is the scheduling; it looks intricate at first, but after a few hours you find out it totally lacks any realism. The amount of passengers only depends on the demand and you can program your flights at basically any time of the day, hello 2AM departures! Basically your sucess at the game just depends on cramming the biggest number of route and charter flights in the schedule rather than making regular flights (the flight numbering system is automated and wonky).
The user interface is atrocious in the whole game, you have to physically walk to different offices, with loading screens, to get going. While the idea is commendable, it will soon become a chore and you will soon give up booking charter flights just because they require constant walking outside your office (loading screen), to the elevator (loading screen) to the charter office so you can grab a few contracts, and then the same annoying way back so you can schedule them.
The options are so limited and not user friendly at all, the tooltips are inconsistent and unclear over the board. The scheduling board is extremely poorly designed. It's hard to place the flights with precision, the "repeat schedule" option, which is meant to allow you to hold regular flight is the most user unfriendly ever and simply doesn't work. Any flights that take off before midnight and land after midnight will break this feature. Also you are forced to do some makeshift workarounds, like setting the schedule you want to repeat for tomorrow, then waiting a whole day before deciding to repeat it, because the game doesnt let you modify today's schedule, but it only allow you to copy today's schedule, not another days... so user unfriendly it's a crime. And did I mention the annoying "clear flight schedule" button located next to other buttons, which will wipe all the work you did without a confirmation screen?
The game itself is also full of bugs. The schedule locks itself frequently for no reason, the text doesn't match your actual objective, you get teleported back to your office when looking at a competitor's aircraft, the tutorials (which are themselves rather useless) get stuck while in progress, so you have to repeat the same actions twice.
The game does have a cute little design feel to it with some pretty cool airplane models (the airbus 380 with full ringed wings and 8 engines for example, or the cute curvy concorde), but this doesn't save it from the abysmal depth, or lack of depth, that it sinks into. Most people play simulation games because they enjoy some variety and custom options. In this game:
* You cannot rename anything (airlines, aircraft, staff)
* There is only 1 airport interior, all airports in the world are the same
* There is only 1 aircraft interior
* None of your choices has any real effect on the game anyway.
* Regardless of which mission you are in, or sandbox mode, you start each day at 9AM with a speech from the airport director, the speech is always the same and he repeats it 3 times as well for each of your competitor airlines.
Playing this feels about as fun as groundhog day happening to you...

TL;DR version: This game is frickin' beautiful. Go ahead and play it, if not for the sheer beauty alone.
In-Depth version: This game is frickin' beautiful. It's graphics are unbelievably stunning for such an Indie game. Every scene is beautifully crafted to be asthetically pleasing, but not distracting or too in-your-face.
Although, good graphics don't make a good game. But Sanctum 2 doesn't have to worry too much about anything else. The gameplay is smooth and fast, going from building/upgrading towers to fighting the vicious Lumes and defending the core.
There's something strangely satisfying about seeing a giant alien get blown apart by a shotgun blast at point-blank. With explosions in the background. The weapons range in S2 are amazingly fun to combine and shoot. From giant frickin' shotguns to electro-Tesla cannons to frickin' rockets, this game has all of your wont and destruction needs covered.
However, don't plan on coasting through this game by yourself. It's dangerous to go alone. Literally, it's pretty tough to beat a level with only one player, so do plan for near-mandatory online matches.
All in all, this is a great game. The first was a masterpiece, and this one is no different. Besides a very difficult single-player campaign, Sanctum 2 ranks pretty high in all parts. Do get yourself a copy, and your friends. You'll need them.

Freely place and move decoration like hedges and trees and flowers, stalls and shops, special items like garbage bins and toilets, and of course the enclosures! (And the animals in them.)
You can buy enclosure expansions and stick them to existing ones for more creative shaping of said enclosures (and redo it when you dump the stuff back into your inventory - it separates enclosure from expansions).
There's a great big variety of types of enclosures, and stuff to add to them, and from what I can tell, they all aren't merely cosmetic, but also make your zoo more attractive. There's also a great big load of animals to add, with, from what I've seen so far, a choice of up to 3 different types of enclosure you can put any specific animal into. Like you can put a parrot into Forest, Savanna, or Jungle, but obviously not into ice. :)
It's a bit of a shame that you can't put animals that would get on into the same enclosure, like sheep and goats for a petting zoo. (I don't know if at later levels there might be an actual petting zoo, though.)
You can lay paths any which way you like. But to remove them or rearrange the layout you have to buy 'remove path' pieces. (More bothersome than anything, and a bit tough to find. :) Might get a bit expensive when you need to re-buy rather than move the costlier types of paths. Or maybe by then their cost is negligible.)
There are Story-tasks to tend, and small tasks that pop up now and then that require direct interaction with stuff in your zoo. Unless you have hired help for that, then they'll tend most of those small tasks automatically (they won't build new enclosures or place animals). You need to be a certain level to build the administrative building that lets you hire folks for different things, but you also get a few free ones to test them out as reward for building it (which is a Story-task).
Without hired help, things like emptying garbage cans, feeding animals, collecting money, also needs to be done manually anyway. Gives you something to do while waiting for more cash. :)
Small bonuses turn up at every corner, like the treasure chest that gives random stuff after a time (which increases with each use, but can be reset with gems), daily booster pack, tending friends' zoos and collecting stars for an extra card. Some of these items are split into several pieces that you need to collect a certain amount of. You can also offer to trade these for what you want instead (the building for trade unlocks at some level, too, building it is another Story-task).
Btw, friends can only be made on the same language world (server). You can change world by changing to a different language in the settings for the game in Steam, but it'll be an entirely new zoo from the start there, then.
Lots of eye-candy, like cute little animations for every animal (shame they stay in their spot instead of moving around) and people walking around and stopping to look at stuff, and detailed plants.
And last but not least, there are great supportive devs, also active on the Steam forum!
