Much like Terraria, Starbound sets itself apart from the over-expanding genre of Survival Sandbox by removing a lot of the complications that require a huge time investment or constant checking back. The mechanics like crafting, mining, maintenance and travelling is simple enough that allows you to drop in for awhile to get things done. There is no need to spend hours just mining for resources to build a modest home as the process is not as tidious as other games of its genre.
Where it diverges from Terraria, is in its exploration and space travel. You are capable of travelling to different planets with different biomes and sub-biomes. You're not tied down to mining every worth out of the world you are given and travelling is even rewarded with Chests, Dungeons and NPC Villages scattered around other planets. The game heavily focuses on this as different resources can be found in different planets.
If your goal is to build a nice settlement, the game offers you not just the option of not having to ruin the world around you to gather its resources, but there are different Planets with different environments to provide you a suitable location for Bunkers, Underwater Domes, Huge Sprawling Buildings and even Space Stations. For those who just enjoy moving from planet to planet, your personal Ship is all you need for all your utility needs when exploring the huge galaxy.
The graphics is charming with a large range of colors and details for players and NPCs. The lighting system works nicely in creating ambience. The tiles available are nicely drawn and vary from Medival Bricks to Titanium Panels to the humble Wooden Plank.
To some, the amount of content may not be enough. Starbound is easily modded to fill in what you find lacking or to expand the game even further thanks to its modding community.
P.S. I absolutely adore the Avali custom race.

Originally touted as a Truce Crime game based in Hong Kong, Sleeping Dogs has you play as an undercover policeman infiltrating the triads. It’s an open world game, your character can go all around the city, steal cars and drive them, beat people up – the standard fare really. You have your standard missions, some for the police and some for the triads and a bunch of side missions and collectibles, – your standard fare really, nothing revolutionary. Now that’s fine, provided they have something about them that pulls me in. Sadly, it fails miserably to do that.
I was really hopeful for this one. From viewing the previews, it looked like the selling point would be the free running mechanics and a fun and very brutal fighting style, based in an open world Hong Kong. The free running works ok, but isn’t anything special. The fighting mechanics are similarly uninspiring. Since the Batman games came out, its fighting style has become the new formula that everyone has followed, from the combos, to counters to enemy types. Generally that’s a good thing as it’s an excellent system, but if you’re going to copy it at least do it properly! The controls are clunky, imprecise and unreliable, even compared to the original Arkham Asylum that came out 3 years before it! That’s almost a lifetime in video game terms, and it’s still worse!
This gripe runs right through the game. The free running mechanics fall way short of Assassins Creed (even the first one), the driving mechanics are ♥♥♥♥ing awful, shooting is very mediocre and the world, which initially looked like something that could draw me in, was really very dull. Hong Kong is presented as a large city, but everything looks the same, like they just recycled a couple of blocks over and over. Really, this game offers too little given when it was released. It feels like it came out early last console gen yet it actually came out at a similar time to games like Far Cry 3 – which is simply miles ahead of this game.
For the record, I didn’t finish the game so I can’t really say for definite how good the story is. I got 6 hours in, where my impressions were poor. The characters seemed shallow, voice acting was poor and Shen, the ‘protagonist’ just comes off as an unlikeable♥♥♥♥♥♥ Sure he’s a hard man, but when the only thing about his character is being able to punch things and the game isn’t even good at that, I think something’s wrong.
In summary, Sleeping Dogs is an ok game, but nothing more. It’s nothing special and doesn’t even work particularly well. There’s nothing unique or innovative about it and for that reason I can’t say there’s any reason to play it. Sure, if you’re dying for yet another cheap GTA knock off then give it a try, but given the massive amount of amazing games with truly innovative ideas and amazing stories, I couldn’t possibly recommend this. It’s not broken or offensively bad, but not very good either. Really, this game is just there.
Pros
•	OTT violent combat, great finishing moves
•	Emmm…
Cons
•	Clunky controls
•	Poor story
•	Terrible driving mechanics
•	Just boring
Final Score 6.5/10

Warning: ESSAY
Starbound demostrates a critical weakness in the Early Access format: Early Access games cannot be cancelled (Spacebase notwithstanding), no matter how fundamentally flawed their designs are.
Many other negative reviews have accused the development team of not doing anything, but this is untrue. A great deal of development has taken place on Starbound, said development has merely failed to move Starbound forward. We've been through what, four combat systems at this point? The fundamental problems of the game have if anything, gotten worse.
The design's two main problems are the infinite nature of the game world and overreliance on procedural generation. I will be comparing both of these points to Terraria, both because Terraria is a very good example of this genre and because the implict marketing of Starbound is "Terraria IN SPACE!"
The infinite planets in Starbound mean the game world has no persistence. There is no need to ever return to a planet, so the process of learning and modifing the geography is pointless. Likewise, the only persistent element of the game, the player's ship, is big enough to hold anything the player would want, so building on planets is pointless. Strangely, ships used to be small enough that storage space on planets was needed, but this was changed. The removal of the food system also removed the need to farm, one of the only other reasons to construct on planets. The game contains a good set of tools for building, there is merely not reason to do so. In Terraria the areas needed to advance are in the gameworld, thus rewarding exploration and the creation of routes. Starbound uses pre-scrptied areas with no spatial relationship to the gameworld. The only thing to do on planets is dig straight down and collect ore, and maybe clear out a dungeon for no reward.
This problem exacerbates, and is exacerbated by the second major problem with Starbound's design: the overuse of procedural generation. Every planet and monster is randomly generated in such a way that everything feels exactly the same. Every planet is the same under the crust (the only area that matters), and has the same set of four monsters: Guys that shoot you, flyers that shoot you, walkers that shoot you, and walkers that charge you. Contrast this with Terraria where even the starting forest has that level of enemy variety and different enviroments play quite differently.
Perhaps these problems could be resolved, but the course of development thus far has made me confident the development team doesn't even realize these problems have to be resolved.

What can I say that hasn't already been written.  I played/read through all three parts about 4 years ago using the fan sub version, as soon as saw the official English release on steam I knew I had to buy it.
The Muv Luv trilogy is a seminal visual novel, which builds your emotional attahment to the characters and their story as you progress through each game.
To get the most from the series you need to read them in order, think of Extra as the getting to know the characters/personalities of everyone.  Unlimited is then the introduction to the world/reality and Alternative is the main course.
Whilst Extra starts off as your typical high school/dumb guy gets the girl type visual novel it still stands up on its own. Some of the issues covered are hard hitting and emotional.
It is worth completing more than the two main heroine routes to experience these.
Unlimited follows a similar format to Extra but because of the new reality the characters are in starts to take on a slightly darker tone but still injects doses of humour.  Which ever ending you go with will still have an impact on you.
Overall these two are really worth the time to read/play through, not just for Alternative when its released, but as VN's in their own right.

Muv-Luv is a two part visual novel. First part is a standard rom-com and the second part is a sci-fi / adventure / action / mess. The Muv-Luv series has a large following and fanbase but a lot of it has to do with Alternative, the sequel to Extra and Unlimited.
The story, as already mentioned, is in two parts. Muv-Luv extra is a school rom-com. It is also exactly what you expect from a school rom-com, nothing special, nothing amazing. Just pull a few heartstrings, have a few laughs and there you have a successful rom-com. Nothing wrong with that mind, but some people might find it a bit dull. Unlimited, the second part, is a sci-fi / action / adventure / mess. The story itself is a bit cliché but again, and in my opinion, is not all that great. You spend most of the Unlimited story trying not to screw up your survival. The romantic routes barely differ from each other and it is very blunt about whose route you take.
The characters have very few unusual traits and are all terribly tropey. To drive a point home I will now state all of the main cast: the bland nice guy who all the ladies inexplicably fall for, the cute and dumb best friend, the bossy tsundere, the deredere, the one who doesn't speak much, the oblivious rich girl with no common sense, the mad scientist and the decent looking, kind teacher. It's like the guys who were looking for inspiriation played a game of darts with a trope stuck on both the triple score and single score areas, making it near impossible to make a non-tropey character and still win the darts match. I can't help but feel that despite the fact that they are likeable, they have very little depth.
The artwork, when looked at today, is ok. But you have to take into consideration that Muv-luv is over a decade old now, and when you notice that people still play it today without complaints about it, you realise that the artwork was pretty good.
good, but compared to some modern stuff, isn't actually that great but you can't expect it to be. So, fairly speaking, it has fared well. Another thing to state is that this is completely censored. I also couldn't care less about it and if you do, you can wait until later this month when the uncut patch is supposed to be released. The music, however, is nothing special. I could not pull any track out and call it great, but the soundtrack as a whole is not bad.
So in conclusion, the story of Extra is a standard school rom-com and you can expect exactly that out of it. You can expect it to pull a few heartstrings and to get a few laughs and all in all, have a good, dumb time. Unlimited, in my honest opinion was not great and while it too, does invoke some feels, it tends to drag on a bit. This is a critical part of the Muv-Luv series however and while it might not be everybody's cup of tea, if you intend to play Alternative you should play this. So if Alternative is what you are planning to play, you should start here. If you want to play a dumb rom-com VN then wait for it to go on to a good sale. If you want it uncensored, wait a few weeks (at time of edit, the patch has now been released). If you want to get into Muv-Luv I suggest you also wait for it to go on sale.

EDIT [2015-06-04]: This review is out-of-date. The developers contacted me to tell me they've greatly improved the game and ask me to play and review the game again which I just haven't gotten around to.
This game looks beautiful and I hardly ever encountered game breaking bugs, i.e. on average less then 1 in 10 hrs.
The game starts of nice and smooth, pacing feels good but soon turns into tedium. Around player level 10 you rarely get the feeling of progression. Still the game is quite addicting. It scrapes facebook-ishiness but manages to keep the player occupied, i.e. you don't have to wait for some stupid energy bonus to pop up every X minutes.
The reduction of player progress to a crawl is what makes me not recommend this game.
Fortunately this game is still in development (2014-11-04: version 0.3.1b.62) so you don't really need my partial venting below. However here are some pointers as to pros and cons for Steam Bandit Outpost. The wishlist at the end may also give more insights.
Pro:
* Nice graphics featuring multiple biomes and a multitude of NPCs and support characters
* Potential to be developed into a well-balanced game
* Good enough story
* Almost no game breaking bugs and only one so far a restart won't fix
* Highly addictive
Contra:
* No character development, only new characters and new equipment
* Combat disregards attack power and defensive capabilities
* Next to no rewards for grinding which is still essential to game progress
* Combat feels like stupendous clicking with unnecessary animation
* Bad management of Captain Missions
* Bad management of equipment (obvious tablet user interface structures)
* Bad crafting management
* Highly addictive
* Upgrades are expensive and their respective usefulness not well documented
About progress:
Outside the main story line which is bound to player level progress it gets pretty hard to acquire XP. For example, progress from level 13 to 14 needs 3,676 XP. The main story line provided something like 1K XP, don't really remember, let's say 2K. So you need over 1,5K XP to get to the next level. By that time I have occasional access to repeatable fights granting roughly about 8-15 XP. So in the unachievable best case that's 100 fights which you need to unlock as battle islands in repeatable captain missions - as opposed to player missions they need time to finish (10-20 minutes).
About fights:
Now, the actual bad thing here is that you need to go through fights and fights are boring. The standard attack does not develop yet, neither does defense - both are roughly fixed right now, i.e. a standard attack does around 10 damage except for misses or critical (x2). So you need to find weapons which have special attacks dealing triple, 10-fold, 14-fold damage. Those weapons are given to you at some predetermined points in the main story line and with them you have a good chance of winning a 15XP fight but the enemies may also just wipe the floor with your three fighters.
So, apart from a few boss fights, the "strategy" is hit enemies indiscriminately with your strongest attacks until one party is defeated. This alone calls for an autofight feature - right now your click and confirm each attack, targets are auto-selected and can be changed. The battle animations are unfuriatingly slow or rather feel that way after hundreds of fights. This calls for a skip animations feature.
Basic fights feel like obstacles rather than challenges. They require unending clicking and give almost no rewards - human enemies drop money (up to 8 gold; my next financial goal is 10K :( ) and the very rare random enemy may drop equipment. I almost want to request a throw dice option to just tell me if I win or lose simply in order to not have to sit through the fight.
About resources:
In order to progress you need resources of which there are 5 types which come in different qualities, e.g. Wood can be made into Planks which I guess can be made into Sturdy Planks. I know there are Sturdy Planks because I found them in a chest but I can not yet produce them. Why is this important? Because crawling progress. I can make Planks from Wood, i.e. 1 Plank from 28 Wood, a process which must be individually scheduled for each Plank and takes 10 seconds to complete without scheduling (which takes about 2 seconds). While a workshop produces nothing else can be scheduled.
The last level upgrade for my main building, I think to level 4, requires 96 Planks. So whatever amount of Planks I don't find I need to schedule in a workshop. I can have three workshops in parallel (actually more but then on different sites switching between those being to slow to be considered feasable). The upgrade also needs 96 Glass which can be produced from 28 Silica (sand) each - again in 10-second individually-scheduled production cycles.
This is fun for about 30 seconds.
Wishes:
* No Click-Through; clicking some UI elements also counts as a click on the terrain below deselecting buildings or resulting in unwanted movement
* Easier Captains Management; If there is a picture of a captain have access to load-out
* Easier Missions Management; Show all Captains with stats and all Missions as list
* When equiping captains make other captains easily available
* Have every time displayable on map, e.g. resource gathering buildings
** Display progress bars in interaction UI (bottom right), maybe along the circle, don't forget actual time
* Crafting queues
** In Engineering have a slider to order multiple productions of the same higher-level resource
* While equiping display in-battle skills (Heal, Smash, Poison etc.) with equipment
* It's bad design to have equipment that is a wrench not affect Engineering
* Have pets display required items before they are used
* Have building extensions show what they do (harvester 20->30;tavern 50->70->100)
* Have building show current stats, resources held vs max capacity
* Auto-fight/deactivate combat animations
* Remember starting settings
* Toggle animation of essential action aka less animation, more effect

Time to really update this review!
After the update I still keep my note of 9/10 and, but looks of it, it's going to be a 10/10 in the future. Considering it’s a small team, it’s a bit normal for updates to be delayed.
Now, i keep all the pros from the old version, but I would like to add more to the list:
-combat speed increased, but it’s a bit to easy
-island development is faster; from 96 wood planks and 96 glass for the level 5 office it went to 15 planks and 15 glass (same with all other buildings, but the ratio varies)
-character progress is faster
-with these 3, it’s very easy for a new player to check the game’s content faster than before
-extra story to fill in the gap
-lowered phone requirements (~900 mb and a really cheap smartphone required)
-it’s steampunk :D
Alpha2: 0.3.1b.62:
All I can say that the oct reviews are up to date. Don't know how the game was in the early stages, but now it's great! It is pretty linear until you hit level 10 and get yourself a jet pack and start sending captains on explore missions; these things can be easily obtained if you follow the quest line.
Considering that it's an early version, I would give it 9/10!
Pros:
-lovely design
-city building in a basic, but wonderful form
-enough RPG elements to make you wonder what's next
-option to play on PC and mobile (the phone requirements are really low excepting the ~1.8 gb required)
-ingame button to send bugs which really speeds up the process
-repeatable quests even if some are bugged; it can get you an extra daily hour for nice rewards
-FF/Septerra Core combat style
-option to explore different island (combat for XP and loot, resources, creature)
-resources generate while your away; the bigger the level the more resources it can hold
Cons:
-bugs (what do you expect in this stage?)
-FIXED: combat speed, but it'll be changed with the next update
-unbalanced captain missions (don't do the diplomatic escort!)
-FIXED: lack of content after level 13 (except the few daily missions)
-FIXED: takes some time to realize it's full potential
With all this said, I would recommend the game without a second thought!

Some pros and cons/suggestions
Pros:
+Vikings!
+Norse Mythology
+Graphics
+Seasons
+Random Events (though not too many so far)
+Territory Conquest
+Tech Tree
+Fun
+Strategy is required!
+Can upgrade workers' tools to improve them
+Can recruit a Giant hero after giving them a Valhalla's worth of food.
+Combat can be somewhat micro'd (though selection of a specific unit is difficult)
+Great performance (only a half second hiccup when the season switches back to Spring from winter)
Cons/Suggestions:
-Map Customization options are too limited - need geography sliders, separate islands, climate
-Defensive fortifications are too limited - need a fort and palisades. I get why Towers can't attack into enemy territory but they should have an attack radius into friendly territories.
-Only Vikings - Would love to see Saxons, Picts, Frisians, Irish, Germanic Tribes, Russians (yes, very ambitious, sorry)
~Would like to see some Persistent Element to the game - ideally in the form of a customizable warchief that carries with you between games.
-Longboats need another use - transport and landing on enemy coasts (even if unexplored).
-I can't say I'm too fond of the scouting mechanic.
~I would love the option to be able to slow down the seasons so each month lasts a little longer.
-Unhappiness is too great early game and unnecessarily slows down progression.
Features Added due to Community Request:
<>Victory Condition Options! (3/2/17)
<>Unit variety removed from cons! Yay! SHIELD WALL!
<>Multiplayer added (5/21/17)
<>Females have arrived from the homeland.
I look forward to subtracting from this list as time goes on.

Sanctum 2 is a hybrid of the tower defense and first-person shooter genre. It runs in a 3D environment and posseses a stylized aesthetics. Based on the peer 2 peer system, sanctum 2 allows you to play solo with a perfect ping or join existing rooms of other players that are set to public, with a max of 4 players per room. The game also has a unique and captivating story as well as characters for those who are interested in these things. The soundtrack aint half bad either.
This game offers a variety of gameplay styles due to the abundance of perks or passives and different types of towers both made available as you level up. This is accompanied by unique character classes that offer a specialized approach to gameplay. For example, Simo is a sniper class that has better accuracy (less spread of bullets), and deals more damage on weakspots. It is also possible to draw enemy attention or aggro by getting into their face, and the character Haigen Hawkins was designed with this in mind.
One thing to remember though is that this game is both a tower defense game and an fps. You can't go one way without the other and you will be rewarded for shooting the enemies where it hurts as well as being able to conceptualize the best tower placements. It's a thinking + shooting game, and one that I recommend.

I have history with this game, I remember it like it was yesterday and by yesterday I mean 2009 on the PS3. When I picked this game up I thought great it's just going to be another burnout like always... but I was so wrong. This game to put it lightly was the start of a new era in the racing genre and at the time it may have just been a little ahead of it's time.
This has everything you would crave for in a burnout game, it has road rage, stunt runs, races, marked man and showtime just to name a few. The biggest and most amazing-est addition was free-roam and oh my god it is fun, with that comes a bunch of things like road rules, exploration, smashing fences and billboards, stunt jumps, hidden car parks, secret locations. Car unlocks are great you progress through and once you unlock one you go out into the open world and smash it down to collect it in your garage or you can collect some through collectibles and by completing a burning route race. Junkyards are your garages for cars, bikes etc there's also paint shops (gas stations). If your not the biggest fan of cars the ultimate box comes with bikes with there own set of races. It has online and there you can roam, race and explore with friends or strangers. Did I mention the soundtrack? OH THE SOUNDTRACK is something to admire because it's the kind of playlist you won't hear nowadays. The keyboard and mouse work fine fully rebind-able keys and the same goes for a controller straight out of the box. Navigation in this game is simple yet so good it doesn't hold your hand, you have to remember paths and sometimes rely on tail lights. The crash cams are still as good as they use to be if not better, with all the head on collisions and metal scrapping and crunching. The greatest thing about this game is the fact that the game revolves around what you progress through, there's no story just freedom.
I would love to say this game has nothing wrong with it I really really really do want to say it's perfect but it's not and why is that? Firstly the big issue is the false advertising since I've been around from the early days the ultimate box feels like a scam, I mean all you get is free DLC "FREE" everything else you have to buy which would be fine if the store didn't shut down, if you want the awesome content you have to go through a bunch of loopholes. Secondly they left out content which are "Cop and Robbers" and "Big Surf Island" huge content missing from a near perfect game. Also a minor issue is the game doesn't have windowed mode so for all you lovers out there sorry but it just straight up isn't here.
I would still say the game is worth buying because the single player is still fun and the community is some what still active, BUT if you do have the option to purchase a console copy go straight ahead because at least there you'll get a more updated version.

A huge improvement on the first, Sanctum 2 possesses so much more content that it will keep you coming back over and over again. If you've played the first and enjoyed it to some extent, you should definitely consider buying Sanctum 2. It improves on the gameplay of the first in that you now have perks, a wide variety of weapons to choose from and an abundance of unlockable towers, of which you can mix and match your choices with any friends you are playing with to actualise a coherent strategy.
Most of the gameplay revolves around elements that are standard to the tower defence genre; a key difference is that it also combines fps gameplay with the tower defence elements to provide a unique gameplay experience. Enemies will not only focus on reaching the core of the level (which, if destroyed, will end the game) but will now also assault the player, who can also die. This adds new strategies that can be applied to the game, as you can kite certain enemies if necessary.
In conclusion the game is a vast improvement on the original, and the original was a decent experience in and of itself. I'd recommend it to anyone who enjoys either tower defence, fps or strategy games. 4/5

The Muvluv trilogy is simply fantastic. As someone who had read Muvluv Extra, Muvluv Unlimited, and Muvluv Alternative, I can honestly say it was one of my favorite stories I've had the pleasure to read. Extra and Unlimited (the two parts included in this purchase) will probably range from good to mediocre depending on your tastes. The first two parts of the Muvluv trilogy are lighthearted and comical. However, even if your not a fan of Extra and Unlimited's more carefree tone, I highly reccomend you still read them. Muvluv Alternative is a dark and grueling experience that many, including me, would say is a contender for the best Visual Novel ever made. Despite its cute appearance, Muvluv is not for the faint of heart. If you don't feel things by the end of Muvluv, either you weren't paying attention or you're a heartless alien uncapable of human emotion. To tell you anything else about Muvluv would just spoil the experience.
Anyone who is a fan or visual novels or just dark, mature stories in general will love Alternative. Sadly, Alternative is not included in this purchase, so make sure to buy that too (when it is released on steam later this year). Trust me, its worth every penny.

HONEST REVIEW: I would only recommend this game for any person that remembers what it was like to truly win at something and not just be handed a participation trophy. Fighting games and particularly Street Fighter games require 100s of hours of practice to just get good. There are no short cuts, there are no easy level ups. You have to devote yourself to learning how to beat the other person with your character of choice. Playing street fighter is like playing chess and poker in 1/12 of a second increments. You have to make the right move or the right call FAST! There's no easy win here boys and girls. It's a game where it's just you and your opponent, no teams to bail you out or blame for their terrible plays. You have to hold that "L" all to yourself, so if you want to know what it's like to really be a winner then pick up this game and play it. Play it until you hate, then play it some more until you realize how amazing this game truly is. Once you finally reach that level where you can dominant your opponent. That's when you'll know what it feels like to truly be a winner.
Pros:
• Amazing multiplayer with a good list of characters and more to be added (well balanced as of 7-1-16)
• Awesome story mode (4 hours of content with some good humor and surprises)
• Training mode (with recorder) to practice numerous setups. Needs a few more tweaks and online mode to practice with a friend, but taht should be coming.
• Graphic Modding (don't like a skin. Change it)
• Capcom is fully backing this game with updates on a monthly basis so more content will be added all the time. Majority of the content can be earned for free by playing the game or paid for if you wish. Only cosmetic items like premium outifts will cost you.
Cons:
The game was released early as it was rushed to be ready for the 2016 tournament season. The multiplayer was finished, but everything else was not so the game has suffered in reviews. Since Feb. the game has seen a number of additions with more coming so I believe most of these will be addressed in up to a years time with that said as of 7-1-16 there are still a few things that need to be addressed but are not game breaking such as:
• Rage quitting in ranked (no true deterrent as of yet), but can be avoided in casuals or battle lounges
• 8 frames of input delay (this affects your ability to react to punish moves. It's currently under review by capcom to address it)
• Rather long load times between matches. 30 seconds to a minute feels like forever when you are staring at a blank screen.
• The in game recording of your stats is still not functional (It's sort of like a fitness tracker for your character)
• Model clipping that makes the game feel a little cheap and unpolished. (I have a feeling this will be addressed last as it's only noticeable on load screens).

The second game of the Dreamscape duology, there were definitely improvements though there were some sacrifices made to make that happen. They managed to include Hidden Object scenes so this game is officially a HOG.
PROS:
> They definitely raised the bar with the graphics, the backgrounds and items were pretty HD on widescreen but it's not surprising since this game is from 2014-2015. The quality is definitely up to par with Artifex games, with pleasing visuals and special effects.
> Dynamic hint system that's like a minigame in itself
> Still packed with achievements, morphs, bonus content and gameplay
> The interface was easier to use and navigate
> Puzzles were still varied and they looked good!
> You only experience HO scenes once per chapter (as opposed to most games using it twice)/HO scenes don't repeat
CONS:
> The voice acting is still pretty lackluster, and the horrible Sandman accent is back and still grates my ears
> Really unattractive character models, it's a really recent game so there isn't any excuse for them looking like they came straight out of 2005! The cat looked like a scary muppet...
> The story didn't have any build-up and the conclusion was horribly rushed. The entire plot of this game felt like a giant bonus chapter content rather than a story of its own.
> HO scenes were weak and posed no challenge but I can appreciate that they looked consistent, hand-drawn and not horrifically cluttered
> There isn't a lot of puzzles in this game and it felt like it focused on the point-and-click item rubbing aspect
Overall, this game is even more average than the first, now neutralized by the HO scenes (they really weren't all that necessary). The graphics though was pleasing, and I really enjoyed how clean and polished it all looked. Basically, it felt like decoration---nice to look at but that's all there is. I'd recommend it to anyone who has an hour or two to spend.

The is a sequel to Dreamscapes: The Sandman, which I played and reviewed
The story follows the first game where the Sandman now is taking control of Tim, Laura’s husband. You play as the same unknown person as before trying to help defeat the Sandman by going into Tim’s mind and exploring his memories. As opposed to the first game, this one does have several static hidden object scenes.
The art style is even better and very sharp. I believe it ran at my monitor’s native resolution which is 1440p. I assume it’s upscaled from 1080p, but this is a big step up from the 1024x768 max of the first game.  Animations were nicely done and the effect of the flying sand for the Sandman was really awesome.
The puzzles are pretty easy and there really are not too many of them. The main portion of the game centers around finding items to use on other items in the environment.
There was no mention of what the different difficulties do, but I played on Expert and would recommend this unless you want a
easy time through the game.
Voice acting is still pretty bad and laughable at times. Also, the text dialog when you click on things can give away too much of what you need to do.
I noticed throughout my playthrough that the pauses between scene changes and event activations was noticeably slow. It may only be for a brief second or two but was something that caught my attention.
When playing with the inventory locked on the screen, going back in certain scenes would be tricky to get the back (down) arrow to appear. I ended up playing through with the inventory unlocked and that worked out better for me.
+60fps
+Detailed art and environments
+Nice animations
+Collectibles
+Voice acting
+Too easy
+Plot is less interesting this time
+Pauses between scenes and action
+Moving back a scene can be tricky with inventory locked (see above explanation)

Compared to LEGO Marvel Super Heroes, this game feels like a gigantic step backwards. First off, this game feels like a poor movie to video game adaptation compared to the previous LEGO games like LEGO Indiana Jones or Lord of the Rings. I think the issue is that the game shackles itself to the movie and tries to follow it too closely, which breaks the whole theme of the movie which is about being creative with LEGOs. I think the game would have been much better off if it had been a prequel or parallel story of some sort that could better utilize the potential presented by the world of the LEGO movie.
This unsatisfying story is exacerbated by the rather pitiful overworld that is miniscule in comparison to other recent LEGO games like Lord of the Rings or Marvel Super Heroes. Bricksburg is all of two city blocks, the wild west is the town square, and cloud cuckoo land is two or three (small) clouds. There's a few side quests to do in these hubs, but they pale in comparison to the previously mentioned LEGO games and make this game about half as long in comparison.
To add insult to injury, the game has a surprisingly decent selection of vehicles that can be built from the treasures found in the missions but they can only be used in the bonus room (i.e. a kid's bedroom) which is basically sterile and devoid of interesting things to smash. A huge letdown from the bonus areas of the previous LEGO games.
This is all on top of the standard LEGO game bugs which required me to restart some of the missions partway through because a script wouldn't work and I would be stuck. The character creator is also fairly pitiful.
The one highlight of this game is that it adds giant mechs that can be used in some of the missions. Those would have been fun if Bricksburg had been a proper city and if the game allowed vehicles to be spawn in the hubs.
Overall I was disappointed by this LEGO game and wouldn't recommend it unless you're trying to collect all the LEGO games. Even if you liked the LEGO movie, I would say go play some of the older LEGO action games or find an old LEGO creator game instead.

Normally I do not purchase early access games, but I had been following this game for quite some time. When I saw it included in a bundle it was a no brainer, so I got it. This game alone has changed my opinion of early access games completely! This is a fun, light hearted, casual city builder/RPG. You build a city and collect resources every so often, adventuring to other lands inbetween. The graphics are great and everything runs really smoothly.
Pros:
Charming graphics
Multitude of things to do
combines city builder/RPG really well
Resource collecting/crafting implemented very nicely
Cons:
Combat animations are to slow
No world map for the different islands you visit
As others have mentioned the combat can be agonizingly slow, especially against some enemies that heal every other turn and drag out the fight. So I would recommend some tweaking to the combat system overall! Also seems like no matter what weapon you choose, you do the same amount of damage. While combat is annoying, I am able to look past this for now.
The other major downfall of this game is there is no world map for the lands you visit. I constantly find myself wondering around trying to find a specific person for different quests. This can be really annoying when trying to progress through the game.
Overall it is a well polished game, and a steal for $15! In its current state I would rate it about a 7.5/10. I have faith that it will reach its full potential in the near future!

This game is aweeeesome!!! I loved the original Sanctum for the fact that I LOVE Tower Defense games. I loved building tonnes of towers all over the map and was kind of disappoined by the way that Sanctum 2 was re-engineered compared to it's predecessor...
I recently got myself a new graphic card and decided to buy the game when it was on special. I tried it and was slightly confused by how the game worked.. There seemed to be a restriction on the amount of towers which was 15....???
But after playing the game more with my friends online I have started to enjoy it much more and begain to quickly realise exactly why these changes were actually HUGE improvements over the original game.
As much as I loved Sanctum 1, Sanctum 2 has just become a much more immersive experience and enjoyable experience.
I'll give reasons why I love this game below!
1) Building even more complex mazes than the original game.
2) Experimenting with the awesome variety and different combinations of towers. (There are so many different towers, from long range cannons, lasers, lightning, mind control, anti-air, ground pounders, slow generators, supports towers to increase damage and range of neighbouring towers as well as other misc ones I'll leave up to you to find out about yourself)
3) HUGE selection of perks that allow you to drastically customize how your character plays.
4) The maps are really well designed, both in aesthetics and well thought out design to really make you think about the most appropriate towers for each situation.
5) The challenge that comes from trying to deal with different combinations of enemies AND the bosses that can wreak havoc on your maze.
6) The gorgeous graphics in general.
7) Huge selection of maps.
8) Sandbox mode that allows you to have as many towers as you want(Which shows that the game was designed to have 15 turret cap to keep the game strategic and trust me, it really forces you to make the right decisions and think strategically)
9) 5 different characters that have different traits and primary weapons.
10) Secondary weapons are unlockable and allow you to completely change the feel of each character.
11) Completely overhauled enemies from the original sanctum as well as a big variety of New enemies, some gargantuan aliens that I can guarantee you will have a tough time dealing with!
12) Easy and Fast game creation allowing drop in and drop out at any time for your friends to come and join the fray, with each player having their own choice of 4 different towers to use.
13) This time the enemies can see you and react to you. They are actually intelligent and won't hesitate to mash your face to a pulp if you get too close. Some of the enemies just run straight for the core, but others will spit and shoot at you, blast you with shock waves, charge at you and pound their fists into you until you are dead. This time they are not push overs. But neither are you. You can  hit back, and hard!
This game is NOT Sanctum 1 so do NOT expect to just let your towers do all the work.
This game focuses a LOT on First Person Shooter action.. This time, when you use guns you actually feel like you're doing damage which was a problem in the first game as the enemies got tankier and tankier.
This time around the enemies don't get any stronger as the waves progress, there are just more of them and brutal combinations of enemies that will really force you to make the right choices for tower selection.
If you are quick witted, strategic and with good aim then this game will be right up your alley.
Before playing this game I was frustrated and annoyed by the choice they made to have a cap of 15 towers to use in the campaign. I loved the tall tower blocks and slow fields in Sanctum 1. I loved the way you could upgrade 6 times in Sanctum 1. I also loved the way I could upgrade my own weapons.
But this time around in Sanctum 2 I can Guarantee that there is NO need or WANT for upgrading your weapons as the perks system is far superior in allowing you to create a much more enjoyable experience.
The weapons feel far stronger in Sanctum 2. They are extremely customisable in how they function. The towers are FAR more interesting. The maps are far superior. The graphics are MUCH better. The Character selection is AWESOME.
The Towers can be upgraded from Level 1 to level 3. Which might not seem like much but you can permanently over-charge towers. (Some towers gain more range when over-charged, others gain damage.. But it doesn't stop at just range and damage... Find out for yourself! :D )
I give Sanctum 2 a Solid 10 out of 10 for gameplay, graphics, strategy, customisability and simplicity.
The story however seems completely not relevant to my experience, I have barely read a word of the story in fact... But somehow it makes you feel more in tune with the characters, making the experience just that tad better.
The only thing I could see done to improve this game would be to add rendered cutscenes but this is completely irrelevant.
Awesome game and worth buying whether it's on special or not.
A Big Thumb Up The Bum for Sanctum 2!!!

I'd say this is definitely one for strategy fans to keep an eye on and even in it present state I would say it's a good value proposition.

I don’t remember why, but last weekend I was browsing through Steam—also known as video game heaven—when I saw that there was a game that was free to play for that weekend only.  It was also on sale for eighty-five percent off, and before even trying it, I took a leap of faith and bought the complete game with all of its DLCs (downloadable content) for a whopping $3.70.
Brave, I know.
The game is called Sanctum 2.  I had never heard of it before, but its brief description—and its price tag—caught my interest.  Sanctum 2 is a tower defense (TD) and first-person shooter (FPS) hybrid game.  As with any other TD game, you must construct a maze of turrets from a spawn point to an end point, utilizing the space given to you as efficiently as possible in order to safely clear each wave of invaders.
And in Sanctum 2, you also get to shoot them yourself.
This game enthralled me so much because of how it blends the two genres.
When I was in elementary school and middle school, I played a lot of tower defenses with my older brothers on Warcraft 3.  The last couple of years, my brothers and I typically spend our scarce free time together playing a variety of zombie survival shooters, like the ones introduced in the Call of Duty franchise.
Sanctum 2 sounded like it expertly mixed both of those into one game, so I bought it not only for myself but for my brothers as well, since the game has four-player co-op.  After already logging thirty hours after less than a week, I can safely say that it was worth the investment.
The game has a healthy amount of complexity.  The goal is simple: defend your core by building a maze, force the aliens to travel through the maze by making it the only way to the core (which is their goal), and line that maze with all sorts of different turrets to whittle the alien forces down.  All the while, you’re running around through the maze or aiming down a barrel from the high ground to pick off their numbers yourself.
But Sanctum 2 also has enough content to keep its players entertained for a long time.  With all five DLCs, the game offers thirty-two unique levels, which is a lot considering how large each one is.  I’ve spent twenty minutes aimlessly walking the corridors of the buildings in the levels before, testing how detailed and expansive the game really is.
It’s rather detailed and expansive.
In addition to the wide variety of levels, the game also offers a story-based campaign, three other game modes, five playable character classes, sixteen weapons, twenty unique turrets, and over fifty “perks” or attributes to customize your character.  Not only are there a lot of levels to play, but you can still play the same level over and over again with different settings and equipment.
The game is not only addictive, but it is also beautiful.  The game’s alien world has breathtaking scenery.
Despite being a lesser known game, Sanctum 2 feels like it was a large-scale project by a major company.  But I’ve never heard of Coffee Stain, its creator.  I think that just goes to show that some of the best games are those made by the “Indie” companies.
I would rate this game a 9.5 out of 10, and I withhold the remaining 0.5 only because I want the creator to continue this series and somehow improve it further—perhaps with even more content.
It is a game I think just about anyone can pick up and enjoy, and the game is normally only $25.00 for the complete pack, which is a price I would still easily pay after testing the game out.
If you enjoy playing tower defenses, I would recommend you pick this game up.  Although it is the second game in its series, Sanctum 2 really takes the genre in a great direction, vastly improving upon the content and feel of its predecessor.  Even if you’re not that keen on tower defenses, I would still urge you to try this game, as it is an amazing experience with the company of three friends.
This game is worth a try.  I couldn’t give it a higher rating.

Cons:
-Now, I know this game IS in early access and features are bound to disappear and reappear without much notice but what was one of the defining features of the game, and the thing that made it stand out from others in its genre was that monsters didn't do damage on contact. They had specialized moves that hurt you if you touched them, for example you could stand in front of a monster and then it would swipe upwards, damaging you. But this is now gone, replaced with the whole 'damage on contact' as WELL as the melee and ranged attacks. Overall, Starbound is an amazingly fun game and I highly recommend it. I love it so much, it's the most played game and I have over 100 hours- and that's since July last year, on top of an immense homework load, limited screen time and frequent holidays.

Fun game with lots of potential
This is a review for the early access copy of Blitzkrieg 3 running on a MacBook Pro 2015.
On initial release back in April, it wouldn’t even load. Instead it froze or restarted.  At that time I left a negative review and asked for a refund.  Several weeks later with a new copy and the updates, I am able to play the German Faction with only one crash. It does take a long time to load, but this is probably due to my system not the game.
Id think on a strong PC, the code might run smoother and be more enjoyable.
I appreciate that the developer's respond to emails about the game.  They seem motivated to make it better
Commanders:
Each faction (german, british, soviet) has general's. In a battle, these general bestow certain bonuses to their respective units (artillery general buffs artillery, air marshall buffs air resupply). After a win, there is a chance the general might give access to a new unit via the deck.
Deck:
By playing (and replaying battles with different commanders) one builds up a deck of units. Units from your deck may be swapped and customized for a battle. Each unit has a corresponding value and rarity. The particular scenario caps the initial units, so its a balance.
Engineers:
Winning battles bestows research points which can be used for upgrades. The tech tree flows through three eras of the war and the upgrades seem reasonable
After playing a few skirmishes, one can play PvP in base defense or skirmishes which is pretty fun. Eventually, one might expect some mods and an interesting community of players
The good:
-Not swamped with microtransactions or DLC’s, yet.
-By using different commanders, one can adjust play style and unit selection giving replayability.
What I’d like to see:
On field repairs of vehicles, perhaps using resupply points as repair currancy once a vehicle is withdrawn from combat.
-Engineer units to make traps and defense
Overall: its a fun RTS with lots of potential.  After a decade of COH(2), its nice to have something new.

This review is divided into three parts :
What you will find in the game
Evaluation of each aspect of the game
Whether I recommend it or not.
Content
Muv Luv is what is called a visual novel. A visual novel is essentially a visual and audio interactive book. You read dialogues on static pictures while listening to the voices and music. From time to time you are offered with choices that could change the story. The gameplay is thus almost non-existent but that shouldn't stop from enjoying a visual novel if you can enjoy book.
Muv Luv contains actually two stories. The first one, Muv Luv Extra is about the daily life and romance of Shirogane Takeru, a Japanese high school student. The second, Muv Luv Unlimited, is about military training in an apocalyptic future. I can’t say anymore about that. Muv Luv Unlimited is closely linked with Muv Luv Extra so you absolutely have got to play Extra first.
To go into more details about Muv Luv Extra, there 6 girls you can date. Sumika, the childhood energetic girl, Meiya, the heir of one of the biggest company in the world, Tama, a friend that looks like a cat, Ayamine, the stoic girl and finally Sasaki, “iinchou”, the class president. All of them are very unique and enjoyable. Oh and yes, there is one more (or two) girls but...
The first story lasts about 20 hours. The second story also about 20 hours but then you can replay it by choosing another route (girl). Unfortunately the first half of the game will almost be the same. I only played Meiya and Sumika routes so I don’t know about the others.
Note that everyone is voiced in Japanese except Takeru, the main character. That is done deliberately to help you put you in the shoes of Takeru.  Feeling immersed in the Muv Luv is very important to enjoy it.
About the H content, there should be a free 18+ patch available later.
2. Evaluation
Graphics : Muv Luv was released in 2006, 10 years ago. Because the graphics are anime-styled, it doesn’t matter as much how old it is.The art style is different from most modern anime production ( less round, more straight) but I still think it is a plus. The interface looks and works very nicely. This is a huge improvement over the original game. They are a number of CGs but not that much compared to, say Fate Stay Night. Still, I think it is enough and moreover they are used effectively. Also because the sprites are well drawn, I would say the graphics are quite good for a visual novel. Rating : 4/5 .
Musics : Like the graphics, I think they are very good and particularly fitting to each scene.  Nonetheless save for a few of them, they are not exceptionally good. Rating : ⅘
Gameplay : It’s a visual novel. Rating : ../5
Story : The story of Extra or Unlimited or even Alternative alone is not exceptional. However if you read Extra and Unlimited then it becomes great. If you add Alternative then it becomes exceptional. A masterpiece. That’s the reason it is seen as one of the very visual novel ever. Nonetheless, make no mistake, Extra alone is at least good and likely very good! It’s funny, light-hearted and touching. Rating of Extra and Unlimited: 4/5 if you don’t read Alternative. 7/5 if you read the trilogy.
Value for money : The price of Extra and Unlimited is about $28 and gives you more than 40 hours of content. A book costs about $6 and can be read in 5 hours if you’re very fast.So you have the same content as a book of the same price. Except you have pictures. And musics. And choices. It should be clear that Muv Luv is very good value for money. Rating : 5/5.
Final evaluation : 4.5 /5 a very good game
3. Recommendation
It should be clear that I strongly recommend it. However if you :
Don’t like reading
Don’t like comedy
Don’t like anime/manga (even so, maybe you could give it a try?)
Then you should not buy it. In the other cases, buy it and enjoy it at your leisure! You will have to wait for the climax, Alternative which should be released in December, anyways. I recommend you to at least clear Extra once first, preferably Sumika or Meiya and then play Unlimited.

Crossbow Warrior – The Legend of William Tell is an action platformer game, developed by MobyDick Games, releasing in early December 2015.
Usually I am not a massive fan of platformer games, but this one took me by surprise. The game play is somewhat easy to grasp and pleasantly fun to play. You play as William Tell, a crossbow warrior. The platforming is done slightly different, you can sometimes be playing from a side view simply traversing the environment, sometimes you can be in a third person view taking on an endless runner sort of challenge as you try to dodge on coming obstacles. There is a small element of combat too, which I wasn’t a huge fan of, simply because it is hard to control the crossbow. It takes about three seconds for your character to ready himself to fire, and the aiming technique feels very clunky and hard to actually figure out where your shot will land due the poor hitbox detection.
Crossbow Warrior can be controlled either using the keyboard, or a controller. For platformers, the norm would be to use a controller, so this is what I opted for, but it just didn’t feel very responsive to my actions, there is a slight delay in between pressing the button and what is actually carried out on screen. Obviously in platformers you need there to be no latency at all with the controls so this was very off putting and did hamper the gameplay to quite a large degree. Some people have noted that you don’t get the latency issue with the keyboard but it is still hard to control any sort of platformer with a keyboard. This really needs to be addressed in a patch in the future.
From the screenshots on the Steam store, the graphics look really nice, and whilst they do look really impressive in game, there are some moments where you are stunned at some really poor work. For instance, the enemies are very poorly rendered at a very low quality. The environments and backdrops you are playing in though are really beautiful; and the water effects are actually very very good. The graphics are somewhat of an up and down issue with Crossbow Warrior; I wouldn’t be too bothered about them if the gameplay were up to scratch.
The early levels of the game are very simple; you can easily progress to about the half way point in the game in just over an hour – that is where the difficulty starts to ramp up though. The difficulty is definitely not helped by the controller issues, but there is a significant increase in the mechanics you have to use to progress. The game does a good job of splitting up the different types of stages you have to complete, so you don’t get the same missions repeated after each other. You can add a little more difficulty to your run through by trying to collect all the items in the levels as well as trying to beat the “expert time”.
I finished the game in just over three hours. I felt that to be just the right length before the technical issues with the game really became an actual major annoyance. There may be an essence of replay ability with Crossbow Warrior with the mechanics such as beating the expert times, but sadly I don’t have any urges at the moment to go back and complete them, so I am happy with the one play through, and I would think most would be satisfied with that too.
Apart from the glaring issues with the controller latency, I did notice a few other problems, such as a minor stuttering issue on some of the levels which are obviously more graphically intensive. Also the game launches in German language for some reason and even after you change the language, some of the menu text still remains in the wrong language which I thought was a bit sloppy.
To sum up, Crossbow Warrior – The Legend of William Tell is a game that I am struggling to put into either of the categories of thumbs up or thumbs down. I am going to recommend the game, simply because, yes I did finish the game and yes I did have some fun whilst playing it. It is by far one of the better platformer games, this is definitely not helped by the controller problems, but it is definitely not the worst platformer on Steam. The regular price of £4, 99 is fair but I can certainly see this game being included in a couple bundles over the coming months.

Disclaimer: I'm new to VAs.
Compelling story, interesting characters, art is spectacular. Game is not absurdly long, you'll likely set it down once before finishing your first walkthrough. Even if you don't, there isn't a lingering feeling of being taken for your time/money (one of my major concerns going in), which is really nice. After saving Laura from her dreams and from the Sandman, she has now the Power. However, she can't use it for herself and the Sandman used that knowledge to attack her dear friend and now husband Tim. You're the only one she can count on, so, you're going to save Tim from his nightmares and put an end to the Sandman's revenge.
Dreamscapes: Nightmare's Heir is the sequel of Dreamscapes: The Sandman. While it's not an obligation to play the first game, I suggest you to strongly do it, as you will have a better understand of what's happening. The story is still nicely written and if you played the first game, you knew that there was going to be a sequel at one point. Here it is, with the Sandman ready to take over Tim and taunting you about failing this time (though he was sure of that in the first game too). As usual, a cute creature is helping you, though it's not Benny anymore but another one.
There was a huge change in the gameplay: now, you have hidden objects scenes included, where the first game was just a point-&-click with puzzles. It doesn't change anything in the end, as it's still pleasant to play puzzles (they're easy) and to clear the scenes, with a well-balances difficulty. The beholders are still there, however, where in the first game, it was easier to find them, here, they're kinda very small apart for some.
As you're now in Tim's nightmare, you have different fears to face than in Laura's story. They're less into "exotic" locations: everything is way more darker than for Laura - if I think about the depths of the sea and the swamp - else, Tim was twice in a house, in an apartment and on a road. I don't mind a change of scenery but I wish it was more inviting to a journey. However, I found the apartment's dream very interesting as everything is in black and white, like in an old polar story and items themselves in your inventory were in black and white. But the graphics are still good, though I found Laura's hands a little too big in the cutscenes.
The soundtrack is also fitting to the ambiance. And the voice acting is good too, mainly our adorable creature's sounds.
The big relief is that Dreamscapes: Nightmare's Heir doesn't suffer of crashes, like for The Sandman where you had to set the CPU affinity to 0 or 1. It means mainly that you can play the game without having to worry about any workaround or crash or corrupt files. I don't know what really changed for that though.
Dreamscapes: Nightmare's Heir is the sequel you were waiting for, without crashes, with new worlds to visit, though now, it's Tim who is affected, and with hidden object scenes that are breaking the monotony of using items and going back and forth between locations.

The game uses hub worlds which house connected, individual levels. Very reminiscent of late 90s platformer games. There's a lot of stuff to do in each hub world and the connected levels. Expect around 10-13 hours of playtime to reach the ending and around 20-24 hours to 100% the game.
Pretty varied but all challenges and puzzle are based around LEGO. Each minifig has a specific ability that you'll have to use in order to progress throughout the level. There are some fun minigames sprinkled around the levels, in just enough quantity to keep the player interested.
The game looks pleasant to the eye. Level design is varied, rich with little details. Graphical fidelity could be slightly better but it does its job.
Sound effects are decent. Character voices sounds alright in most cases (with the exception of a few lines of dialogue that sound rather silly). Soundtrack is interesting and uses tracks from the movie. Oddly enough, Batman's "no parents" song from the movie seems to be replaced with a generic drumstep wub-a-thon, for some strange reason (licensing issues maybe?).
You play as over-night-chosen-one Emmet (and friends) trying to stop President Business from ruling the world. The game closely follows the story of the movie, although it expands the first two acts of the movie and shortens the 3rd act into just a few levels. This actually works in favour of the game, as you're able to explore more of the areas that were hastily rushed through in the movie. In theory, you could just play the game without watching the movie as the story is explained pretty well in the game. Still, I'd personally recommend watching the movie first.
Runs without any issues on my 5 year old PC (Dual-Core 2.66GHz, GeForce 9600GT, 2GB RAM) on 1920x1080 resolution with SSAO and V-Sync turned off. No jittering, no sudden framerate drops. Loading times are usually pretty short. Expect way better perfomance on newer machines than mine.
Yes, the "Bonus Room" is a very cool touch.
The game suffers from some really weird collision and clipping bugs. Didn't break the game for me but it was annoying at times, forcing me to restart a level at some point. Also, the minifig selection screen is a mess and doesn't explain which minifig has which ability.
I give The LEGO Movie Videogame a double-decker couch out of 5.

People complain that you're a father/mother and not your own character. Okay.
-Fallout 3 you're a man/woman trying to find your father
-Fallout New Vegas you're a man/woman trying to find your killer.
Now you're a father/mother trying to find your son. OH GOD! HOW HORRIBLE! Now don't get me wrong, I am fully against paid mods. It's pathetic. More so than the lootbox system companies are trying to enforce (and sadly being successful at doing so so far despite it usually being optional). Apart from the negativity however, Fallout 4 to me is the best in the series. Here's why.
You are....wait for it....you. The difference is, you had a family before the nuclear apocalypse. And you have a son. Your wife was killed and you task yourself to finding your son and why he was taken by mysterious people. The story isn't the greatest. None of the Fallout stories are. But as far as stories go, it's okay.
Yes, this is still an RPG. You still level up, get skills and have the famous V.A.T.S. system. Looting is a lot more convenient. Unlike all the previous games, power armor isn't something you can just freely walk around with 24/7 and I love that about this game! It's unrealistic to be able to walk around with that much bulk without some sort of POWER to get it running. You can upgrade your power armor, customize the paint (which has bonuses for a complete set) and get different/more powerful sets. The same goes for weapons and regular armor. I love upgrading and tuning my armor and weapons to how I'd like them to be. Being able to build my own settlement is also fun. I spend hours making my house feel like home. The only downside to gameplay is the companion AI. They love to get in your way.
The wasteland and everything in it is savage and beautiful. Not much more to say!
The base game is a ton of fun. If you don't care for mods, definitely get it. I got this at launch and I do care about mods, but regardless the game is still massive fun. Just don't support them by paying for mods and you'll be fine.

As much as I have enjoyed Fallout 4 and the hours I've spent with the game I'm still hard pressed to recommend this game over say, Fallout New Vegas.
In Fallout 4 the graphics have improved, the story although still somewhat bland has still managed to improve in the way it delivers itself to the player. The shooting mechanics are more fluid but at the end of the day it just doesn't feel like a Fallout game. A lot of the quests feel uninspired and copy pasted with no real payoff. However the world itself is stunning, long vistas with plenty of different locales to explore and different characters to meet. Fallout 4 for me is a love hate relationship, lots of aspects have been improved but it is what made previous instalments great, now feel dumbed down or totally removed all together. Nearly everything this game does in terms of world building I feel New Vegas and even Fallout 3 did better. Basically the mechanics of the game have improved massively but the overall feel of the universe is lacking compared to previous versions. Also base building can do one. I prefer being my own person, not  village.
Do yourself a favour and play New Vegas but also play this... I recommend this because it's still Fallout but I also don't recommend this because it's the weakest one out of the bunch in my opinion.

A simple accumulations and scalings game. Find all of the little ways you can increase your income until you're rolling in the sheckles. Effectively free-to-play despite the in-game purchases, courtesy of daily bonus rewards.
Favorite Pro: Diamonds, your main progress-tracking currency, can only be acquired by trading all of your current progress (except for important things like research and achievements).
- The amount you ultimately hold after the trade (regardless of how many you had before) is based on how much progress you traded in.
- The amount you hold amplifies your other incomes.
- You can drop some of the ones you hold (which you essentially gain back next time you trade your progress) to get cool stuff.
Pretty neat mechanic.
Cons:
- The art style is generic and fairly minimalist, and the game is certainly nice enough to suit a more stylish appearance.
- A slightly-too-interesting usage of grammar and commas. I'm that kind of guy.
Overall:
Me likey. I want to see even more features to look forward to spending my Qas, Sps, and Sxds on.

When reading, keep in mind this is not a finished game! I am giving it a thumbs up based on the direction I see it heading and its potential. Never buy an early access game if you want a bug-free, totally polished experience.
That being said, Steam Bandits: Outpost has great potential. It plays a like a mix between Kingdom for Keflings/World of Keflings and Torchlight/TL2, but with a good old fashioned turn-based fighting system. I like real time fighting as much as the next gamer, but it's been a while since I played a game with turn-based fights so it's a fun change.
The art is lovely. The quests (past the tutorial) have a nice sense of humor. In fact, the whole game has a lighthearted feel that I enjoy. The writing, combat, and parts of the UI need some work, and sometimes it feels a little too much like a Zynga game (such as weird wait times for things to complete), but remember, this is still in beta.
For things that need improvement, the dev team is extremely responsive to suggestions and bug reports.
Do get this game if you like town-building and questing, and want to be part of the development process. Your feedback very literally will shape the direction of the game. That's pretty cool.

A pretty interesting game, all things considered, and if you're looking for a good racer to pick up for a couple of hours, I vouch for it.
It's a bad Burnout game, though, and there are a lot of really annoying problems with it. An open world racing game is a cool idea, until the negatives of the open world start to take over.
First off, enjoy all the races that take you out to the middle of nowhere part of the map, which you then need to drive back from in order to start a new event.
Have fun having a great run in a difficult event, before one of the randomly spawning pop-in cars decides that this is the proper time to screw your day.
Nothing beats the amazingly repetitive nature of racing in the same city, over and over and over again, with slightly different routes.
The crash mode, a staple of Burnout games, has been replaced with some kind of weird bounce-your-car-forever crash mode thing.
It isn't a bad game, and it is a fun experiment, but don't expect a lot of real lasting power out of this one. You can use some mod to unlock the 360/PS3 DLC content, but I've never personally bothered doing it. It is a great game to boot up every couple of months and run through some races/events, but the problems with the game overtake the potential for it to really have true lasting power.
Also, there's no real "complete" point beyond 100%, so if you are obsessive about finishing games in your backlog, enjoy this piece of backlog herpes.

Starbound, oh Starbound, how I love thou Starbound.
There's a certain charm in the game from the moment it loads; the soft nature of the soundtrack, the simple character creation that has you flicking between options endlessly to get the perfect character. Each of the races have their own quirks and qualities, from the bird-like Avian to the cowboy/girl Novakids.
The game has developed a fair amount since I bought the game, and this is probably the only place that it falls down, personally. It seems to be taking too long with not enough updates to warrant it, but there IS still quantity here and, more importantly, quality. It's said all too much that this game is not finished, and its not. It doesn't really seem close, either, but I honestly don't believe that matters.
In an age of AAA games that demand £40 for 20 hours worth of content this is a true gem. £12 is nothing, really, for a game that will easily see you reach the 100 hour mark. Mod support increases playability, but really everything needed is already in-game.
Setting off as a new character is much more structured than it used to be, and whilst it starts off slow it is well paced. Mining is addictive, there is no getting away from that, and before long you find yourself at the core and backtracking to the top again (though underground teleporting is now a thing - just not as fun). There is a feeling of emptiness as you fly through systems, but that just adds to the game, the correct sort of atmosphere that makes encountering your own species that much better!
I genuinely believe this game is worth buying, even if it never leaves the Early Access status, you will not forget it!

Crossbow Warrior – The Legend of William Tell:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
The year is 1307, 18th of November, if my memory serves me right. Mr. Tell and his son, Walter, were visiting the stunning village of Altdorf (I have been there and it is a breathtaking place, surrounded by majestic mountains). Tell refused to bow publicly in front of a hat that was positioned on a pole in the market place by Gessler (Vassal of the Austrian Emperor). As punishment, he was arrested and required to shoot an arrow, with his crossbow, through an apple placed upon his son’s head, in order to avoid execution for them both! All I can say is, I am very thankful that I was not born in the 1300’s and that my name wasn’t Walter!
Crossbow Warrior – The Legend of William Tell is a 2d action platformer where you will play the story of this legendary hero from Switzerland. There are 29 challenging levels to beat and you will have to collect a specific number of the beautiful Elderweiss flowers, find the hidden apple (in each level), and to make it even harder, do so within a specific time-frame. And let me William (Tell) you . . . you must be an expert in this genre of game to achieve all of them in the same run! Nah, not possible in the same run!
I like the different type of presentations, some levels will be as your formal side scrolling platformer and some like a speed runner one. Which makes it fun!
Aim with your crossbow carefully so your bolt hits the archery targets to unveil hidden places. Shoot through hidden apples, drop boxes on despicable Harbsburg soldiers, jump on their heads or just shoot them! Face furry and cuddly cute animals, I would like to name one in particular . . . the fluffy bear!
This game has a good and cute style of carton graphics and shows good humour too, for example: chocolate will give you a speed boost and cheese more health (that was in the old days)! . I enjoy the soundtrack, it has an inspiring touch to it. Control-wise, it could be smoother in my opinion. Anyone can play this game but be aware it is quite challenging at times.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Good graphics & soundtrack
-	29 levels to beat
-	Good platformer / Speed runner
-	Fun To play
-	Achievements
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Control could be smoother
-	Can be very challenging at times.
-	No trading cards
7/10

FYI: This is a port of a mobile game.
Crossbow Warrior – The Legend of William Tell is a budget indie game that tells the story of the unlikely hero William Tell’s triumph over a tyrannical emperor. Unfortunately I found the game’s storytelling and gameplay mechanics underwhelming. While the game is no slouch in the audiovisual department these aspects don’t outweigh the fact that Crossbow Warrior is just not that fun to play.
The game opens with a tutorial level to get you acquainted with the basics. This is essentially a side-scrolling platformer with the most basic of combat mechanics and there are actually levels that be completed without defeating any enemies. During the levels you can pick up various items like chocolate bars that make you run faster and flowers that server as collectables, there are also secret areas in some of the levels. The levels are designed to be played multiple times inspiring you to go back to get a better clear time or to collect all of the items. There are a few levels that deviate from this formula like when you must navigate a dangerous river while in a rowboat or endless-runner style levels that have you avoiding obstacles without stopping.
Regardless of the level type they are all held back by the unresponsive and unintuitive platforming. William Tell has no weight to his movements, so I could never get a feel for whether he would land and continue for a few steps or just stop dead in his tracks after a jump. This led me to over and under compensating constantly when landing because it never felt consistent and consistency is paramount in a platformer. There were also many occasions where I would press the jump button, but Tell would not jump he would just continue running into a river… Or an enemy. This led to a very frustrating experience as jumping is a primary mechanic in the game. These imprecise controls carry over into the endless runner style levels where you can’t always tell where you can or can’t walk. This leads to premature jumping that results in landing just shy of your goal. I’ve played many platforms in my time and the platforming in this game just doesn’t feel right. I’m sure it’s possible to reach a point where you could learn the limitations of the system, but nothing about the game inspires you to keep banging your head against the wall until it clicks.
The storytelling amounts to still images with captions underneath them. From what I can tell this is a faithful retelling of the legend of William Tell, but the presentation is very dry. There was a point when I wondered if this was meant as more of an educational tool rather than an actual video game much like Valiant Hearts, but the story bits were so sparse and bare-bones that I can’t see this being used as a teaching tool.
Crossbow Warriors is a very pretty game with a great art-style and fantastic effects. The lighting is top-notch and the weather effects do a great job of making it look like you are in a torrential down-pour. One of my favorite levels tasked you with navigating a river with many hazards while rain poured down obstructing your view; finding hidden items in this level was fun and exciting at the same time. William Tell’s animations are very stiff however and this also affects the gameplay as well as the visual presentation. The audio presentation is also excellent offering appropriate music and sound effects that fit well with the great art-style.
I wish I could recommend Crossbow Warriors – The Legend of William Tell without exceptions. What you get out of this game is very subjective. With the low price point you may be able to overlook the unresponsive controls and lack of storytelling, but I cannot. For me the game just doesn’t play well enough to justify any price point. It is too bad because the concept is great and the presentation is on point, but unfortunately the moment-to-moment gameplay and storytelling drag the the experience down for me and I cannot recommend this game.
