Fans of film directors like Johnnie To, Ringo Lam and John Woo will feel right at home in Sleeping Dogs. You take control of Wei Shen, a Hong Kong native who has just returned home after spending some time in the United States. He is working as an undercover cop under superintendent Thomas Pendrew and his handler Raymond Mak in an effort to take down a powerful Triad gang known as the Sun On Yee. Wei's assignment positions him as a lowly thug under the wing of a 'roided out hothead named Winston Chu and follows his ascension to a prominent figure within the Sun On Yee. Things become complicated however, as the line between undercover cop and criminal blurs. Wei becomes deeply entrenched in the criminal underworld, building friendships with his gang-mates while witnessing signs of corruption within the police force. The yarn spun by Sleeping Dogs is solid enough but it's telling stumbles. Pacing is all over the place, and many important elements seem undercooked. Sleeping dogs has issues integrating plot points into missions and providing build up. For example, Winston has a fiancee that is revealed when you have to run a few errands for her as part of a mission. She softens Winston's image and makes him a little more human but, unfortunately she exits the plot just as abruptly as she shows up making her little more than a tool to develop Winston. Thankfully the finale builds in a satisfying way and there are some sections that are really effective and engaging in the middle portion of the tale. Its just a shame that it couldn't be more consistent and better developed.

Being an undercover cop Wei must straddle the line between right and wrong and missions reflect this. Good guy Wei finds time between running errands for the triad to assist a police inspector with some of her cases. Triad missions are strait forward affairs that usually involve collecting protection money, stealing stuff, beating the hell out of other gang members and maybe shooting a few people. Cop cases play out more like multi-stage quest chains commonly associated with RPGs. Wei also earns experience for both a cop skill tree and a triad skill tree. You earn both types of experience in both mission types but being a public menace and destroying public property or killing civilians will take away from the cop experience you can earn in a mission. Throughout the course of Sleeping Dogs Wei hacks cameras, races, sings karaoke, cracks combination locks, plants bugs, triangulates cellphone calls, bets on♥♥♥♥♥♥fights, plays mahjong poker and picks locks. The game does a great job of mixing these elements up and missions are generally interesting with only a few lame ducks.

All of the aforementioned elements are secondary to the driving, fighting and shooting you will be doing to make your way through the game. The fighting system in this game really shines. Wei relies on strikes, grapples and counters to dispatch his foes. Enemies come in varieties as well, some specialize in strikes and block many of your attacks, grapplers are burly chaps that you want to keep at bay with power strikes, some enemies wield knives and tire irons and later in the game you will find enemies that are really only susceptible to counters. If you want to live in Sleeping Dogs, you will have to prioritize your foes and time your attacks carefully. Your wushu can be supplemented by finding Jade statues that can be returned to the Kung Fu master in the game. These moves are valuable tools and you will find yourself utilizing most of them. They allow you to snap your opponents limbs, deliver powerful blows and disarm your foes. It's a great system and is evolves enough during the course of the game to remain engaging. Driving is similar to other open world games with cars that handle differently based on weight and size. The one unique addition to the driving mechanics is a button that allows you to throw the car sideways by pushing the appropriate button or key and moving in the direction you wish to go. This allows you to ram vehicles that are in hot pursuit of Wei. Motorcycles, scooters and boats are also among the vehicles you will pilot. Shooting is of the cover-based variety and Wei can vault from cover and enter slow motion as well as blind fire. It's solid but the mechanics are not as unique and engaging as the hand to hand combat. In light of this most of the game focuses on hand to hand confrontations.

Sleeping Dogs' interpretation of Hong Kong is an efficiently constructed playground. There is an unusual amount of verticality in this game despite the lack of air vehicles. Wei can climb the ledges and scaffolding around a number of the building and access rooftops. Pedestrian overpasses on the streets also provide access to high places in which numerous collectables are tucked away. Free running is also a part of Sleeping Dogs' bag of tricks. At certain points Wei will have to pursue targets on foot through a gauntlet of barriers and other impediments. These sections involve the player running after them and timing button presses to clear obstacles gracefully, poor timing results in fumbling over an obstacle and loosing ground. The animations for these sections don't flow together as smoothly as those in Assassin's Creed but the extra input required to complete them is a welcome addition that adds a small layer of interactivity in what is usually a passive experience in other games. It's just a shame that the camera is not exactly stellar. It seems to have a knack for being in the wrong place most of the time. Strangely absent is the ability to center the camera with a button press that's so common in third person action games.

On the PC, Sleeping Dogs is a really pleasing game to look at. Square Enix has also made a high resolution texture pack available for those with decent rigs and includes some DX11 features. Hong Kong is wonderfully detailed with neon signs glowing, power lines forming webs overhead, air conditioning fans spinning on the sides of buildings, and plenty of pedestrians and traffic to make the city feel alive. Also, the game wisely uses rain to give everything a nice sheen--as it rains the wet pavement reveals reflections of neon signs and characters appear wet. The handful of interiors are also detailed and pleasing to look at. NPCs are not too detailed and are a little more robotic as a result of a low poly count and the cars are not tremendously detailed but these are technical limitations that are to be expected. The main characters however are richly detailed, making the cutscenes a treat. Skin textures are very detailed and the tattoos that adorn the bodies of the gangsters add quite a bit of character to each of them. You can also customize the clothing that Wei wears and wearing certain combinations of clothing can provide stat benefits. Cloting options are rather varied accounting for both ridiculous looks and strictly business attire.

For a game that was almost canned, Sleeping Dogs is quite impressive. The story fumbles around before ending on a strong note and the camera can be irritating but these faults are offset by great mechanics and strong visuals on the PC. Sleeping Dogs isn't ready to dethrone Grand Theft Auto as the best open world crime game but it's robust mechanics and numerous diversions make it a strong addition to the genre. It appears that Square Enix stuck gold by reviving this dead dog.

Let's get into it.
My first review was an obvious kneejerk reaction, as I liked the game a lot.
It released without a story mode. Said mode is coming very soon. Still, I would never, ever recommend a Street Fighter title at its release pricepoint of 60 dollars solely for the story mode, even if it released with one that provided 800 hours of content. Because it would be a convoluted, incomprehensible mess.
Let's be honest. The reason you're pondering whether or not to buy this game is so you can play Street Fighter with friends and/or people around the world.
Should you buy it if you're into that? It's a tough answer. The fighting is great, the combos are nice and simple but the game still has great depth. It looks pretty, it has crossplay with the PS4, Juri and Urien are gonna be in it, smug Asian-European waifu is playable, and the online can be a wonderful experience.
But it can also be so, soooo bad. If you're patient enough to deal with teleporting Rashids, if you want to train for tournaments, or if you have someone you really want to play it with, then yes, by all means buy it.
The problem is that SFV sells itself on its more basic roots, it tries to appeal to a more casual audience. If you are one of those casuals who's never played a fighter before, I would much rather recommend something like Brawlhalla or Killer Instinct, which offer much more content for a far less ridiculous asking price. KI has a singleplayer mode and the best training mode in any game besides Skullgirls (another game to recommend!).
These games give you vs. AI Single Fight modes. They give you attainable goals, they ask for much less in order to purchase the full gameplay experience. They give good netcode, in-game chat systems, and quick matches. These are all things SFV is severely lacking.
There is another type of casual, though.  If you're the type of guy that tried to get into Ultra but found it too complicated,  has played Mortal Kombat a few times, and has a copy of UMVC3 he plays with friends from time to time, this may be the game that gets you into Fighting Games for good, so long as you discover your inner Dhalsim and control the salt that arises from the game's many issues
Do I recommend it? I wish there was a maybe option. I like it, but it's crystal clear to me why others absolutely despise it. For now, it's recommended with some huge caveats.

I was a big fan of Blitzkrieg 2 when it came out in the mid 2000's. So far, this game was a bit of a dissapointment for me.
Issues
- Not enough people playing online. I waited a very long time during multiple timeslots throughout the day adn wasn't able to get a match. I think the matchmaking system is based on your single player progress since I wasn't able to access the "tier 3" technology and wasn't able to match with people who had that tier unlocked.
- Singleplayer is incredibly difficult. The singleplayer relies on you using your own units. This is problematic since you don't start out with many types of units and there is a cap on what you can use. There's no chance for reinforcements unless you have additional units in your queue. This made the first levels very difficult to play.
- The interface needs some work. I discovered the multiplayer button (titled "Frontline") on the main map by accident. It didn't give any indication of what this button did until I clicked on it. The units in the game pop up icons when something happens to them but there is no way to decipher these icons.
- Blitzkrieg 2 had a nice unit stats window that would appear on the main UI when you clicked the unit. This showed the gun's penetration capabilities, the armor, the HP, and how much damage the gun can do. This one just tells you the armor on the vehicle: it's less intuitive than B2's.
- Performance is subpar considering the graphics quality and the fact that this is a RTS. I encountered lag quite frequently during the singleplayer despite having a GTX 970 and an I5.
I think the "clash of clans" style base assault multiplayer has potential. I will be checking this game out in a future release, but right now I'm not ready for it.

I have beed following this game from update to update since the very begining of this game. With 77 hrs of playing, I have to say that this game was intriguing at first, with the new systems and mechanics that are unique. You have a ship to build, some randomly generated dungeons to conquer, millions of planets to set foot on, which are indeed some cool features of sandbox. However, behind this cool concept the game seems not to be so well executed. First this game currently does not have a well-plotted storyline to follow but a penguin-themed army. The quests are irrelevant as NPCs just ask you to burn your fuel and find stuff. Second, combat is boring, moves are rigid, you do not get much reaction from monsters. Third, upgrading your gears becomes boring as you feel that mining is repetitive after you reach tier 3 gear.
That is why I prefer Terraria. Once the player cannot see the main story, quests do not provide enough feeling of immersion. Plus that the targets players focus on are thrown into this vast ocean of planets, which inevitably prolong your gameplay. And that will result in your exhaustion after hours of playing, and you will find that you are repeating what you have done.
I have read some info in the archive and notice that the developers have actually done a lot in building the background. And the frescoes in that ancient ruin are magnificent too. And that's why I still recommend this game because in the future updates there might be more culture in this game. It is still in early access anyway.
**Edit**
When this game came out of Early Access as Starbound 1.0 I have to admit that this game is fairly complete now. Now we have a proper intro, a main story line, and a lot more cool stuff, which will surely grant another 100+ hours of gameplay if you choose to create a new character as I did. And when you beat the final boss there is still the awesome Frackin Universe mod you can download and try which will give you another 50+ hours of gameplay (if you don't cheat). With the support of steam workshop, this game is good enough.

This game.. it is just epic... I have played both Fallout 3 and New Vegas and I truly deem this game as a worthy addition to the series. It got a lot of things right, and it is just providing me with endless hours of entertainment. You truly get to influence the world around you and create your own settlements or in my case, defensive positions and outposts where I could fall back to should things get a bit too hairy. The ability to craft weapons that fit your play style is also a VERY VERY VERY welcome feature. I could not stress how much I love crafting items, and I am glad Bethesda got rid of the whole weapon maintenance thingy from both FO3 and NV... that is one of the things I dislike about those two aforementioned games.
The DLCs are also amazing, Nuka-World and Far Harbor in particular are both excellent and a cut above the other DLCs in my opinion. However, I do feel the game is missing a few things, particularly classic weapons such as the M16 and the M1 garand like in Fallout NV... Sure there are mods out there that could remedy this problem, but you won't be able to get any achievements with mods enabled and it could corrupt your game files if ever. Hopefully, Bethesda adds these into their new Creator's club, I would surely buy those if I have the opportunity. :)

Muv-Luv Extra is your typical romance harem. Nothing groundbreaking but what it does, it does well. It is coupled with Unlimited you see the trilogy start to distinguish itself and the later Alternative, due later this year, it becomes a masterpiece. In total you may end up with a hundred hours to read all three and the story is well worth it.
The sprite animations from Alternative is a nice addition to the new release. Other than the system shapeups, clear list and new translation; it is the same story as before.
Thoroughly recommended for anyone interested in a great visual novel story, but this is considering the three parts as a whole. While the two parts in this game are both nice on their own, they work best together with the third. If you are worried about the price or losing the threads of the story between now and the coming release of Alternative, feel free to wait a bit. Some may recommend you only read a summary of the these two stories and go for Alternative alone. I encourage you to play through them instead. It is a better way to get to know the characters and the setup for the third cannot be underestimated.
While this is an all-ages version and certain parts have been excluded, a restoration patch is on its way for those wanting the extra scenes. For Extra at least I haven't found their departure detrimental, yet to play through Unlimited.
So fall in love with the characters, enjoy the story and look forward to the coming of Alternative.

Very short game (20 minutes long if you do everything right) with a repetitive and mechanical gameplay.
The game is a straight puzzle, if you mess with some pieces you are  destined to get stuck, waiting for your dead.
The mechanism is simple but very annoying especially if you have to repete the game from the beginning after beeing dead: You can pick up an item and use it only when you have interacted with a specific object or found a clue on a note, also your inventory has a limited number of slots.

For example if i know that to activate object X i need the item Y, first i have to to interact with X or find a note that says something useful about that item and after that i can pick up the item Y, that can be placed very far away. But the big annoying issue is that some objects works only in a specific conditions in a limited amount of time and if you fail one time you risk to scew up the entire game progress.
Also there are multiple ending but this does not make any sense, because you have to do exactly the same operations for the 95% of the game progress, that is very mechanical, it feels like a job routine.
So, if you want, give it a try, the price is very cheap and it works without problems, but the game design doesn't fit very well in my opinion, expecialy for a game that has been designed to easily kill the player.

You drive around doing whatever you want to do; you gain access to better vehicles either by smashing them up on the open road when the game periodically tells you you can do so, or level up your drivers license by winning events accessible at intersections throughout the city.
Or you can just drive around randomly and at a high rate of speed while doing jumps, finding shortcuts and wrecking your car (complete with slowdown matrix-time wrecks, every time; it is awesome!)  Speaking of wrecking there's really no ingame penalty other than losing a little bit of boost (which is easy to get back and is just like your nitro bar).  The game is what you make of it, it can be just a casual drive around the city fast game, or it can be a collect every collectible and get every car game or both.
The city/hillside you drive around in is very well-made to allow you to drive full speed everywhere kinda randomly without having to worry about the map if you just want to chill out and drive fast in a city setting.  That's one of the best things about this game, I think, is how you can just go go go and not have to think about your route.
One negative aspect of the game, unless I'm missing it, is there is no way to set waypoints to places, so I find myself checking the larger map (which pauses the game and sorta breaks the flow of driving) more often than I would prefer. edit: one more thing I dislike is how in-game notifications (not steam notifications) appear right in the middle of the screen; when you're driving fast that's the most important area and it's really stupid to put giant flashy graphic/text banners about things you've done in the game across that entire area for several seconds at a time
Also I don't know why this is called the Ultimate Box, it's just the base game.  You can mod in the DLC, but you can't actually buy it anymore and the game doesn't include it.   Stupid marketing.
Anyway this is years too late to review the game, but if you read this then maybe it gave you an idea of what to expect out of this game.

For the sake of full disclosure I did back this on Kickstarter.  I have completed the Muv-Luv Trilogy, via the unofficial fan translation, twice.
The Steam version of this game is the All Ages version. That means the explicit adult content that is in the normal game is removed or in some cases censored.  There is a Director's Cut patch available.
This review will be as spoiler free as I can make it.  The thing that makes the Muv-Luv experience so memorable is not knowing where it is going to go or what will happen next.  I would hate to ruin that for someone else.
The Muv-Luv Trilogy is considered by many, myself include, to be one of the best Visual Novel experiences of all time and to see it receive an official English release is really exciting.  Muv-Luv's Extra and Unlimited are meant to function as an introduction to the characters and the universe.  Skipping either would be doing yourself a big disservice.  Thankfully boasting improved visuals, much needed engine and UI changes, and of course translation updates, this iteration should offer a fresh experience for both veterans and newcomers.
Discussing the story in Muv-Luv is a very tricky thing to do.  Doubly so when you are trying to avoid spoilers.  Unfortunately one of the biggest twists is proudly displayed on the store page: the genre shift.  I'll be dividing this section it two parts, one for Extra and one for Unlimited.
That is the elevator pitch.  Pretty simple, right?  The story plays out much like you would expect in any standard harem centric romantic comedy.   With a large cast, including Takeru's fellow classmates, teachers, and a whole host of other supporting characters, the story can be really sweet and funny but mostly feels an exercise in absurdity.  On the surface Extra may feel mediocre, especially if you're not new to visual novels.  In reality it is actually a very clever parody and deconstruction of the entire trope filled genre.  The fact that it is stuffed to the brim with subtle foreshadowing only makes it all the better.
The goal of Extra, at least the first time through, is to introduce you to the characters.  There are routes for each of the main girls along with a few common routes.  In the original release you would need to complete both Sumika and Meiya's routes before you could unlock Unlimited.  All other routes were considered optional.  In this release however Unlimited is unlocked from the start.  As a result I would suggest still doing both Sumika and Meiya's routes before moving on to Unlimited as a bare minimum, and ideally doing all the routes.
Extra has a lot to offer but to fully appreciate it you need to know the whole story.  Many suggest replaying Extra after completing Alternative.  I am one of those people.  You don't know just how much you'll miss it.
Welcome to Unlimited.  Hopefully you didn't get whiplash from genre shift.  At this point I don't think any of this is a spoiler, especially since it is proudly displayed on the store page, but for those of us that jumped in to this series all those years ago with no clue what was in store for us this was like flipping the world upside down.  To go from a bog standard romantic comedy to post apocalyptic hard science fiction?  It was jarring.
Where Extra exists as a way to introduce us to the characters Unlimited instead introduces us to the world.  We get a lot of lore and a lot of world building.  The tone for Unlimited is more serious than Extra but still retains some pretty light hearted and goofy moments.
There are a total of six routes in Unlimited, five associated with the main heroines and one "hidden" route.  Despite that the main story is fairly linear.  I personally suggest completing at least Meiya's route along with the "hidden" route (though I'm unsure how that route will work in the All Ages version).  Other routes are once again optional but to get everything out of Alternative that you can, much like Extra, I suggest completing them all.  Unlimited gives you a glimpse of what you've signed up for.  It is the final jumping off point.
Muv-Luv was originally released in 2003 and despite that I think it holds up pretty well darn well.  Not everyone will agree with me, the art direction has been a bit of contentious topic for years, but there is more detail, action, and movement in this series than in most visual novels.  The sprites are very well done and varied, backgrounds look good, the CGs are fantastic, and the handful of movies look just fine.
All of the various improvements, which are based off of the Japanese console releases some years back to my understanding, are welcome and do a good job of bringing Extra and Unlimited up to the same level that Alternative is on.  At the time of writing the only issue I currently have is that because of the process of moving from the original 4:3 aspect ratio to wide screen there has been some zooming in and cropping of CGs.  Thankfully the developers have addressed this issue and made the various CGs scrollable within the gallery.
The best way I can describe the OST is iconic.  Some of the tracks still give me goosebumps.  But, as music is pretty subjective, I'll try not to drone on.
The voice acting is top notch.  Not much else to say.
The original version of Muv-Luv was a prickly beast.  It was old, it was clunky, it didn't play well with a several different OS versions, and the translation could be rough.  Our official release however has none of those problems.  There are some things that I wouldn't mind seeing changed like the limit on the number of saves, bringing back notes, and the ability to customize text colors, but as a whole the experience is a lot better.  Some people have pointed out that the UI is a bit ugly and very reminiscent of a mobile game, but I think it is fine.  The stability improvements and translation updates are the big things and in that regard it delivers.
I love Muv-Luv.  Hopefully you will too.

A Beautiful Day sets itself on a path to make a unique game.  It is an early access survival game, which are absolutely a dime a dozen, but ABD is trying a different route.   It is an MMORTS in the same vain as Age of Empires.   Definitely caught my attention when my friend mentioned it to me yesterday.
The devs are even kind enough to give you a free key if you are a current/former military vet.   I was lucky enough to receive a key, not just because of the dev's generosity (for which I am thankful for) but also it saved me spending $17.99 on this "game."
Truly, early access can be a very useful tool for developers to polish their product and make necessary changes that the player base would like.  However, while the tool is nice, there is a time and a place to utilize it.
Simply put, A Beautiful Day is anything but beautiful for the time being.  It just isn't ready for even early access in my opinion.
You maybe thinking, "you've only played this game for less than an hour.  How does your opinion matter?"  True, very true.  In the first 5 minutes the game has crashed a multiple of times.  Not an issue, bugs pop up with different systems naturally.  It isn't just that though.  The text in the game is extremely low res and hard to read.  The game skips past the starting menu screen and even bypasses your choice for race.  It literally throws you in an empty forest with other players.  All named "Jeff".   I couldn't cut down trees because I didn't have an axe and I couldn't attack players because I didn't have a weapon.  I couldn't interact with the interaction box nor read anything for the resource bar.  I could just right click move around at other Jeffs and listen to the very loud music/footsteps (hit escape and the game closes and the menu button doesn't do anything.)
Normally, I would write this game off as a complete sham but the developers are nice and do seem to want to make a solid game.   They had stated that they will be patching the game quite a lot so let's see if they can turn this around.
I will give the developers the benefit of the doubt and check on the game and progress if it is made I will reevaluate my review and recommend it if it is fun and playable.   For now?  Don't spend your money.
Edit: 8/17/15-  A couple of patches have been put out.  I can now choose what race I want to play as but unfortunately can't move.    Still, the devs seem to be working on fixing the issues.  Will keep this updated :)

This is a bare-bones review. I don't care whose feelings I hurt, I'm going to keep it raw. I finally started to write a review of this after months of first playing it, but wasn't able to finish it, so I had to start over. Nevertheless, I would 100% recommend this game. Town of Salem is probably the funnest game I've got to know about from Steam. I've played this game more than any other. Obviously, the reason why Steam only recorded me playing it for a little over an hour on its app is because I followed the advice of many reviewers at the time who recommended the browser version of the game on BlankMediaGames' site.
Some of my most interesting achievements in the game include:
-Win 100 games of Town of Salem
-Win 25 games as a doctor
-Win 25 games as an escort
-Win 25 games as an investigator
-Win 25 games as a jailor
-Win 25 games as a lookout
-Win 25 games as a medium
-Win 25 games as a sheriff
-Win 25 games as a mafioso
-Win with all of the mafia members still alive
-Win with all town members still alive
-Be acquitted by a tie vote
-Be acquitted without revealing to the Town (that I was mayor)
-Save 3 people in one game (as a doctor)
-Get your target lynched on day 2 (as executioner)
So as you can tell, I've spent a lot of time playing this game.
Now the negative aspects of the game:
-Developers have got to buff mafia. Town almost always wins. And with a combination of town winning more often, and the mafia roles being boring, it's gotten so bad in ranked mode that it's common for those chosen to play mafia roles to leave the game immediately because they don't want to be mafia.
My suggestion: Put 4 mafia instead of 3 in ranked. Add to that Mafioso needs to be able to control who he kills. So if both the Mafioso and GF pick a target, the Mafioso (since he's the one going out) should get precedent on who he kills. Nobody likes GF taking over. Give GF another responsibility. It could be something like every 2 days, GF sends a threat to somebody, paralyzing them and making them stay at home for one night/rbing them. GF, because he's an important figure, can be like the queen in Chess where they combine both the rook and bishop. In this case, the GF can rb and still kill. That would make these mafia roles more enticing.
-Arsonist needs to be buffed (there's a reason why his win-rate is the lowest in the game-and if you think I'm pulling this out of my♥♥♥♥♥ know that this came from the developers themselves).
My suggestion: There are various ways to buff the arsonist, my suggestion was simple: Giving him the ability to ignite every three days in addition to dousing somebody. For example: night 1, douse, night 2, douse, night 3, douse and ignite. The arsonist wouldn't be limited to only igniting every three nights, he would still be able to ignite any night he wanted to, it's just the third night would be a bonus. That's a simple solution.
-Huge announcement was a DISAPPOINTMENT. They made a huge announcement complete with a countdown and some graphics on their website. People were speculating on what it was, I thought they finally took my suggestions of buffing certain roles. The announcement was...drum roll please...THEY MADE A BOARD GAME OF THE GAME. BOO! A lot of us in the community were disappointed as hell.
Overall, this game is fun as hell, probably the funnest game I've played from finding it on Steam. My many hours and games playing it vouch for it. I even supported the developers by paying for the game on here even though the browser version is free.
A quality ridden sandbox game in the same vain as GTA IV and SR The Third and is well worth your time.

Do you like Street Fighter?
Do you want to play Street Fighter?
Do you want to be part of the Fighting Game Community (FGC)?
Do you treat fighting games like a sport (in both playing/watching)?
Do names like Infiltration, Tokido, Momochi, PRBalrog, FChamp, etc. mean anything to you?
Do you know what a Capcom Pro Tour is?
Do you plan on attending or watching EVO this year?
If you answered yes to any of these questions... then buy this game. If you answered yes to two or more of these questions, you probably already OWN this game.
If don't know or care about any of that stuff, and just want a game to play against the computer, there are a bunch of other fighting games available to you, this is not the one you're looking for.
That being said, this game is good. It's probably the best fundamental-gameplay Street Fighter since Third Strike and has done away with all the nonsense that Ultra Street Fighter IV brought into play.
I recommend this game highly... because I don't care about things like "story mode" or "arcade mode." If you DO care about those things, there are other fighting games available to you. I, however, care about great core gameplay. Street Fighter V has that in spades, and it will only get better.

People have a right to be upset with the state of the game WHEN it launched...
The main problem was that it was lacking in A LOT of content, and honestly even I (who is a huge fan of the franchise) could not stomach the AAA price point when it was released. And to make matters worse, MOST people didn't even know that the game was going to be so bare bones at launch, only for content to be regularly patched in over the next coming months. Thusly creating a whirling dervish of negative reviews and passionate fans that felt cheated by the very thing they loved most... Street Fighter.
But that was then... and this is today. The current state of the game is amazing and only getting better. Match making isn't perfect... but it's MUCH better than it used to be, and the roster is solid as hell and only growing month by month...
I can not stress this enough... this is THE BEST. THE TOP TIER FIGHTING GAME OUT THERE. PERIOD. The amount of depth to the game is mindblowing... and I have completely lost any spare time to constantly thinking about moves, techniques and tactics every single day... and I'm only practicing with ONE character.
If you love fighting games... get this now... and welcome. If you're on the fence... then hell just buy it, try it out, see how it feels... if you dont like it, you can always return it within 2 hours of play time or a couple of weeks (which ever comes first as per Steams refund policy).
The game is in a GREAT state right now, and only getting better, and the community surrounding the game and professional scene is sensational.
Don't get me wrong... there IS stuff to complain about still, I understand this. BUT, there is no way that this game's current few short comings over shadow how fantastic and deep a fighting game this is.
Whiners and much of the negativity surrounding the game is really no longer justified. Grow the ♥♥♥♥ up, and enjoy the fantastic game that is Street Fighter V. See you online <3

tl;dr: Good title, becomes excellent when combined with its sequel, Alternative, which is not yet released.
Ignore the play time, I've read the series before this Steam release.
First things first: if you plan to read the entire series (or even just Alternative), go in as blind as you can for the best experience. DON'T google search, DON'T search Youtube, DON'T go to wikis, as these are all places where you will likely encounter spoilers in some fashion. Even if you don't run into a spoiler directly, any site with comments has a high potential of *that guy* who likes to spoil things because he wants to be a♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥
Muv-luv is a highly acclaimed series of Visual Novels, much of which is focused on Alternative, the third part of the trilogy which has not yet been released. This title contains the first two parts, Extra and Unlimited, which I believe are essential to the experience. While Alternative is where the rollercoaster is most thrilling, the climb up provided by the two parts in this title enhance the experience, and in my opinion, are pretty good themselves.
Extra is the first part of the trilogy, and it is a fairly standard Slice of Life High School Romcom. It establishes many of the important characters in the series, and has some foreshadowing of future events. Its most important role is to establish emotional connections between you and the characters in a carefree environment. If you find this part unbearable, the main route(s) to read for plot are Sumika's and/or Meiya's. These two routes are largely the same, except for the ending, and completing these two were originally required before unlocking Unlimited. The other routes obviously delve more in-depth with the other heroines, and also introduce a few side characters who pop up later, but are not necessary to the main story.
Unlimited is the second part; in this Steam version, it is unlocked from the start, but I would highly recommend reading at least one of Sumika/Meiya in Extra before reading Unlimited. The genre shift from Extra to Unlimited was originally a surprise, but over time it has become rather well known, and even a selling point for the franchise. It is spoiled in the preview video, but I can't blame them when the part of the franchise that most people think of is after the genre shift. Most of the side stories and spinoff VN titles are concerned with either Unlimited or Alternative, and the world most think of when talking about Muv-luv is introduced in Unlimited. The routes in Unlimited are nearly identical, save for a couple unique romance scenes; completing any character's route is more or less the same as finishing any other, though each route has the same two variations of endings. If you don't have a favorite character to choose at this point, Meiya's route is probably the best option story-wise. Unlimited has a significant amount of world-building; some find it tedious, others fascinating. I fall in the latter camp, but regardless, understanding the world established in Unlimited is important for understanding Unlimited and, ultimately, Alternative. Let's just say the ending is rather...abrupt.
Much of the hype understandably goes towards Alternative, but I would still recommend buying this title as well. I found Extra more tolerable that others, it seems, and found Unlimited quite enjoyable. On its own, I might recommend waiting for a deal before purchase, but upon finishing Alternative, I believe buying both titles at full price is well worth the cost. There is some debate whether it's worth buying something when you only experience an enhanced payoff in a later title, but I would recommend getting both. Having some time between the releases is useful in a couple ways; it gives you time to digest what happened in Extra and especially Unlimited before diving back into the world with Alternative, and if you find Extra or Unlimited tedious, there's plenty of time to get through it before Alternative arrives.

So yes, play/read this. And then prepare to have your mind blown when Alternative gets released.

The game is interisting, the pixel art is really good, but it's poorly executed.
Basically, I can point two major flaws:
1) As a pont-and-click adventure, you have to get items to interact with your surroundings and solve the puzzles. It's fine and dandy. But in order to get said items, you have to know that you need them. For example, you have to break a wall, you need a sledgehammer; until you know that you have to break the wall, you can't pick the sledgehammer even if you find it. It makes sense for a number of reasons (people don't stuff themselves with random items and from a gameplay point of view it prevents players from using the knowledge from previous playthroughs to directly going to the item), but it's very rigid and sometimes even ridicolous. It also makes very difficult to understand what are you gonna need for your quest and what's just a background element, since it's not always based on common sense and you have to follow the exact mental track of the developers. Furthermore, it keeps making you go back and forth, stretching the limited game setting with tedious backtracking... There's a total lack of level design here
2) For the horror part, you have to keep your heart rate low, balancing items to relax yourselves with the scares you'll get while exploring. However, some of them are fixed (you can't avoid getting an increase in the heart rate because you need to do a specific action, kinda unfair for the player), some of them happen randomly based on RNG elements... Some of them can be avoided (for example, avoid a certain spot, but it's all knowledge from previous playthroughs), but other seem to have no rhyme or reason. You just get them. And since you can die from them, it's really frustrating when you get them in chain just because. Maybe I'm the one that can't find a way to avoid them, but even then it's all about getting in the developers mind scheme since it's not intuitive. So yeah, you can die despite your best efforts and be forced to replay the whole 'back and forth to get items in the correct order' riveting game mechanic. Also, it's hardly to be scared from pixel art, the scare jump effect is quickly neutralized
So yeah, there's some good in this game, but it's ruined from major gameplay flaws that makes it annoying and frustrating. It would have been better if it were more a story than a game (no heart rate mechanic, for example), just following the clues and leave to the player the fact of being scared.
It's not terrible, but it fails in being truly enjoyable. There are worst ways to spend 3 dollars, for its price it's still quite good, but its flaws are big and penalize the gaming experience

DISCLAIMER: My first review on Steam and is simply my ramblings and praises for the game series. This is not a critical or professional review and will try to be spoiler free. I have personally backed and funded this visual novel on Kickstarter and have read the series when it was first released.
After 13 long years and a with an astoundingly successful $1.2 million dollar Kickstarter, the first of most highly acclaimed adult visual novel series arrives to the west in English and on Steam!
Muv-Luv (pronounced Mabu Ravu) is comprised of three parts: Extra, Unlimited and Alternative (the 3rd which will be released in English on Steam later by the end of 2016). Muv Luv (originally released in 2003) begins as a simple highschool slice of life romantic comedy that slowly evolves into a post apocalyptic science fiction mecha story of survival. If you can look past the quirky character designs and well-aged old art style (the game series being more than 10 years old) Muv-Luv can be charming and an enjoyable read on its own.
As an enthusiast of Japanese Otaku subculture, I can say that Extra/Unlimited will probably at first read and appear as mediocre, average, or even perhaps boring to anyone that has had previous experience with all the various anime/manga or visual novel mediums out there. However, do not be fooled by Extra/Unlimited's cheerful, laid back and moe filled story line. Although it appears innocently dumb, a plethora of allusions, foreshadowing and subtle hints litter the first hour of the story and onward, which when looked back upon when one completes the series, will amaze you. You can even say that the entire narrative of the first two games were confidently written in preparation for the final game in the trilogy.
Extra can be seen as introducing the characters and relationships, while Unlimited shows you the world and background for the grand finale which is Alternative. Extra will bring you laughter and joy and Unlimited will bring you sadness and hope. Essentially, Extra and Unlimited lay the foundation that leads to one of the most highly acclaimed visual novel of all time. It is well worth the read to to get there and is an absolute requirement in understanding the characters and its story.
The Muv-Luv series is one that is near and dear to my heart. An exceptional experience that I will never forget. A story of unique quality that is rarely written once a decade. One of the few visual novel series that I'd wholeheartedly recommend to anyone that is a fan of romance/comedy, mecha and science fiction. Lighthearted, goofy, and sweet... Muv-Luv Extra is like any other generic romantic comedy visual novel out there, while Muv-Luv Unlimited introduces a unique sci-fi genre twist. The appreciation of their value and beauty can only be truly seen once one reaches the Alternative.

All roles have certain attributes.
A big part of the game is figuring out "who is who", friend or enemy, who needs to be protected or who needs to be executed.
During the day there will be a chance of having a public trial and lynching one player, if enough players Vote for it.
At night, there are loads of ways to get killed...
Will you become a Town Folk, a Mobster or the Serial Killer?
The Serial Killer wins if all the Town Folks die.
At night, the Serial Killer can visit another player and kill them.
The Maffia (3-4 players) wins if all the Town Folks die.
There are several roles within the maffia such as God Father, Framer, Mafioso..
The Town (7-9 players) wins if the Serial Killer and the Maffia dies.
There are a lot of roles within the town such as Mayor, Sheriff, Jailor, Medium, Body Guard, Doctor, Transporter, Spy, Investigator, Vigilante, Lookout...
Then we have a few "Neutral" roles, who win with either side - as long as they complete their mission.
Jester - Wins by getting lynched in the public trial. As dead, the Jester can kill one of the players who voted "guilty" and had him killed.
Executioner - Wins by having their Target (chosen at random) lynched in the public trial. If their target however dies during the night, the Executioner becomes a Jester.

[bFinally a Clicker Heroes competitor that shows promise[/b]
Having played Clicker Heroes for ages and ages, and sadly not being able to find anything to compare, I'm blown away by this game.
I've yet to see if it holds up the the thousands of hours I've put into Clicker Heroes, but I can certainly say that it has kept my attention for the hours I've already played it.
One of the biggest problems with clicker games is that, unless the dev really understands the need for multiple upgrade systems, these games often fail to last more than a few thousand clicks. Midas Gold Plus is so deep with restart systems, leveling up of skills and characters, raids, bonuses, boosts, etc, that it just pleases the player, left right and center.
I've been at the computer for a pretty lengthy time, already today, just leveling up stats, buying upgrades, and watching the gold come flying in. Even better, when I'm out and about, I am actually excited to come back and see what my idle time has unlocked and opened in the game. The fact is, the feedback loop of this game is extremely intelligent in that it rewards the player in very positive ways.
As you play the game, you begin to unlock advisors which have bonuses that you can use during your play. In the beginning, there are two, one rewards you with bonuses for clicking, one rewards you with idle bonuses. Later in the game (I've yet to unlock more) there are advisors with even stranger skill sets. You can change your advisor on the fly, so if you're at the computer, select the guy with skills that reqard clicking, if you go out, select the one who rewards idle time.
It's painless and easy to switch advisors, and each time you switch, you have a bunch of new bonuses and boosts to use your money on to upgrade.
This game is free. Simply put, even without paying a single penny, you'll enjoy this game if you enjoy clicker games. It's simply just perfectly thought out, very rewarding, and progresses at a wonderful pace, whether you pay real money or not.
Additionally, if you DO decide to pay real money, the packages are very fairly priced, and the "Hot Deals" packages are fantastic bonuses that supercharge the gameplay from the get-go.
If you are a fan of clicker games, and you are on the fence about this game, take it from me. It's well designed, rewarding, deep as the sea, and fantastic fun.

Street Fighter V is a game with a godawful launch. However, Capcom is finally getting their crap together, and releasing multiple things at once. Starting July 1, this game will be the complete package everyone has been waiting for. I also have faith that Capcom's community managers are finally understanding the importance of communication with their consumers. They say they are dedicated to long term support for this game, and I believe them there. Alright, for the review
The good: Balanced gameplay, all characters feel fun and unique enough to try. Combos are not super difficult, learning each characters quirks is fun. Battle lounges are finally working well (where I spend ALL my sfv time). Story mode and 2 characters are dropping July 1!
The bad: Matchmaking has improved with a couple patches, but is still not perfect. Rollback netcode still needs a lot of work, matches can be almost unplayable with people less than a 5 bar connection, and even then nothing is guaranteed. Ranked is hard, because if you care about your points (I personally do not) you will get frustrated with rage quitters and dropped connections.  Another bummer is that you cannot search for matches by location, leading to some less than desirable connections.
Verdict: If you care about your online rank, this game might not be for you, but if youre waiting for the complete package people have been wanting, get this on sale from the summer sale after July 1, you shouldnt be disappointed.
November Edit: After Season 1 is complete I can say that things have improved, new characters are fantastic, and things are looking up as far as updates go. Capcom has said they are committing themselves to the longterm health of the game, which is a nice( hopefully not empty) promise.

The only downside to the competitive play is that there are quite a few people that ragequit before they lose to preserve their LP (league points), which seems like it would be easily fixed. Low priority matchmaking or loss of LP could easily be implemented, but I'm not sure what Capcom's stance on this is, as SF4 never had anything in place to prevent people from ragequitting. Still the multiplayer experience is enjoyable despite the ragequitters, as I only encounter one out of every 10 opponents or so.

I have beed following this game from update to update since the very begining of this game. With 77 hrs of playing, I have to say that this game was intriguing at first, with the new systems and mechanics that are unique. You have a ship to build, some randomly generated dungeons to conquer, millions of planets to set foot on, which are indeed some cool features of sandbox. However, behind this cool concept the game seems not to be so well executed. First this game currently does not have a well-plotted storyline to follow but a penguin-themed army. The quests are irrelevant as NPCs just ask you to burn your fuel and find stuff. Second, combat is boring, moves are rigid, you do not get much reaction from monsters. Third, upgrading your gears becomes boring as you feel that mining is repetitive after you reach tier 3 gear.
That is why I prefer Terraria. Once the player cannot see the main story, quests do not provide enough feeling of immersion. Plus that the targets players focus on are thrown into this vast ocean of planets, which inevitably prolong your gameplay. And that will result in your exhaustion after hours of playing, and you will find that you are repeating what you have done.
I have read some info in the archive and notice that the developers have actually done a lot in building the background. And the frescoes in that ancient ruin are magnificent too. And that's why I still recommend this game because in the future updates there might be more culture in this game. It is still in early access anyway.
**Edit**
When this game came out of Early Access as Starbound 1.0 I have to admit that this game is fairly complete now. Now we have a proper intro, a main story line, and a lot more cool stuff, which will surely grant another 100+ hours of gameplay if you choose to create a new character as I did. And when you beat the final boss there is still the awesome Frackin Universe mod you can download and try which will give you another 50+ hours of gameplay (if you don't cheat). With the support of steam workshop, this game is good enough.

Great oldschool realtime strategy game.  WW2 subject matter has been beautifully addressed with a serious tone throughout and a focus on squad tactics.  A overworld map is shown during mission selection and loading screens that could possibly mean there will be branching missions and even more exciting, strategic decisions and maybe turn-based modes implemented?  One could only hope.
Supposedly multiplayer modes in as well though mostly a SP and AI skirmish player here.
Will comment or change / update review if impressions change.
UPDATE:
Now out of early access, in my opinion way too soon.  I don't blame Nival since they did an excellent(IMHO) job on the earlier games, especially Blitzkrieg 2.  However this new game tries and fails in too many directions - SP and MP are both lacking and feel empty because of the resources seemingly stretched too thin.  The game is always-online as well, a downer to oldschool strategy gamers not comfortable or just OK with the idea of the game 'phoning home' constantly, when even playing through the campaign.  The game does not even load without an internet connection.  Sadly also the campaign seems to be a bunch of skirmish maps bound together by nothing more than the newly designed globe interface.  While the posibility to choose missions, and even switch sides mid-game is welcome, any sort of cutscenes or even historical narrative would tie each objective together much more.  And this is why the game feels built from the ground up for MP, but while some co-op or colloborative mission types would feel right at home, all I discern is the basic capture the points gameplay which is way overdone in the genre of RTS and especially modern indie-ish titles trying to stand out like Blitzkrieg 3.
Unfortunately have to change from recommended to not recommended in light of more recent gameplay, post early access.

A black sheep of Blitzkrieg franchise.
I was expecting Nival to produce a further evolution on the epic Blitzkrieg 2, which shouldn't be too difficult, but now it seems more like a degeneration than an evolution. Many features already present on Blitzkrieg 2 are missing in 3. You cannot rotate camera with your mouse, you cannot control midair aircrafts, you cannot replenish ammo and HP, and more intolerably, YOU CANNOT SAVE OR LOAD YOUR GAME, one wrong move and you have to start over from the very beginning, yes. Instead they added some useless features, such as "capture the house" key for the infantry, which I have absolutely no idea what meaning it has.
Speaking of campaign, it is UTTERLY USER UNFRIENDLY, partly due to the game mechanics. The walkthrough of a single mission is very long. It is especially frustrating when you cannot save your progress (imagine you just lost your only tank and you can not load game). Also, the campaign is unbelievably DIFFICULT, DULL and severly RUSSIAN BIASED. Russian infantry can wipe out German counterparts for breakfast without a scratch (in 1941!). BT-5 can one shot a B1 frontally whereas latter takes more than 3 minutes to do so. And you have no reserves while AIs do. I highly suspect whether gamemakers themselves can clear the campaign or not.
The multiplayer is dull as well. The player matching is long and not based on any parameter like skill, the map is way too small and predictable, the game mode is lacking (only defensive and offensive). I don't want to continue, you name it.
Overall, it's a very disappointing experience and I can tell the devs are not enthusiastic about this game for a single moment. Maybe they shouldn't make a sequel of Blitzkrieg 2 at all. A legend is better kept than ruined.

I'm sure many people at one point have desired a standalone game focused solely on good naval combat, and Blackwake scratches that itch very well. The game does a good job portraying how it feels like to be sailing on your very own ship. Everything from fixing sails/holes, pumping water, putting out fires, firing cannons, and navigating the seas require your crew to work as a cohesive unit. Every ship will require one person to be the captain (decided by a vote) who steers the ship and commands his/her crew via voice chat.
There's also more to this game than just firing cannons. You can fire grapples at the enemy and board them to engage in direct combat with your muskets and rapiers. Guns can insta-kill you but the game balances this out by making its reload time painfully long. They've also added islands and small forts where you can capture booty but I haven't enjoyed it very much.
Map diversity also changes how you play each game. Sometimes you're spawned into a map with lots of small islands, making it easy to seek cover from cannonfire. Sometimes your crew will have to navigate around glaciers to avoid sinking, and sometimes you'll be busy trying to escape from a water vortex.
As to be expected, there will be people who actively try to ruin games, but I've only encountered one in my ~15 hours of gameplay. You do require 7 peoples' votes to kick someone out of the server and this system is exploitable if a group of people decides to gang up on an individual. I've heard few instances of this happening, although I myself have never experienced this. Thankfully, there always around 5 or more servers to join.
The game can unfortunately be repetitive. Your experience can be very easily ruined by an incompetent or serious captain. While the map diversity is nice, the core pattern of "find ship, fire cannon, reload, fix holes" pattern can be tiring. The game could always use more diversity. More shots like chain shot or heated shot,different cannons, different ships, and even more game modes could enhance immersion and replayability value.
The playerbase isn't tiny for a new game but there's only a handful of servers with people in it. Otherwise, it has great potential and already has very good content. I am not terribly worried as the developers are receptive to feedback and are already addressing several of these issues. This is the one early access game I do not regret purchasing.

1. The streamlining of systems such as the leveling, where you can obtain small upgrades instead of interesting abilities. Some abilities NOONE uses, and if anyone does it's for a special thing that isn't probably serious.

4. The factions are just meh. The minutemen are the only decent enough people but those damn settlements are always in need of help and let me bring on #5.

-Is it a bad game? Far from it. I'd say it's a good game by itself.
-Is it a good RPG? I'm not so sure.
-Is it a good Fallout game? I don't think so. I just can't recommend this game because of these issues. If you're looking for a good fallout game i would say look elsewhere for a similar game, but go and get if you're looking for a good game itself.

Muv Luv is one of my favorite japanese franchises. This game currently spans the first two parts (Extra and Unlimited) of the main trilogy, with the third and arguably best part (Alternative) on the way. Without spoiling this game, I can only say that I love the way it subverts several classic VN, light novel, manga, and anime genres. Extra starts off as your stereotypical harem VN, and gradually leads you down the rabbit hole. The characters, outwardly cliche VN archetypes, gradually develop into unique and compelling personae. Extra exists to attach you to the characters, and while there are a few pacing issues, its more than entertaining enough to get you to put the time in to learn about the characters and setting. Unlimited introduces you to the real meat of the muv-luv universe. You really want to avoid spoiling yourself on this, so all I'll say is that Unlimited introduces a magnificent twist to the drama, putting the characters you grow to love in Extra into an entirely new light, and setting the stage for the  âge-soft's magnum opus, Muv-Luv Alternative. There's a reason why MLA is ranked the highest rated VN of all time.

Sleeping Dogs is a great game that is not without its flaws but has won a place in my heart nonetheless. Once you get past the stunning visuals, you are met with an immersive underworld set in Hong Kong where an undercover officer climbs the ranks of the triads while being forced to consider his own loyalties.
Unlike other games in the genre, the combat is primarily focused on the melee aspect. Officer Shen is a very competent martial artist, and learns more moves and improves the ones he knows as the game progresses. The system feels fresh at the game's onset, but by the game's finish, it loses some of its charm. It is very visually pleasing, but from a gameplay point of view, it is very easy to master the moveset and dominate enemies under all circumstances. This does, however, propagate the sensation of being the invincible hero of the traditional asian fighting movies from which Sleeping Dogs no doubt has drawn significant amounts of inspiration.
Story-wise, the atmoshpere is great. Being in Hong Kong, people speak both English and Chinese, and you often hear the two intertwined. One of the most unusal parts was, in fact, getting used to driving primarily on the left side of the road.
You are met with a good deal of characters, some memorable even after one encounter, but many of them are unfortunately flat. This is due mostly to having too little exposure to each of them, the average being two missions for each character - one where you meet them, and one where you do them a favor of some sort. Most benefitted from interesting missions, but there were a few cases in which I felt I'd wasted my time. This deficit applies primarily to the side missions. It is worth noting that some of the side missions fall into extremes; some were very humorous and/or interesting, and some were excruciatingly boring.
Racing constitutes a major side activity, and it is decently implemented for a game that focuses on other aspects. You can purchase cars and use them in races, many of which take you through challenging routes. I often felt myself remembering the feeling I had playing Need For Speed Underground while playing through the races in the game. (It's a good feeling)
For the primary missions, the cast is built out of stereotypes, but they play their parts well and the story itself, while having some cliche elements, is pleasurable to go through and does have a few unexpected twists. Since you are a police officer in parallel to being a triad member, this opens up a series of circumstances that were especially pleasing to see playing out. The main character is also very likeable, being a smooth talker when the need arises. There are a few moments that are absolutely impossible, such as surviving a shotgun blast in close range or taking down dozens of triad cars on the street like it's nothing, but those can be forgiven since Sleeping Dogs is an action game.
The most irksome parts were getting around and going after collectibles. Getting around was immersive at first - you got to see the nooks and crannies of Hong Kong, and there were plenty of very well-detailed areas to enjoy. However, as you progress later into the game, you find yourself constantly wanting to be on the other side of the map, and with often no taxis in sight, the drive that can take several minutes gets tiring. An especially brutal offender was the naval part: getting on or off boats was extremely tiresome, primarily because of invisible walls that made it very hard to transition between sea and land.
The collectibles became annoying to deal with because many of them were placed in impossibly hard to reach positions that took ages to scout out for possible entry points. Also, you are heavily coerced into going after two of the three types of collectibles, as you need them to improve your fighting skills and health pool, both of which can pose a serious problem in the later parts of the game if ignored.
Finally, I'd like to mention the game's soundtrack. As is usual with such games, there are a number of radio stations, each catering to a different taste. I found myself enjoying several stations personally, and the commentary and advertisements between tracks were well-done and immersive.
This sums up how I feel about the game, having just finished it less than an hour ago. I mention the game's shortcomings a lot because those made the experience less enjoyable, but it was definitely a game I enjoyed overall and would recommend to others. It compensates well for what it lacks through solid mechanics, a virtual Hong Kong teeming with detail and a plot that manages to keep the player engaged from start to finish.

Left 4 Dead is a spectacular first person cooperative shooter, and it's largely given rise to the massive coop and party game focused generation we have right now. Before Left 4 Dead the only major coop exclusive games were mods like Sven Co-Op
However, as much as I liked Left 4 Dead it was an imperfect game that was only improved upon gradually through patches and DLC. One of the features that makes Left 4 Dead and it's successor interesting is the AI Director. Valve must have realized Left 4 Dead would be exclusively a rental unless they spiced things up to the player. What the AI Director does is decide where zombies and items in the world are depending on the player's progress and how well they work together. Every time you play the game it is completely different, especially depending on who you play with.
The biggest factor to buying Left 4 Dead is wether or not to purchase the second instead. I believe the campaigns from L4D1 have already been ported to L4D2. As a result Left 4 Dead remains just a curious bit of history and only a purchase if your not a big fan of Valve's big budget changes with L4D2.

I sincerely can't understand why everyone is complaining about this game. I just bought it for fourty dollars and already played about five hours, enjoying every second of it. If you're on the fence about it, let me put your worries to rest.
First of all, knowing that SFV will continue to get attention, polish, and content in the future makes me feel like this was a great investment. The characters are all different and interesting to play, the music is awesome, and the game looks absolutley gorgeous at max settings. On the topic of input lag, it's true that it plays a little differently from USF4 but if I could adapt in a matter of ten minutes, then anyone else can; not to mention once you get a feel for the game, it controls like a dream. The V-System is great and the combat feels the best it has for a long time. First I have to say fallout is far and away my favorite franchise. With the exception of 4 and BOS for play station I have finished every fallout title to every ending. It pains me write a negative review on this game and I do so only in the hopes that an appeal like mine reaches the ears of those who can make decisions of future content.
The Good
NO PURE EVIL: Fallout has a long standing tradition if making even the most evil factions have at least some silver lining or ideology that is hard to disagree with. The master in FO1 was trying to unify the mutants and create a race immune to the ravages of radiation, The Enclave is on a quest to rebuild a nation where people are safe, even Caesars Legion can say that it's trade roads are some of the safest in the former commonwealth. And FO4 has done a pretty impressive job continuing that trend. Even a faction you hate you can still see their point.
IT SURE IS PRETTY: admittedly most of this can be choked up to general advancements of technology but I wont pretend the game isn't gorgeous.
THE CRAFTING SYSTEM: admittedly I ended up spending half of my carry weight stealing everything not nailed down in every building I came across but it was a really in depth system and it really deserves recognition.
REALLY HIGH LEVEL CAP: I like that you can potentially make an amazing character with all good stats a character that can do everything is a character that can do anything.
The Bad
TINY ROGUES GALLERY: almost everything you face falls into 8 catagories, Robots, Bugs, Humans, Mirelurks, Synths, Animals, Mutants and Deathclaws. But out of all of these categories the only ones that really have verity are Humans, and Robots. And Mirelurks and bugs, they had a verity of tactics, weapons, and challenges. Everything else was just re-skinned versions of the same. A glowing Deathclaw with spikes rushes you and slashes you up same as every single other Deathclaw a Legendary Synth shoots you same as every single other Synth. I think as gamers we can demand a bit more than what they in 1987 with Final Fantasy. Actually Final Fantasy did it better at least in Final Fantasy even though the enemies where just different color in the picture they at least had different abilities.
NO REAL OPTIONS: Another long standing tradition of Fallout is having a lot of ways to solve a quest chain, but I gotta be honest FO4 never really delivered on this it seams like every major quest chain could only be solved in a very clear pattern usually kill this dude. And every single repeating quest was go to X place and kill Y number of Z dudes.
NO REAL IMPACT: nothing like clearing out the a radar station full of raiders for the Minute Men to immediately go right back there and kill a bunch of raiders for the Railroad only to go right back there to clear out still more raiders for the Brotherhood the population of Boston right now 673K and change without nukes and monsters running around everywhere and I feel like I killed at least that many raiders along between a clothing shop, a hardware store, and a Radar station.
NO REAL CITIES: a city is more than a set of markets it has interesting people with different quests, agendas, and back stories, by my count FO4 had 3 towns, the Institute, Diamond City, and Goodneighbor. And even then honestly the Institute and  Goodneighbor where a bit weak. In stead we built our own cities.
LEANNING WAY TO HEAVY ON SETTLEMENTS: settlements where made more or less to replace towns and the game leaned way too heavily on them. Ever 10 feet I came across another one of these things. It actually wouldn't be so bad if the settlers where anything but robots. Actually after the DLC came out I started just building settlements of nothing but robots. Who cares the game sure didn't and they had just as much personal ambition, back story or interest. The only settlement that is interesting to build is the first one and that is largely because of the tutorial how to build a settlement quests at least gave you something to do.
WHERE IS THE SILLY?:Maybe it is just me but FO4 took itself way way too seriously. I think the height of its humor probably peaked at FO2 with at least 4 Monty Python references and many subtle things the background. But it felt to me like FO4 didn't really have any references to anything other than  other Fallout games at this point. With the exception of some quest titles.
The Ugly
PATHETIC DLCs: at least 3 of the DLCs where so small they could only be considered mods. Just a bunch of settlement addons half of which really should have been there from the beginning the other half really never needed to be there at all. All of which the mod community could have done better. These where obvious cash grabs and the sooner we drag that kind of practice into the cold light of day the better.
HIGHLY RESTRICTED MODS: congratulations Console Gamers for finally being able to eat at the table scraps of the buffet PC gamers have been gorging ourselves at for about 2 decades now, but I hope I don't shatter any illusions when I say that you are only getting the bare minimum of what PC gamers get. Bethesda says it is to reduce mod clashes and errors but honestly I got more buggy mods for Bethesda then I ever did from the Nexus.
POOR COMMUNICATION SKILLS: a lot of people asked for a lot of things in a fallout game I don't remember anyone asking to speak entirely in “Gist” just tell me what I am going to say. More than once I agreed to a course of action I didn't want to just because the response said “sarcastic response.”
In the end it comes to this. I feel like fallout 4 sold it's soul for a payday and that makes me very sad.

How can I describe Starbound to best show what you should expect?
Well, for starters, every planet is randomly generated, each with its own atmosphere and types of weather. Enemies, NPCs, and weaponry are also randomly generated(to an extent). This means each experience is different, THIS means there's plenty of replayability.
There are plenty of armor/cosmetic items to customize your character in a way that suits your playstyle, these are especially useful for roleplay with friends.
The game is still in development currently, so some things are likely to be changed in the future.
Starbound also has a huge mod community allowing you to add twists to normal games or to completely create your own world.
I would highly recommend it if you have a lot of time to waste!

Review update on ver 0.9.3.1
After many month of not playing the game i see the game have developed quite significantly due to hardwork and passion of the developer making the game. I really appreciated it because not many EA game do this (props to guys at nival ;)). Now I will breakdown my review on 4 major point as :
1. Campaign
I REALLY LOVE the effort on the campaign because the map look beautiful, the voice lines narrating the game match the nationalities, and the level of difficulty on each scenario.
2. UI
The UI feels less wonky and clutter from the previous one which is nice addition to the game. Also i love the new potrait style commander. But i dislike when you boot the game you jump directly into the worldmap mode where campaign and multiplayer option placed in one big map. Maybe split the page between campaign and multiplayer would be nice
3. Realism
I miss realism part of blitzkrieg where supply play major part of the battle. Good progress on armor rework, i like that !
4. MP
MP game are split between base assault and traditional 1v1 2v2 or 3v3 format. As for base assault it got huge improvement as the ai call unit to recapture the flag and so on. But this type of gameplay is not fun to watch and play (in my taste). Maybe some people like it but i personally dislike it.
Now the traditional format. Skirmish in my opinion are too barebone. The reason i say this because in 1v1 (the game i played) the objective to capture 3 victory point. The problem is when you already cap this point, you can simply ambush his spawn point until he out of reinforcement. This make the game boring because you cannot comeback nor do some tactical move because as soon as you spawn, your men will die as fast as you cook oatsmeal. On the other point the map you make is really good. My input to this is increase spawn point further from enemy spawn point or give cue where your unit will spawn with some protection or base defense.
My point is the MP matches is too fast to end and don't give the excitement when played. But i liked the loadout system now before going to combat because it make your army comp varies (as before i disliked it). So TLDR i dont get what concept rts style are on skirmish as is fast as CoC battles but have concept like defense in-depth, trenches, mg, smoke,etc.
Now the bonus part, Technical part. The game run average on my rig, consider this is are EA the subject may change. Also skirmish servers are lag which is annoying in my opinion (curios about server location, because i played COH2 quite fine). I like your bug department which is fast in fixing bug (+1).
=================================================================
So TLDR Blitzkrieg 3 is a beautiful game with OUTSTANDING campaign scenario and voice over but WEAK MP due to lack of strategic and decision thinking made in the game . If you buy only for the campaign and Base attack style game (CoC formula with some addition) then open your wallet and buy this game as soon as your money available. But if you like me where you seek pleasure in MP game where moving troops, tactical decision matters(when to cap vp, push, etc) and become a salty person as soon as you lose, avoid this game and reconsider to buy it when it mild sale or heavy sale because the MP in the current state is too barebone and boring. Hope it helps you guys :)

I've bought this game without knowing a lot about it, I've just seen a gameplay.
So, the game basic idea is a tower defense, actually a first person tower defense where the main objective is protect a core. You can build your turrets and barrier and, when the horde comes you can use your two weapons (a main weapon and a secondary weapon) for killing the enemies.
About the scenary...is simply amazing! the background is well done (as you can see on the screenshots) and the musics are enjoyable.
About the enemies, I have to tell you that the hordes come randomly, I mean that when you play a level and then you play it again, waves are not always the same. The monsters you have to kill are a lot and differents, some small, fast and weak, others big...very...VERY big, slow but with a solid armor. Of course flying enemies are in this game too. Sometimes you have to defeat a BOSS that is a bigger and freakingly strongest version of one of the other enemies with a stronger attack or a different (but always strongest) one. Some monsters have weak points so if you can you can use them for a faster massacre.
There are a lot of different towers with different strength, speed and specialized again different tipe of monsters that you can unlock by levelling up. Same thing happens for the secondary weapons and the skills you can give to your pg, a lot of secondary weapons and skill that suit better to a particular pg more than to another one.
A thing that I have found quite fascinating is the possibility of the multiplayer, you can choose to play alone by playing a private campaign or you can allow other players to enter in your map and play with you.
So if you are looking for a game with a quite good plot, a lot of action and sometimes very difficult enemies, Sanctum 2 is the game for you.
