If you are a fan of LEGO games, then you are probably going to love this. With a plot loosely based around The Matrix, it features some fantastic sequences, like a high-speed pursuit on a futuristic bike. As Wyldstyle (the female Trinity-esque protagonist) jumps from one vehicle to another while being pursued by the bad guys, it uses LEGO's two character co-op format brilliantly. Matrix 2, eat your hat! Early on though, a lot of the 'action' does involve building and demolition in the construction world. It's a clear nod to the real-world LEGO and you even have to seek out the instructions for the builds. These are identical to the type of instruction leaflets packed with real boxes of LEGO, on of many nice little touches to the game. I haven't watched the movie yet, but it's likely it pretty much recreates most of the scenes from the movie, as previous LEGO movie-tie-ins have. This time of course, with it being LEGO's very own product and movie, they have free reign to go nuts, throwing everything at you like a bucketload of trademarked plastic bricks. It also continues the trend of featuring humorous dialogue and sight gags. It's probably the funniest of all the LEGO games, and quite possibly the best. You rush through plenty of different themed LEGO worlds in the multiverse, donning some nifty apparel, which changes from location to location. There are as usual, plenty of characters to unlock, or purchase in the game. It doesn't really scream originality, with the usual tasks of collecting many, many hidden items  in an attempt to add replayability. It does pretty much what previous LEGO games have done before, but it does this very well, and is nicely graphically polished. Those who avoid LEGO games won't find much here to change their opinion. But fans will simply enjoy the ride. And the annoyingly catchy "Everything is Awesome" song will be rolling around your head for days after.

It's difficult to talk about the Muv-Luv series without devolving into platitudes like, "an unforgettable experience," or "one of the greatest VNs of all time." That's because it truly is something special. It's an introspective epic, full of action, comedy, and pathos. I consider it a masterpiece, not only within its genre, but among all contemporary fiction.
If you are at all interested in mecha, this is a must-play. If you are enjoy military fiction (e.g.
), you will love this. If you want visceral drama -- if you want to feel hope, horror, sadness, and relief -- this game will take your emotions for a ride. If you want to read something with intricate detail in military operations and quantum mechanics, this is it.
Yet it's difficult to recommend.
Muv-Luv is a visual novel (all story, no gameplay) originally released in 2003. It comprises the first two entries in the Muv-Luv trilogy: Muv-Luv Extra and Muv-Luv Unlimited. The final and most renowned entry, Muv-Luv Alternative, was released as a separate product in 2006, and, accordingly, the English localization will be sold separately.
If that's confusing: don't worry about it. Point is, this game is only 2/3rds of the full Muv-Luv experience, but it's the entire original game. For the purposes of this review, I'm looking at the series as a whole.
Why is Muv-Luv difficult to recommend to newcomers? The main reason is its sheer length. Extra and Unlimited together (that is, this Steam product) will probably take an average reader 40+ hours to complete. Alternative is about another 50+ hours on top of that. The whole series is bigger than most other VNs, including Clannad, Fate/stay night, and YU-NO. It has more words than
twice over, or all the Harry Potter books put together. It is
.
If that scares you, turn back now.
Still with me? Of course, the prose is nowhere near as dense as
, and a very large portion is voiced dialogue that goes at a comfortable peace. The series has highly advanced graphics by VN standards, with moving sprites, traditional animation, and 3D scenes, and a phenomenal soundtrack featuring JAM Project. It's not a dry read by any means.
But compounding the issue of length is that the game doesn't fully blossom until its final part, Muv-Luv Alternative. The themes that compose its central drama are merely touched upon in Extra, and Unlimited only goes toe-deep into the pool. For that reason, there are some who advocate skipping Extra, or Extra and Unlimited, entirely.
There's some merit to the idea. Frankly, Extra isn't anything special by itself. It's a generic romantic comedy, albeit a fun and amusing one, with little of import to say. Unlimited is largely the same thing, except with a change in milieu and some minor mecha elements.
However, I strongly recommend against skipping straight to Alternative. Not only would you lose out on crucial story, foreshadowing, and character development, it would be missing the entire point of Muv-Luv.
I have been intentionally scant on plot details throughout this review, but I can safely say this: Muv-Luv is about what we take for granted. It's about the duty one bears not only to himself, but to his country and his loved ones. The protagonist, Shirogane Takeru, lives a blissful, unaware life at the story's beginning. By the end, he will be confronted and challenged time and again, forced to evaluate himself and strive toward virtue.
The banality of Extra, then, is a crucial part of the experience. It grounds ourselves (as readers) in a world similar to our own, if slightly wackier and more harem-centric. When that carefree lifestyle is taken away from our protagonist, we feel the loss too. And when glimpses of it return later on -- fragments of peace amid despair -- we cherish it all the more.
What Muv-Luv does is bold and unusual. The first 20+ hours that a reader invests into the series are of enormously different character than its greatest part. Pragmatically speaking, that isn't bearable for most people, especially since it's polarizing content in its own right (being anime-inspired, reliant on Japanese culture, etc.).
Moreover, even when Muv-Luv is at its best, it's not the sort of writing that will appeal to all tastes. Lengthy action scenes are marked by even lengthier build-ups, and there are frequent monologues during periods of reflection. And tangential “infodump” scenes break up the pace to flesh out the world and explain events in more detail than practically necessary. These aspects make for excellent immersion and worldbuilding (think
), but can be off-putting to a reader looking for nothing more than hot-blooded action and drama.
So Muv-Luv is not for everybody.
But I love this game and wish for it to be loved by more.
If you haven't played a visual novel before, but find what I've said appealing and aren't scared away by the copious amounts of moe, give it a shot! If you are a fan of visual novels but haven't played Muv-Luv, what are you waiting for? It's a masterpiece.

Before I begin, I must make it clear that I have completed this release with the fan translated release, and have not yet completed the Steam release. And given how Degica chose to promote this release - by spoiling elements presented later on in Muv-Luv Unlimited in their released media - my review will cover both Extra and Unlimited and the bare story elements contained within each. Excluding that, my review will be spoiler-free. Additionally, I will rarely talk about the final part of the trilogy (Muv-Luv Alternative) in this review which plans to release on Steam in Q4 of 2016.

Since its release in early 2003, the Muv-Luv trilogy has risen to be one of the most well-regarded and popular visual novels (aka VNs) ever released, with its final work, Muv-Luv Alternative, being ranked #1 on the
and ranked in the top three in Japan's VN rankings. Ever since its fan localization, the series has gained worldwide recognition enough to be later be the #1 most funded visual novel and ranked in the top 30 most funded video game on Kickstarter raising over $1.25 million in support. Length-wise, this two-part story spans the length of 25-40 hours varying, especially if one decides to read the extra routes presented in both.

In comparison to the original, the UI has dramatically improved, with a beautiful options screen coated in a glorious pink containing a wide range of options. The only change I would like to see is the addition of sliders for text speed and auto-read speed instead of the default Slow, Medium, and Fast.

As for the translation, Degica has made a notable improvement in cleaning the rough grammar and wording that the English fan translation lacked. Additionally, there is an option for Japanese text as well (but as an non-Japanese speaker, I have a hard time evaluating it).

Opinions vary regarding the aesthetic of the game, but in my opinion it’s passable. Although the character designs are quite rough and outdated, they are cute and simple. My feelings are quite similar about the CG and backgrounds.

Muv-Luv Extra follows the story of typical high school protagonist, Shirogane Takeru, and consists of a wacky slice-of-life romantic comedy involving a wide array of potential romantic interests the player can romance. Other than having a couple of interesting and absurd plot revelations, ML Extra is a pretty stereotypical romantic comedy with some interesting deviations. Apart from the two main heroines, Kagami Sumika and Meiya Mitsurugi, the other pursuable love interests are uninteresting and tropey. Despite this, ML Extra is still a passable love story with some single tear-worthy and funny moments. Although it’s nothing special, I'd still recommend reading it if one would want to read a cute romcom and for the main purpose of getting to ML Unlimited (and later ML Alternative), as those two pieces are worth the read and reward the player for reading through ML Extra.

Muv-Luv Unlimited consists of the same group of characters introduced in ML Extra, but setting-wise, is completely different. In this sequel, the player is introduced into a whole new world, one consisting of sci-fi technology and concepts including mechs, aliens, and much more. Originally, Unlimited was supposed to be revealed as a surprise to ML Extra players later on, but with the way Degica promoted this two-part game, any and all elements of surprise regarding this setting were abandoned. In comparison to ML Extra, little is different regarding the characters. Story-wise there's not much to praise or complain about with the bulk of it being so-so. The introduction of mechs and military certainly up the interest though and were fun elements the characters dived into. Fortunately, towards the end, there is a huge spike in quality regarding the story in its attempt to set up the player for the later masterpiece, Muv-Luv Alternative.

(or TL;DR)
ML Extra and Unlimited are passable pieces of fiction, and although are nice in various parts, are average overall. Despite this, the reading experience was still enjoyable, and reading these two pieces are definitely worth it in preparation for reading ML Alternative in the near future, which I believe to be one of the greatest pieces of military sci-fi fiction to have ever released.

Soooo after a fairly decent wait, however not long at all considering how other kickstarters have worked, we finally have the first two (Technically one) VN's in the muv luv triology, since i have read both of these thrice over or so i'll just do a quick review after skimming sumika's route
First up, they have done an excellent job importing this to the Alternative engine, this brings more life to the vn with actual movement and lip animation in the characters and of course a 16:9 resolution over the original 4:3
Along with that they have also improved the translation quality which is amazing considering it didn't take too long for this to be released, they also added an option to switch between english and japanese image text (and normal text) which is also another bonus
Anyway on to the vn itself
Extra:
This is a generic romance, not going to hold anything back because this is my favorite VN series of all time, the characters are all cliche as f*ck however they aren't that bad in  terms of writing, the reason why Extra is techinically 'bad' is because the entire setting and such makes the characters act in a typical uninteresting way which is what this triology relies on heavily. You have your main character which can appear as a 'self insert' if you lok at it that way although he generally is a lot more agressive and a lot less, ahem, frgid?, you'll also notice that Extra likes to make fun of typical romance tropes, a lot actually since the bulk of this game is pure comedy which isn't that bad
Overall without spoiling, Extra is a romance with decent comedy, general charcters and settings, nothing is surprising and it's fine that way, how much you enjoy extra will be based on your experience with the Romance/SoL settings in general
Next up is:
Unlimited:
Yes, this is where the story takes about a 90 degree turn (180 is alternative) and thrusts our poor Shirogane in to an entirely different world, or is it?
*SPOILERS START HERE*
This is where everything starts to get interesting, the entire world has been at war for over 50-60 years with an alien race codenamed BETA [Beings of Extra-Terrestrial origin that are Adversarys of the human race) and the town he had lived in was now a crumbled mess and he 'spawned' in his house in the same location as his house in the previous world, a quick walk around town still leads him to believe it to be a dream, it's only when he approaches a seemingly miltaristic base where his school used to be that he starts realising it's a reality, or well, kind of
Unlimited largely relies on your familiarity with the cast as they all appear in Unlimited (MINUS ONE), while yes it does rely on slice of life and romance genres like Extra, the setting and events all push it out differently, All the characters still retain their personalities of the previous world however due to their experiences and such in this world their ideologies and such differ a little and Takeru realises this quickly, however there's no point to dulging in to this quickly as Unlimited just scratches on the surface at what will come in to Alternative
Anyway, Unlimited is quite a bit more enjoyable than alternative, it does delve in to much deeper themes and many serious events occur which start to flesh out these counter-parts of the characters you experienced in the dream world of extra whilst still retaining the dreamish feeling by avoiding any drastic or downright dark events, keeping unlimited still in the realms of a slice of life, it also exists to familiarise you with the BETAVERSE, how the political structure is working, how the civilians and the military think and work, all of this incredibly strong worldbuilding exists here and should not be skimmed over, while it isn't shown a full timeline exists showing every single event since the beta landed over 60 years ago.
The VN ends off at a point which makes you ask questions, i'm not going to lie as this is not a VN with a 'happy' ending, the ending is supposed to make you anticipated for the sequel, in the end there is nothing that could be done and the dream is shattered, it's definitely an ending that will hit you if you have actualyl read Extra + Unlimited

The amount of game time for my Steam profile may be low, but I've played through the original fan translation.
This review is as spoiler free as possible
Is it worth it? Yes most definitely. If you enjoy Sci-Fi stories with great characters that have depth, then this game is for you. Muv-Luv is a visual novel so that means it's basically a virtual book with some light choice making that puts you on different story paths.
Before you start there's a pretty big change from the original, it lets you choose which story arc you want to start with. While it may be tempting to immediately jump into Unlimited, the one that seems the most interesting. However the best way to play it in my opinion is to crack open Extra and play through Sumika and Meiya's routes.
The reason being is that playing through those two routes will establish characters and events that the other will constantly flash back to.
In terms of this port, it's fantastic. The original version was notorious for crashing and glitching out and that is completely absent from this version. The updated UI looks way better than the cumbersom 90's visual novel UI that the original has. And finally the presentation was updated to match Alternative's, with no text boxes and animated sprites.
Overall this game is great and and the story is fantastic. I'd recommend getting it as soon as you can before Alternative comes out so you can jump immediately into it.

I do genuinely enjoy this game.  I'll make that clear.  People have complained about the mashup words dominating the setting, but, personally, I find it no worse or sillier than most pulp sci-fi franchises, such as Warhammer 40k or Star Wars.  The setting's generally put together with enough earnestness that one can appreciate it right through that sort of problem.
That said, this game is by the writer of Heroes Rise, and it shares many of that game's weaknesses.  I hated the forced "Reality TV" mechanic in the Hero Project, and it's back here in full force.  If anything, it's *worse*, with both sides quickly revealed to be total jerks very early on, making caring too much about their petty political struggles extremely difficult.  Characters are allergic to saying anything outright, not for in-character reasons, but either for contrived environmental factors or to hold out information for the sequel.  And it's far, far too easy to accidentally drop a stat you were raising making choices that won't obviously alter it.
And they threw the hint system in as DLC instead of an unlockable in-game mechanic!  Bad designer!  Bad!  No need to port over the worst practice of the Heroes Rise series!
All of that said, it shares Heroes Rise's strengths too.  The sometimes-byzantine mazes of stats from the older games are pared down nicely into two sets, one for "combat" and one for "social" tests, and the pile of relationship bars is quite nice, offering concrete feedback for how certain actions affect the characters.  And, again, to the writer's credit, if the player gets fed up with the Reality TV nonsense, they have multiple opportunities to slag it off in dialogue.  It doesn't change the pointless bickering factions mechanic, but it at least offers a little catharsis.
If you liked the Heroes Rise generally, give the demo a try.  There's a bit for you here.  And, if you liked The Hero Project best, well, you'll probably like this one even more than me.

My Ally at the time took control of an Asteroid and slammed it into the largest earthlike planet. With 3 eneimes left, I took another 30 ships and sent them to take over the lava planet. First in a series from the same writer that wrote the Heroes Rise series.
The characters are very interesting and encompose a wide variety of science fiction and fantasy tropes.  The story seems to be setting up to be rather long and complex which means it could be years before we actually get to the end.  Your character comes from a culturally isolated world and one of the most important things it tracks, though it has little impact in this game, is Growth; your ability to understand and adapt to new cultures.  Lots of deep issues teased her such as the nature of divinity and what it means to be sapient.  Some of the naming conventions are a bit weird though I imagine that this was largely done to show just how different some species and cultures are from each other.
This game's biggest flaw is that it teases so many things but doesn't really have the time to get into one thing in any real depth.  It lacks a traditional climax which, once the series is complete, may not matter  but can have you feeling a little hollow as a stand-alone game.  As a setup chapter though it is top notch and I can't wait to see where the story and existential distinctions go.

text:
Muv-Luv is a franchise that first began as a visual novel way back in 2003, THIRTEEN years ago. It is only now that the game is officially available in English for the first time and on Steam. The Steam store page for Muv-Luv claims that it is the "most highly-acclaimed visual novel series of all time" and to be honest, that is actually possible. No VN series gained as much acclaim as Muv-Luv did, especially considering the age of the original VN. Muv-Luv to visual novels is like what Star Wars is to movies. It has gained sequels and spin-offs in the form of other VNs, manga and anime.
The Muv-Luv VN that you can purchase here is a story that comprises of two arcs; Extra and Unlimited. Extra starts out as what you can call your "basic VN love story" where the hero has to choose between girls but when the Unlimited arc starts, things kick into high gear. The series explores storytelling elements like timelines or alternate realities but what is prominent in all Muv-Luv media since the Unlimited arc is the fight of the human characters against aliens called the BETA (Beings of the Extra Terrestrial origin which is Adversary of human race). And fans are drawn to the franchise's own spin on giant robots called TSFs (Tactical Surface Fighters). Unlike many other Japanese franchises, TSFs are named and based on real-world military aircraft. My favorite for example is the F-22A Raptor.
Since this is a VN, the gameplay (or lack of, if you're cynical) is what you would expect. Muv-Luv follows a linear plot line, which offers pre-determined scenarios and courses of interaction, and focuses on the differing scenarios of the female main characters. Personally, I think Muv-Luv has a lot more choices than most visual novels and the game has multiple plot lines that the player can follow, one for each heroine in the story, and there's supposedly nineteen possible endings. The game even fails you for making the wrong decision. To view all the plotlines, it is highly recommended to replay the game and make different decisions.
All in all, if you're into VNs, Muv-Luv is more than worth it to purchase and play through many times. It has an interesting world, characters and plot. You won't regret getting invested in the story. However, if you're not the type that plays visual novels or can't stand that much reading, then obviously it's best that you move on and play something else. If you play it and enjoy it, the story doesn't end there. Unlimited is followed by Muv-Luv: Alternative which should be released by the end of the year. And yes, there's going to be a R18+ patch, apparently. You can never have enough "plot".
P.S. Despite what you hear from some people who already know the story, DON'T SKIP EXTRA!!! Yes, the game gives you the option of going straight into Unlimited which is the more "exciting" arc but if you truly want the full experience, play Extra first, ESPECIALLY if this is your first time playing Muv-Luv. Don't be afraid that you'll be wasting time just because somebody else says you would.

TL;DR: The Muv-Luv trilogy is a must-read for anyone who calls themself a fan of visual novels. That said, its legendary status is only made apparent after reading all three games: Extra, Unlimited, and Alternative (note that this Steam title includes both Extra and Unlimited). While I would be cautious to recommend only Extra and Unlimited, I wholeheartedly recommend them in the context of the entire trilogy. Extra is redeemed by Unlimited and you will be thoroughly rewarded with Alternative.
This is a difficult game to explain without spoilers. So difficult, in fact, that the official Steam description and preview video delve into spoiler territory. Regardless, I will try to stay spoiler-free.
Muv-Luv is a visual novel trilogy and franchise that is highly celebrated in both Japan and the west. On EGS (Japanese), Alternative is ranked the #3 VN of all time. On VNDB (English), Alternative is ranked the #1 VN of all time by a significant margin (July 2016).
This Steam title, Muv-Luv, includes the first two parts of the trilogy: Muv-Luv Extra and Muv-Luv Unlimited.
I implore you to not skip straight to Unlimited (Part 2). Extra (Part 1), despite being slow, is a requirement to fully set the characters and tone for the sequels. This series truly is something special, but only when read in full.
Muv-Luv Extra is your generic anime high-school rom-com. The MC, Takeru, is your generic self-insert protagonist. Meiya is the generic affluent ojou-sama. Sumika is the generic short-tempered childhood friend. Ayamine is the generic Rei expy. I could go on.
While Extra is not terrible, it's nothing special on its own. It's leagues better than many VNs on Steam, that's for sure, but its real purpose is to build up the characters and set the scene for the remaining two games.
Unlimited--which is included in this release--is where things start to get unique and interesting (sci-fi, mecha, drama) but you must read Extra to fully appreciate it (and also to eventually appreciate Alternative, which is god-tier).
ART: Despite being an old game, Muv-Luv's art holds up surprisingly well. The rUGP engine was ahead of its time, and that helps breathe life into the visuals for Muv-Luv. The artwork itself, while aged, has an undeniable charm that keeps it fresh even in the age of perfectly polished HD assets.
MUSIC: You may have heard that Muv-Luv has an incredible soundtrack. Anyone saying that is referring to Alternative, which does have a phenomenal OST. Unfortunately, this is not true for Extra nor Unlimited. The slice of life soundtracks are repetitive in the worst way and there's not a wide variety of them.
VOICE: The voices, overall, are pretty good. I would prefer to have a fully voiced MC, but the performances from the rest of the voice actors make up for it.
ANIMATION: Muv-Luv was made long before the Live-2D or e-Mote systems were implemented and stood out as having brilliant animation for its time. The animation, especially in this renewed edition, still stands strong. You won't see most of the animated scenes until Unlimited (and only then ultimately polished in Alternative), but these scenes further down the line make you feel like you're watching a well-choreographed cutscene.
STORY: The series is praised for good reason. Unfortunately, it doesn't shine until Unlimited and doesn't fully blossom until Alternative. You will have to trust me on this one: Extra is a slow trudge, but you'll be happy to have not skipped it when reading Alternative.
This ended up longer than I expected. Should you buy this game? Yes, absolutely. But you must also buy and play Alternative for the full experience.

Son of Nor is interesting at a glance. Although it has some very dated graphics, anyone can look at it and say 'hey, that looks like it could be fun', and they'd be right.
Son of Nor has moments at which I really enjoy myself. But they are few and far between. The game seems dead-set on forcing it's users on trudging through poorly designed levels, plagued with poorly designed puzzles that halt the otherwise interesting action component of the game.
The multiplayer can bring some enjoyment to the table as well, but it's just fluff--there isn't any portion of the game that I truly felt like it would benefit from having another player accompany me through. The levels are small, and that is only hidden by the sea of barely understandable puzzles that seem to be designed to not engage the player, but instead hinder their progress.
I think there's a lot of good ideas in this game, some of which are executed quite well. But at the end of the day, it's tedious, uninteresting, and just not very fun.

So after playing this game shortly after launch on Linux, I have to say, that even though I have not tested it under windows, 30-40 fps with a GTX 970 just doesn't seem right. However, I would still say this game is well worth the price. While the story/dialogue is somewhat confusing, the actual gameplay elements are truly one of a kind. The combat takes some getting used to, but overall, it really is a unique experience. Launching sharp/heavy objects from your surroundings at your enemy can be quite exhilarating, but also having the option to bury them in sand, or drop them off a cliff makes for some interesting styles of fighting. Having no UI is actually implemented quite well in my opinion, and turning to sand to indicate losing health actually feels natural. But where this game really shines is with the puzzles. It makes excellent use of telekinesis, and while some of the puzzles can be a bit confusing at first, once you realize what you're supposed to be doing, they actually have some very clever designs.  Overall, this game does have some rough edges, but for the $20 asking price, I'd say it's money well spent. and if you can get it on sale, then I say definitely grab this game. There really isn't anything else quite like it.

The gameplay is dull. There's only one tactic effective against each type of enemy, and only a few different types of enemies. Telekinesis, which doesn't require mana and is available from the start, is the easiest way to kill most enemies, so there's very little reason to use the spells that cost mana.
The story is not very interesting. I feel like a lot of it was lost in translation, because there just isn't much there. It alludes to there being a lot more lore that wasn't explained. Also, I have no idea what happened in the ending - did my character
? I have no idea. It just cut to credits.
As a better alternative to Son of Nor, I recommend the game "Tiny and Big: Grandpa's Leftovers". It has similar telekinesis-style mechanics, but is MUCH more fun and it has a coherent story.

I'm surprised at the general reviews for SFV, personally ive been able to play online better than in other fighting games available, there were some dc problems at the start but few of these dc's were actually during a match, most of them happened after a match, the dc's inside matches are 9 to 1 ragequits, I suspect people are confusing disconnects with ragequits (wich were rampant at release, but now they are almost unicorn rare since mechanics against this tactic were implemented).
Now on to the actual review:
If you have any history with fighting games, you will probably ADORE SFV, if you are coming from USFIV you might feel it a bit slow at first (but trust me, this game is in tornado speeds once you get used to it), you might also feel you have fewer options on wake up and generally few reversal options overall, but this is not a flaw, the game is heavily focused on footsies and punishes, with the counter mechanics, any YOLO button or uppercut will cost you dearly, so you have to play smart and patient.
One of the heavy appeals of SFV in my opinion, is its learning curve, you can start doing great plays with not that much time invested, unlike USFIV were you really had to grind your tech skill and matchup knowledge just to become mediocre at the game, don't get me wrong though, this does not mean its an easy game, anyone with a clear head and some skill will take you down in seconds if you don't understand the general footsies and approaches. This will be a bit frustrating for those starting to play, the game itself has very few gimmicks, wich means defeat will always be your fault, this can be soulcrushing, but you will live. In short words, the game is amazing for both veterans and beginners in the fighting game scene.
The V skills and activations are also an amazing addition, this can heavily change the course of a match since most activations are pretty strong and modify your character with very nice buffs or quite potent destructive abilities, Bison(dictator) v-trigger activation modifies the behaviour of most of your specials and lets you link them, it also enchances your dash wich is already pretty godlike, this is more of a passive empower, whereas Dhalsim activation is a flame carpet that will damage the opponent even while blocking, making this ability an instant tide changer but does not modify Dhalsim's abilities in any way. Aside from activations, every character has a V-Skill, this skills are varied amongs the cast and can be useful in many scenarios, taking both examples above once more, Bison`'s V-Skill allows him to soak up a projectile or attack upon use, if charged it will cast a fast projectile back to the attacker, whereas Dhalsim's V-Skill will allow him to float in the air momentarily, greatly increasing his defensive and offensive capabilities. Succesful use of V-Skill will also charge up your V-Gauge to have access to V-Trigger faster.
In terms of solo play, this game will really not give you much outside of the amazing training mode where you can enact different scenarios at will to polish your play, but for most fighting games enthusiast the lack of a good story mode or solo modes is a  very minor flaw, all in all SFV lives to the hype it built.

If Street Fighter 5 was free to play I could understand the decision to hold characters for ransom. But it costs SIXTY FREAKIN' DOLLARS to play this game!!
I'm frustrated because I want to love SF5, but this experience leaves me disappointed and cautious of purchasing another Capcom product. Even when the TURBO DELUXE HYPER ULTRA ARCADE CAMMYS SWIMSUIT EDITION comes out I will stay away from this product. There should be no video game with an upfront 60$ retail price that asks you pay more to get the full experience.

This new series... i dont know what to make of it really. It feels far to abstract and pulp sci-fi for my liking. The terms he uses, the world building he has done... it just dosnt work for me. I loved the hero rise series 'a lot', but this new project by Zach is just... well its disappointing.
Story wise its no inspiring at all, and the romance's are simply handed to you, you dont earn them. Far to many muti page narrative dumps, with few choices in between. The whole thing feels padded... with little progress being made. It dosnt feel like anything special happens because my character is one thing or another... at least nothing substantial.
The mechanics for this project are more complex then hero rise, but I don't feel thats a good thing in this case. The stats are presented more as a puzzle for achievement's then as a representation of character development.
The fact this project was designed specificity to run in series has greatly detracted from the quality as it doesn't feel like a complete story has been told... just the beginning. There is no clear beginning, middle, or end... just a beginning, middle, and to be continued. There was no clean or clear cut achievement the main character accomplished to make a conclusion to this first 'chapter'. It just seemed like "Well that seem a good place to stop, time to work one book two.".
Maybe I'm judging this project to harshly based on Zach's past work, but this one has left me disappointed and uninspired. In fact I ended up only lightly skimming and speeding through the final chapter since I had lost so much interest in the choices I was presented. It just didn't feel satisfying.
Take my opinion with a gain of salt though... this story just wasn't my 'thing'. That doesn't mean it won't be yours. Give it a shot if it appeals.

First in a multi-part series, versus places you in a murky sci-fi world where you must navigate between a multitude of conflicting loyalties. Do you seek power, revolution, peace, or love? Choose wisely and you may be able to recieve all of them, but choose poorly and you may find that these all lie beyond your grasp.
Versus is an intriguing choose your own adventure novel, familiar to anyone who's played one of their previous titles or read a CYAN when they were younger. The setting initially starts on a futuristic world that faces an invasion but eventually shifts towards a hunger-games esque world. While some of the words such as "ze" "hir" "blerg" are initially a little off-putting, as you continue to go through the novel it just becomes another aspect of the world. I highly recommend this to anyone that enjoys text adventures. Well worth $3.

If you don't like the storyline, there's a mod for that.
If you don't like creation club, there's a mod that disappears it.

If you wanted fallout, ya got fallout. It's its own version, but still counts.. by all accounts. Some may say the story isnt the best, and they have some good points. None of the other games have really great stories, if you think about it. FO3: find dad, help one group beat another group, save wasteland. FNV: Find guy who shot you, decide the fate of the watseland. The great thing about 4 is the factions. They aren't the flavors of the month like in NV, which you could easily tell right from wrong. "I wonder if the guys who crusify others are bad?" But in 4, you tend to side with whoever supports your personal philosophy on what it means to be human... or whoever you think is cooler. That's a good enough deciding factor.
Now, I will point out the things that made the other games, both in the Fallout and Elderscrolls series, are a bit lacking in this addition. I am refering to the cookyness. The crazy bits that make us giggle, or leave jaws agape. You can still find them in FO4, I assure you, but they don't feel as abundent. A few moments do come to mind that made me freak out, so they aren't none existant. The supposed lack of them isn't such a bad thing, but I know there're who made that a big deal. Fighting is pretty much they same, more or less, because is the same game engine. Tip: use the lean mechanic, it makes a bit of a difference, in my opinion. I will say, while the animations are typical Bethesda, they do a great job of making it feel like there is more to the game in general. Enemies leaning behind cover, melee hits feeling good when they follow through and connect, and the finishers. And in Bethesda fashion, they are a who new level of janky, I assure you.
New content: Building, gun and gear modification, new enemy types, "Legendary enemies and gear" The building is a new aspect that makes use of the whole "Rebuilding the commonwealth" storyline, which only a few of the main factions seem to want... including the raiders... buts that's DLC... so... >_>  The best way to comment on the actual workings of the builing engine is by the fan favorite Obsidian "Not for the faint of heart or the serious of temperament" The ingame modifications are as expected; a subtle level of progression with each new piece being a straight upgrade or with a specific aspect. i.e. being fire proof, reducing limb damage, aiding stealth. The new enemies are an interesting twist, adding in things like a new robot, the assulatron. Re working mirelurks, again, with making 3 tiers. These tiers are 1) shelled 2) kings and 3) queens. The other tiered enemies are similar from "ES:V Skyrim", as they rise in skill as the player does. The new tier brought back from FNV is the Legendary enemies. Unlike NV, where they were in a set location, these are integrated with the normal enemy spawns. This adds a nice twist of unexpected danger with every encounter. These enemies carry a guarenteed legendary, but that doesn't always mean it will be useful.
The only major problem people have is with Bethesda themselves. They took a service that has been community supproted for years and but a AAA price tag on it. It is a sad sight to see, I won't deny that. But you must realise that the whole point of mods in the first place was for people who wanted to add things, big or small, to their games once the developer realesed it. This process is, in a whole, completely optional. Thats doesn't rule out that those who make them already should be overlooked. This was a fullpriced game at one point, so paying for moddifications, not just dlc, seems like a dumb move. It doesnt ruin the game for me, but it leaves a bad taste in the mouth.
all in all, decent game. 3.5/5

Great at what it does.
What it does isn't great.
With sim driving games becoming ever more accurate, entry level driving games becoming more sim-like with every iteration, and the floaty arcade "physics" of the truly arcade "arcade racer" now almost completely a thing of the past, Burnout has basically...yep, you guessed it: burned out.
It's a shame since Burnout Paradise, save for a few muddy textures here and there (namely actually the mud textures) still looks great and has the overall structure of a really excellent arcade romp but what's aged most seriously and most detrimentally is specifically the car handling.
The cars are tuned to be able to corner more or less perfectly at ridiculous speeds (a requirement dictated by the earlier Burnout games) and as such have handling so far removed from real-world physics that even by today's standards, for the arcade-racer end of the driving game continuum, they feel counterintuitive, unwieldy and ultimately really just broken.
For instance if you tap the break it should give you more traction and better handling rather than destabalise the car, as it seems to do across the board without fail in Burnout Paradise.
If someone could get into the guts of the thing and just make the power, speed and handling of the cars actually just vaguely realistic, adjust the camera placement etc., I'd happily play through the entire game, but as it is, even paying only £4.99 for it I still feel like I paid too much, as ultimately, I feel like I bought something that looks great and has a huge amount of promise but which is simply just fundamentally broken at its core.
Burnout Paradise is to today's open world driving games what the Afterburner jet would be to the arcade flight combat games of the Burnout era: confusing, unwieldy and ultimately unsatisfying. Video game driving has moved on; Burnout has been left behind.

Firstly I would like to say that this game had some good concepts and ideas, if were not poorly executed- this game had great potential and generally would not be poor in terms of gameplay, mechanics, performance, dialogue, transitioning; these are the core elements in which should be top quality in a video game.
After playing an hour, attempting to fix an issue of lag, bare in mind my GPU is above the recommended yet it seems to be the case where my GPU is running at maximum capabilities in terms of memory and shader allocations; and yet I still have an issue with framerate and ligthing. I even lowered my resolutions from 1920x1200 to 1280x720, yet still the issue persue.  More on the topic of graphical issues, the 'telekanesis' ability when picking up rocks, in fact anything you pick up has a glitchty outer texture, whether that was supposed to be some sort of glowing effect- I do not know, but it was not well executed either way.
Okay, enough about performance issues and graphics, more onto the gameplay. Do not get me the wrong, the story has a good concept just the characters seem too wooden, emotionless and the whole dialogue just seems to be cliche, typical. The transitions seems to be unnatrual, with instancing between certain areas of the level you are on, meaning you get a loading screen for fixed points in the level. Most items you can control with your abilities, along with shaping the ground with terraforming, I believe that due to most things be prerendered, you get a lot of lag on the start of levels.
Combat is poor, I was expecting good combat with these great concepts, but mostly the AI is poor and enemies are too easy to deal with after playing 3 levels there is no challenge present (I am also playing on hard difficulty). And NPCs do most of the killing for you, which again, ruins the experience.
In conclusion, I would not recommend this game- it was a great idea but sadly was not expressed or brought out upon it's full potential. Which is a shame.

This game is odd in the way that it could have been so good. The music, atmosphere, and ideas surrounding the plot are great. The controls and level design fall short.  It's a 3-hour long platformer that will frustrate you when your inputs are ignored. You cannot adjust the game volume (there's an option, but as soon as you exit it re-adjusts back to the default setting: blow your speakers). The puzzles are very easy to figure out, but sometimes difficult to do because of shoddy controls, or time-limits. Both of which are a platforming no-no in my world. It feels awkward to control at times, funky things happen that (I'm assuming) shouldn't, like getting stuck on corners of platforms instead of landing on top of them or climbing them which the controls call for. For the 75% off price I bought it at, it's worth it; about two bucks. At the full price, it's not worth it. I urge this programmer to make a sequel and focus on controls and level design, because this idea really could be amazing.

Blitzkrieg 3 takes place in WWII Europe, where you control three forces through their battles:
Germany conquering France, Russia conquering Germany and America fighting for Sicily.
In singleplayer, the game is a typical RTS, you command units, that are either added to your forces by you freeing them, fullfilling objectives or just as reinforcements. You have no impact on the types of units that your army is made of, so you basically have to adapt to your army, and not the other way around.
The three nations have the same units, maybe with minimal slight variations, but the overall gameplay is the same for all. And this is where strategy comes in:
The game is basically beatable with very few, very basic strategies, once you learned an effective way to defend/attack you can always go back to that, since
all nations play the same. Thus the singleplayer is nothing special.
The multiplayer on the other hand features something very unusual for this genre: You are provided with a base, the size of which grows with your level,
that you need to build up and defend with units and structures from other players. Upon an enemy attacking, your units are controlled by AI. You gain resources
over time, that you can use to buy and upgrade units and structures. When attacking, you are matched against a random player of similar level and have to fight their setup. It is an interesting concept, very often seen in mobile games.
+Nice graphics, creating a fitting atmosphere
+Troops speak in their native language
~The multiplayer gameplay is new for this genre, but often seen on mobile devices
~Singleplayer offers nothing special
-The singleplayer is very basic
-All nations play the same
-There is no straightup 1v1 battle

Sign Motion is an extremely creative 2D scrolling puzzle/challenge game that begins when events throw your character's sign out of its normal existence.
You play as a stick figure, either male or female (changed in settings), that traverses across of signs from throughout the world.  The signs in the game provide clues as to what puzzles or challenges you will face, ranging from sliding cars to falling rocks, explosive crates, and poisonous gas that chases through through a large portion of the game.
Your progress is saved after each major puzzle or challenge and, if you 'die,' you restart at the most recent save point, ready to begin the challenge again.
Although the game is not overly hard, it provides a hint system for the slightly more complex challenges that explains in three individually revealed images how to pass the challenge.
There are a few visual treats in the game as you go along, including indicators for how much is left to travel before you finish by way of US destination milage signs.
Sign Motion is ultimately a game on level with mobile or console gaming that was ported to PC.
All in all, Sign Motion is a really cute, creative, fun game that will entertain you for a few plays.  Realistically, you could get 2-3 fun iterations of this game before you've successfully completed all of the challenges without issue.
Options are limited in the game, which is a design for both console and PC games.
For HoH gamers, you can choose volume between master volume controls, game sounds, and game music, allowing you to tune according to what is best for you.
As a side note for mobility challenged gamers, this game uses either A and D or left and right arrows to move forward and backward, left control to push/pull objects, and space to jump.  These keys cannot be changed.
This game can be complete and enjoyed entirely without sound, so no captions are needed or provided.
This is a single player game; no chatting.

Alright lets face it.. Street Fighter V.. A Good game or Bad? Thats honestly how you find it..
The Good of the game-
- Its easy to pick up and learn
- Characters you remember from past games, along with some new
- Classic feel at BASE level of other street fighter games
- Music is actually good
-Stages look nice, and have a good feel to them
- Classic 1v1 Street Fighter
-Decent tutorials for the game itself, and each character
The Inbetweens
-Cross play while nice, causes problems as well
- Both good and bad that you dont have an easy way to talk to someone. Really good so you dont hear stuff you dont want, but really bad when trying to find people, or ask questions.
- Its not USFIV (I personally loved Super SFIV.. and AE and ultra kinda were eh to me..)
- "Free DLC Characters" Not really free... but you can get with in game currency.. Wouldn't be too bad, but it seems to become hard to get more Fight money once you beat the few things you can do offline.. So.. have fun trying to play online to get them

The Bads of the game
-Very Bare bone fighting game, especially for the price. I know DLC is coming to add story mode and such but still
- No Arcade mode?
- This is personal but.. I feel the game is wayyy to offensive of a fighter.. Even characters like Dhalsim, and Guile who are known as your defensive characters from games past, seem to have better skills suited for offensive gameplay style.
- No true vs CPU mode- Granted you can do this in training mode
- Automatic picking of your character in ranked matches.. Come on really? What if my favorite character is Chun Li, but I was trying out guile and wanted to play him in ranked.. I have to make sure to switch my favorite character? Why?
- Friends list is pretty bad, along with trying to find games with them, I know this isnt steam or capcoms  fault at all, but SFIV felt so much better at this..
- Roll back... DEAR GOD ROLL BACK.. Ive had this problem since the betas.. Again.. you have a fine example of how to do it, with Skullgirls.. and let us set network delays and show us pings.. but no.. Capcom loves its bar system.
- Rematch in ranked? Seems nice right.. Well.. it auto gives you the same character again.. And its not an automatic best 2/3.. If you give someone a rematch in rank after beating them.. and they win.. They dont have to play the tie breaker if they dont want to.
- This might just be me but visual looks of attacks.. I know everyone is on and on about "frame data" now, but some of these moves.. look unsafe as hell but are not, while others look safe and are not.. Chun Lis EX Legs being -2 (Mostly safe in the way this game works) is fine and all, but my god does it look like the move is punishable as hell
Look, if you love Street Fighter you most likely already bought this game. For what its worth, sure its an ok fighter, if you already enjoy other Street Fighters.. Overall though I would not recommend this game.. I may love Street Fighter, but I honestly can say I do not find SFV fun..

If you've ever played a GTA game before, this game will feel pretty familiar. Whether that's a good thing will depend on your threshold for playing another game that asks you to drive from point A to point B, picking up people, shooting gang members and the like. It's not that the game fails in delivering that kind of gameplay, but it doesn't actually bring anything new to the table.
On the other hand, where it does often deliver something different is in its story and setting. Where other games of this type tend to go over-the-top in its presentation of the criminal world, Sleeping Dogs actually manages to craft a compelling moral ambiguity in its main character, Wei Shen and the people around him. More so, its emotional moments feel real and horrifying. It's all the more disappointing that it doesn't really question that moral grey area that the situation of Wei Shen obviously creates any more than some superficial remarks. Still, it delivers an interesting story with a few memorable characters.
Perhaps what defines Sleeping Dogs the most is its setting. Not only is Hong Kong a perfect place for this type of game, all of it is presented in a callback to the 70s and 80s martial arts films, which is never more present that in the combat (guns are very scarce in the game).
In a nutshell, while it doesn't actually do anything new, Sleeping Dogs has a story to tell and it does so in a stylish manner.

i was wanting to have a fighting game that would replace the street fighter iv series as my most played since street fighter ii. sad to say, street fighter v is not it.
for starters, the mechanics have been, shall we say, streamlined. i understand their intention here, to ease more players into the game, to have beginners have a much better fighting chance against veteran players. downside is that it makes a lot of the characters, for the bread-and-butter combos at least, handle similarly. i can say that there's more than a handful characters where you can use the medium punch > medium punch > special move string very often and effectively.
but the thing is, they have indirectly drove players away from getting this. why? you've heard it - the lack of content.
i've been a long-time fighting game fan. i may not be as good as the pros, but i can say i'm an average to an above average player who can still rack up a decent win streak any time of day. i never thought this lack of content would affect me as much, because i only care about playing with human opponents. but then again, you can have the tightest gameplay and prettiest graphics (which this game both has), but if you can't bring in people to play your intentions for the game are moot.
the game is not a total wreck. it's netcode is better than ultra sf iv and the patches have made noticeable improvements (i can get opponents faster now). but i think it has suffered enough setbacks for it to not succeed. it did not make the splash it was supposed to do, and it was overshadowed by its well-documented issues. you also have to figure in the other current and upcoming fighting games (guilty gear xrd, kof xiv) that get a huge chunk of the attention pie. at this point, even if they manage to cram in more characters and an arcade or a proper story mode in there, it wouldn't do much. people may have already moved on. and we probably will be stuck by the same people that we get to play with online.
it's a game that is letdown by it's publisher's strategy rather than it's quality.

To make a long story short: "Sleeping Dogs" (SD) is so-called SANDBOX game (a la "Grand Theft Auto" or "Mafia" + numerous others). Many of the game aspects are the ususal to the genre, although it has individual characteristics, e.g. there is a lot more hand to hand unarmed fighting in "SD" than most such. After completing the game (which took me 88 hours in all), I stand amazed with "SD". It is BEST GAME I've played in a looong time.
The Plot: You play undercover cop Wei Shen. In Hong Kong Police. The fact that the game isn't set in some fictive American town is refreshing in itself. Wei has a grudge against the Hong Kong Mafia, and although it is questioned if he is the right man for the job, he is placed under DEEP undercover - only three others in the police knows his true background! Wei has spent the last many years in the US, in the LAPD. But is a native of Hong Kong, and is introduced into the minor street gang Water Street Gang by the naive underdog Jackie, and taken in by the gang boss Winston Chu.
The Gameplay: While you gain the trust of the thugs (who are rather suspious at first), you move up in the Hong Kong Mafia Hierachi, all the while you fight (mostly unarmed, guns only appear in the latter part of the game), drive all sorts of veichles in high speed pursuits (at one time chasing a stolen weeding cake!) and in illegal races round the streets, drive speed boats, do big and small "missions" for the gang +  a large number of optional "favours" which helps you gain "face", i.e. access to faster cars, buy new clothes and even new furniture for your apartment. All the while keeping yourself going by sleeping enough, eating right and downing a lot of energy drinks.
The game has MANY new and innovative twists and turns, and all the while you also got to help the police solve crimes including serial murder and kidnapping!
But who will you really be true to in the end? The law and your job as a cop (finding the HKPD more and more suspious) or your "family" in Mafia underworld?
Even though "Sleeping Dogs" does not introduce anything REALLY new to the genre, it is a good twist to the story that you r NOT just a criminal, but "prentend to be" undercover cop. The story is above average and the graphics are mindblowing.
I rate this game 9 of 10 possible points! Hightly recommended!

First it's important to note, that this title is the result of a Kickstarter project with a rather small budget. The developers put a lot of effort to make the most out of it, so it can be easy to forget that it's just a very small indie game and should be considered as such.
"Son of Nor" is a combination of adventure, action and puzzle game built around an unique combat mechanic: Instead of using normal (or abnormal) weapons, you command the world and the elements around you using your extraordinary telekinetic and elemental-magical powers.
These powers remind of "The Force Unleashed", the puzzles and archeological adventures of "Tomb Raider".
But the "Son of Nor" is not only a mere explorer: the destiny of his race, that fled into a hidden refuge from the threat of total extinction 400 years ago, depends on him, his special powers and his wits. If you are smart, you can even decipher an ancient alphabet to reveal the secrets of a past long-gone and the frightening future soon to come.
No worries though, the gameplay itself is rather streamlined and its puzzles were reduced in complexity so that even less patient players should not have much problems to move on. The more challenging riddles are only optional and give access to collectibles, more powerful spells and insight into the surprisingly elaborated plot.
So even if some aspects seem unpolished and far from state-of-the-art, the conception of the game flow is certainly not one of them, and this is an outstanding achievement. There are multiple facets working together hand in hand to make it very dynamic, fluid, complex and offering lots of options, while still being very intuitive:
- The controls are very intuitive and responsive and help to materialize your intentions effortlessly (with some exceptions like rotating objects, jumping and switching specific elemental spells).
- The saving system builds on smart use of checkpoints.
- There is a surprising variety to combine spells and "tricks" with each other. Even after beating the final level of the game you will not have seen them all!
- There is no ammo management.
On your quest you will be able to snatch three energy crystals that each can be filled with three elemental charges of wind, fire and spirit essence obtained from obvious sources in each level.
These sources will regenerate after a small time. This results in a very dynamic gameplay as the powers at your disposal will constantly change. You will run out of elemental power or objects to shoot, but at the same time defeated enemies, dropped weapons or destroyed environment will offer new opportunities. Or you can decide to take the fight close to a source of elemental. It's up to you.
This is definitely a refreshing and unique gameplay and makes "Son of Nor" special and worth of a recommendation!
The presentation is quite good for an indie game, but of course you can't expect a triple A production value.
- The music is very well done and fits perfectly. Especially the combat music is doing it right, it doesn't annoy me like in most other games, and the gentle drum roll that signals the end of each fight is very welcome.
- The voice overs are from top-notch actors and are well done.
- The art concepts and graphics offer a lot of nice sceneries.
- The models are ok for the most parts, but the Sarahuls don't cut it. On the other hand though I am glad that the lizards look a bit goofy and more comical than realistic. This makes sadistically experimenting with them a lot less sick and cynical.
- The animations are acceptable, but lacking in some areas: There are no face animations, and no proper animations of turning characters during cutscenes.
- The graphics engine has nice effects, but in some areas severe performance issues.
Generally the game shows a lot of dedication, but at the same time evolves the certain kind of charm of indie type amateurishness through occasional deficiencies in story telling, presentation and discrepancy between aspiration and delivering.
So even if you are in for nitpicking, you will have a lot of fun dissecting every single flaw of this game.
And most others will enjoy the game in any case.
––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––––
(There follows the former short version.)
The gameplay of this Kickstarter title is similar to the Jedi Knight series (or sequels), especially "The Force Unleashed", just without any lightsabers or weapons of the normal kind.
Well, except if you are able to telegrab a sword from an enemy, then it can be turned against the former owner – or his boss. I just was able to fatally headshot a boss with the sword of his servant... What can I say, I had no elemental powers left, you gotta take things as opportunities arise! Needless to say that it was very fulfilling to see the blade stick out of his body after it turned to sandstone (as every inhabitant of this world does after death).
This is typical for the very fluent and dynamic gameplay of "Son of Nor", you make your plans up on the fly and intuitively improvise your attack strategy. The very intuitive and responsive controls almost always do what you want to do (except for the lack of ability to rotate things). This is done much better than in "The Force Unleashed".
The checkpoint saving system is subtle and smart; a big improvement over the quicksave failure in games like "Jedi Knight / Outcast / Academy" which ruined the gameflow for me.
The production value is good – for being an indie title. Nonetheless some people might have to get used to some "cheesiness factor". But once you figured out how to build bridges out of sometimes very strangely twisted bodies of the lizards, you will even begin to nourish a secret love for the Sarahuls.

I've got this game for free during winter event and i didn't want to complain much but... its not that good.
I've reserved playing this game until it was done, though i did get a glimpse of it month's ago and quite frankly i don't see a lot of changes, except perhaps intro video.
Each part of the game lasts for about 5-10 minutes because game engine just can't handle bigger levels. It can barely handle even those tiny portions of the game filled with few enemies and items to smash and throw about.
Character animations are non existent, from running to talking it looks unpleasant, like it was made years ago. I would rather play it in first person view just to avoid seeing those weird running stickmen hands and legs. In fact - it should've been first person, like Dark Messiah. Though i guess we would have to stare at those horrible, motionless, low polygon npc faces then... sigh.
There are bugs, there are slowdowns, the story doesn't make any sense whatsoever, with unknown names, places and characters introduced for no specific purpose. Oh that person cared for someone and betrayed us? Its fine - he's dead now. Lizards want humans dead? Humans saved by birds? Birds gone away? Long faces whatstheirnames saved humans again? Why is it so unnecessarily complicated, convoluted and why do you pour so much info in the first 5 minutes of the game? Surely there are better ways to present the world and its story than that?
There's also a disconnect between scenes, music, sounds and characters which almost gives me one of those "omg how did it make onto steam?!?" vibes. Its not THAT bad, but at times you can almost feel bad coding, graphics, animations and characters voices misaligning into something resembling "Garry's Incident" or "Slaughtering Grounds". Though, i will mention it again - its not THAT bad.
I suppose what i am trying to say - its not finished. Its unpolished. Its bugged, its laggy, the dialogues are horrendous and the animations (except levitation, which looks pretty neat) will make your eyes bleed. The game is just too ambitious for its own good.
Bigger levels, first person view, scratch the story, make it a sandbox with terraforming, telekinesis, fireballs. Heck - a multiplayer arena with all of those same spells would've been amazing. Sadly - no one is playing this game in co-op, the server list is empty.
I suppose i could've overlooked bad story if the game had bigger levels and better animations, or i could've overlooked tiny levels and bad animations if the story was amazing but (and i am sorry for that) - i can't recommend this.

The LEGO Movie game is just like any other LEGO game, except for once it caters to people who actually like playing with LEGOS.
Instead of just breaking stuff and combining it into whatever you need, now sometimes you need to find instructions for more complex LEGO creations and then play a mini-game that gets you more involved with the building and let's you appreciate how much effort goes into these creations a bit more.
The "job" system also caters a bit more to real LEGO fans since the jobs are the kind you get from normal LEGO sets, firemen, builders, wild west gunmen and cops.
The real difference from other LEGO games is the "completionist" part. This game "only" has 75 gold brick, but after the nightmare of collecting the brutal 250 gold bricks in LEGO Marvel, this is a much less frustrating and more fun experience.
Gone are the terrible racing games that were either too easy or too hard, gone are the overly long and convoluted quests for a measly gold brick. This is something I sincerely welcome and I really hope this stays this way.
You only have to get all the collectibles and all the rest of the gold bricks are in the bonus room, that's it and that's how I hope it stay for the next game.
The fact that I'm probably going to buy a LEGO set after playing this game speaks volumes on how this game is about the love for LEGOs.

A great Indie title which I have owned for a while now. From a fairly small team comes this title which allows you to terraform, use telekinesis and manipulate your environment to swing things in your favour! Multi-platform, extensive co-op/multiplayer modes as well as co-op story mode with lots of challenging levels and puzzles. Combine magical powers with your friends and make fire tornados! Who wouldn't want to be able to use their mind to throw boulders at your enemies' head?
Gameplay?
The gameplay reminds me a lot like Jedi Academy while the visuals and the feel of the game makes me think of Stargate, Indiana Jones and Prince of Persia. Not a bad combination! It forces you to think about your surroundings and the abilities you have to hand in order to defend yourself. Unlike a lot of action-adventure games, you don't wield weapons but have to use elements and take advantage of your surroundings. You can kind of use weapons, but not physically hold a spear, but take it from a Sarahul's hand (the bad guys in this game, like big lizard men) and throw it right back at them. There is also freedom to choose different paths as to how you're going to proceed to your goal. Are you going to go stealth? Go in blazing and take on an army of lizard guys? Flank strategically with your friends? Up to you. For an Indie game title, it's not as linear as you would expect. I believe there is roughly 12+ hours of gameplay available single player and/or co-op, plus PvP arenas and a few other multiplayer game modes.
Cool stuff, GADGETS!
Another thing which really caught my eye was the amount of gadgets you can use in this game. It's compatible with Oculus Rift (although I believe there are some tweeks needed), Tobii EyeX which is an eye sensor bar and finally, EPOC Emotive which enables you to almost literally control the game with your mind! Other than being awesome features, it really broadens the market to other avid gamers who may not be so physically able to enjoy games. Having eyetracker software, and being able to train your hardware to the thought patterns of your brain is truly astonishing. Again, I don't know of many Indie games that enable you to do this. So kudos to Stillalive Studios!
Overall?
Well, I can't be the judge of this game only you can. With anything I would always advise to check out some gameplay of something first and this would be no exception. I personally think it's a really cool little game and a bit of a diamond in the rough. The team at Stillalive have been awesome to everyone by listening to feedback, developer diaries to keep you up to date with changes and to give you a chance to express your views whether they're positive or negative. You can tell a lot of hard work and love went into this title and even if the game isn't your cup of tea, you'd still want to support the developers.

- Fine music fitting the game
- Clever puzzles – some of the puzzles seemed frustrating at first, but once you realize the principle of solving them, you will feel a sense of accomplishment (at least I did) – the puzzles are based mostly on perceiving the physics of the environment and interaction with it

The game is basically one continuous trip (not classic levels) with checkpoints on the way. The one negative that comes to mind is its length. On the other hand, if you want to spend an evening or two with something interactive (rather than watching stupid movies), Sign Motion is a good alternative.

Alright, this will be a long review, so bear with me as I go through many parts of the game and how it works.
RotMG is a fast-paced bullet hell with the aspects of an MMO RPG. What makes it unique is that it is in birdseye view, so you get a top down look at your character. Second, the graphics don't seem too great to many new players. This is so new players with bad computers can still play the game without facing too much difficulty. The game is simple.
Kill enemies, level up, get loot, and play as a plethora of characters from medieval times that we all know and love. Ranging from knights to wizards to archers and even mystics, this game has every aspect of a game that would have an in depth character selection. When you launch the game, there are SO many bots that will spam the crap out of you in the Nexus. Just ignore them and play the game. Sure, it doesn't make the game seem all too great, but that's just chat spammers for you. Getting into the game is what might be difficult. I tried to get so many friends to play, and they all quit whenever they die after a few times because they feel like all their hard work is lost. However, when they look at white stars with top tier gear, they want that level of gear. They want to persevere to prosper. But they feel as if their efforts are futile when they die to a pirate. You need to understand that YOU WILL DIE 100% GUARANTEED! No matter what you do, no matter where you go, if you play the game casually, you will die. And that's ok because you learn from your experiences. It's similar to real life. You may not understand what an adult is trying to tell you, but they know what they're doing. It's called "wisdom." It means they've been through it before and understand how things will turn out. Same goes for RotMG. You may not understand so many things, but give it some time, and you'll understand it so well. I promise, it is worth the time.
The immense joy you are filled with when you max a character, the heart ache you'll feel when you die with a character you worked so hard for, and the SATISFYING feeling of getting great loot for your character. It's all in the game.
This game is SO worth the time you put into it. I promise you it seems like a pay-to-win game, but here's the thing; there is NO WINNING in this game. There is simply achieving and prospering. You don't lose, you die. You don't win, you carry on. There is no end to this game. Heck yeah, you can buy all the items for real money, but a company that has a F2P game needs to make bank somehow. It took me about 2 years to be pretty dang good at the game, and I'm not even the best. You might turn out to be a prodigy that steps up and makes a change in how the world views the game. You might be the guy that struggles just trying to fight simple enemies. But all in all, everyone shares similar experiences with the game, whether it's death, success, satisfaction, friendship, etc.
OVERALL, I would highly recommend playing this game. If it's not your type of game, then who cares? There are so many other games out there that you could try. It's all in your decisions and how you carry on. Sorry for the elaborate review, but I thought it'd help give newcomers a view point of someone who's played the game for almost 1,000 hours. I hope you all enjoy the game as much as I did. I should probably get back to playing :)

Actually pretty incredible! Sleeping Dogs is an open world GTA-style game set in a China-esque city. While I dislike the GTA games, I actually greatly enjoyed Sleeping Dogs, due to the different and interesting setting (how many games take place in modern day China?) and the more enjoyable style of gameplay that rewards not being a crazed homocidal maniac just as much as shooting and crashing into everything/everyone in sight. It's also much more focused on melee fights with a fun combo/reversal system that is fun to play and watch thanks to great animations. The game itself is also gorgeous, with good animations, textures and especially rain effects. I would actually stop doing quests and just travel around the city whenever it started raining due to how pretty everything looked. The main questline managed to be relatively interesting the whole way through, and fortunately really managed to shine at the ending, and in general the side quests proved to be fairly interesting distractions, though some of the repetive side quest goals weren't terribly fun, notabl the races, though that could be thanks to my non-interest in race games in general. Overall, everything just works very well; Driving controls nicely, melee combat is fun, gunplay works, chase scenes are fun, freerunning stuff is fun, graphics are excellent, voice acting is sufficient to good, and the storyline is interesting if a bit basic. Recommended very much if you like GTA-style games, and worth a try even if you don't like them. Free on Games with Gold Xbox 360 right now! (Jan 1 - Jan 15, 2013)

Wyrmsun is a free to play RTS game published by Andrettin. It takes you back to the past were pixelated RTS games were still a thing.
It plays fairly similar to your average RTS game from centuries ago, gather resources, get workers, build farms, get soldiers, build farms, raid other players, and build farms. Did I say build farms?
The interface is also average for an RTS of this kind. You got your unit portraits, their stats, and their abilities at the bottom. You recources, food, and menu at the top. Pretty simple stuff.
The AI is ok, I had problems like enemy workers trying to go to my base camp to harvest resources that they do not have at their place. I mean, why would you go through a whole battalion to get a pile of stone for your guys? Sometimes the AI abandons their base leaving only the workers to fend off for themselves. The pathfinding is bearable at best.
There is an item system, but only certain units can only store stuff in their inventory. Most commonly, the "Heroes" are the only ones that can store items. They can be found in the campaign, or you can make your own custom hero in the Quests menu. These custom heroes can accompany you in various singleplayer modes, which means it can keep it's exp and use it's abilities from one match to another. The most common items that are in the game are food from the farms you built, healing potions from the temple, and dropped equipment by the enemy.
The magic system is interesting. From what I experienced, half of the units have mana which they can use when they get an ability when they level up. Which is unique considering every other RTS, only important characters and heroes are the only ones that could level up.
The plot is meh, some guys are trying to find a new home while the other is doing mercenary work for the guys that hire them.
Sound effects are pretty good, it really sounds like an old school game.
Multiplayer is basically local, unless your one of the guys that can fill out a whole IP for the guy hosting it.
You can mod the game, that is already a plus. I can already feel the crazy ideas coming out of my brain. [Althought there are reports of crashing mods due to updates]
There is a map editor in the main menu, which I can say is pretty easy to get into.
Finally, there is also a tech tree for the different factions in the game. You can aqcuire tech points from the campaign so you can unlock more buildings and units for your specific faction. But from my experience, you can only use the tech for the campaign.
I find it interesting that each individual unit has a unique name. Well, one more point for immersion.
Still confused about the grand strategy mode.
Overall this game is actually pretty great for a free to play title.

CONS: dialogue is passable at best, AI can be suicidal at times, grand strategy mode is confusing (for me at least), some missions are over very quickly leaving you wondering why they were made in the first place and finally there are still some bugs that need urgent attention namely that some missions do not register as complete when the objectives are met (i.e. emmisary escorted to area A and Hero to point B, objectives not ticked off in game) leaving you stranded on a map with no way to progress and having to start all-over again.
Over-all though, great value for money and will certainly fulfill your yearning for the rts games of your youth. 6/10
