Town of Salem brings the crazy role-countering party game “Mafia” onto browsers/digital screens, and despite its drab presentation, proves to be dastardly sinister fun.
Town of Salem is very simple to explain to those who often go out on parties. It’s basically Mafia/Werewolf, except as a video game! It takes the advantage of complex mechanics (that can easily be done in games versus as a party game) to elevate Town of Salem as a much more dynamic game. There are a lot more countering between the roles, which means there’s a whole lot more to keep up with. This is what makes Town of Salem a much more fresh experience.
There’s so many things to keep track of too. You’ve got escorts that can distract players, jailors that can interrogate others and execute them, there’s just so much going on. There’s Last Wills, a Serial Killer role, neutral roles that can get caught in the crossfire, unique Town roles besides just “Citizen”, and so much more. If you plan on playing it’s competitive matchmaking, you have to keep every aspect of the game in mind.
Add Werewolf in the mix, and you get pure insanity. That doesn’t mean you have to play with the Werewolf roles, however. Town of Salem allows for custom matches where you can pick the roles, which will definitely make for a lot more creativity and unique game modes to pop up.
How ever, it has to be said that it’s presentation is really, really bad. If it’s loading times, far from serviceable graphics and bad UI makes it a lot less appealing. While the loading times aren’t as bad as the browser version, and the graphics can be more of a nitpick at this point, the horrible UI can not be excused. It takes so many clicks to do actions that could had easily be cut down, the various windows for the game are placed all over, and the UI while in a game completely clutters the screen. It’s a good thing you can do something about the in-game one though, but those with low monitor resolutions are not going to have a good time.
It’s visuals are honestly subpar, but it can be excused for it being a flash game (Why it is a flash game in the first place will forever confuse me). However, what I found really grating was it’s cheap and horrible music/sound design. It’s music was generic as hell, and the sound effects were cheesy and annoying at best. It’s easier if you just tune into your own music while playing.
The microtransactions generally consist of mainly cosmetics, so it’s not that big of a deal. However, the BS that is the scrolls are completely obnoxious. Purchasing scrolls allow you to get a higher chance of a certain role, which completely ruins the RNG factor that is picking the roles in Mafia. It stoops the gameplay very low, and it’s really sad that people will have less of a chance to pick roles people have put scrolls towards.
However, in practicality, the scrolls end up actually being a total waste of coins, because you’ll probably not get the role anyway. It basically turns what is a game-breaking item into a useless item at the same time.
So let’s talk about organizing the game as a party game. It can work, but it’s ultimately a huge disappointment. There’s no private lobbies, meaning if you have less than 15 people, you will have to play with randoms. Due to the messy UI and bad friend system getting in the way, sending up lobbies can become a hectic mess. Sometimes, it doesn’t update whatever or not a player is online, meaning sending them an invite is virtually impossible.
The Steam version (besides loading times and the fact that it isn’t free) is fine. You get some in-game currency and better loading times since you’re running on a client versus a browser, but if you don’t want to pay for an experience like this, you really don’t have to get it on Steam. Also, it does not save any of it’s settings on the Steam version, which means I always have to toggle “No Fullscreen” and “Mute Music” settings when I get the chance.
But besides that, what can I say? It’s Mafia. Despite the disappointing aspects of the game, I still find it to be a solid time killer and definitely a complex and entertaining game. Tarnation indeed.

TLDR:
Game has potential.  Already decent, although very buggy.  If you had even a passing interest in Guns Of Icarus, you will enjoy this game.  Thrives off of the variety in games even in the same gamemode.  more gamemodes would mean more playability.  obsurd scenario modes and workshop modding would give this game infinite playability.
PROS
This is a game i can get behind.  It comes off as guns of icarus, but without the one crippling flaw.  the que system.  Guns of icarus you'd join a stacked lobby and wait 30+ minutes to get into a game you were bound to lose.  here we have a server browser.  that doesnt exactly reak of balanced games, but just as with games like TF2, it works.  veterans and mods to certain servers can usually sort out teams relatively well between games.
Personally, my other grief with GOI was that there was no player interaction, and there was a serious lack of variety to games.  so player interaction.  well in this game you can board enemies ships.  broadsiding a ship with a volley of cannons and then boarding them is a pretty strong strategy if you can pull it off quick enough.  this already gives rise to more variety between games, as it is highly dependant on how your captain wants to fight, but the devs have gone a step further by adding in land combat in the CTF gamemode, as well as making it possible to take pot shots with your musket at enemy crewmembers on their ship.  They even have a headhunter achievement for landing headshots on the enemy captain.
CONS
I have high hopes for this game in the future.  it still very much feels like early access.  constant bugs plague the game, although none of them make it unplayable.  the sword combat is about as clunky as it could possibly be, and the firearms are only slightly better.  one mechanic inparticular outshines them all in ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥tery, however.  and that would be fire.  it sprouts up from god knows what (I probably shouldnt have to guess at that after 30+ hours), kills a person or 2, destroys all your sails, and then makes part of your ship untouchable until you either slowly put it out with flippin 2 oz buckets, or you sink.  whichever happens first.  I dont think it should be removed entirely, (watching sails burn up looks cool as hell), but it needs MASSIVE tweeks, and it shouldn't be a guessing game on what starts a fire.  Lastly, the british.  it's funny and silly for the first hour.  but the british voices just get annoying after that.  minor grief there, but still...
IN CLOSING:
I touched on variety as a plus before, and I strongly think that is what this game will sell off the back of.  If they stick to what they have, they'll sell a few more copies on launch and it'll be cool.  If they expand the number of gamemodes, make a few obsurd senarios just for the fun of it, and open the game to the steam workshop and modding, this will be one hell of a game.
Excited to see where this project goes.  good luck devs

Full Video Review -
In Randal's Monday you play, as you would expect Randal and yes, it's Monday. Randal himself is a very dis-likable character, take a lazy, borderline alcoholic smart♥♥♥♥♥ Then add some kleptomania and finally make them a sociopath and there you have Randal. Randal is certainly that drinking buddy we all had growing up that we didn't really like but was good to have at a party but a whole lot worse.
The story starts in a bar as Randal, his best friend Matt and Matt's girlfriend Sally are drinking to celebrate their engagement. While Sally is away, Matt shows Randal the engagement ring that he got for a Dorito from a homeless guy and so enters lord of the rings nods left, right and center. After too much to drink and throwing up in the alley Matt, drops his wallet with the ring of power inside, Randal being the kleptomaniac picks the wallet up and keeps it for safe keeping but strangely doesn't give it back the same night. In the morning Randal finds that a series bad things happen to him, mainly his own fault mind you and through more story which I won't spoil, you discover that the ring is cursed. Soon Randal finds himself trapped in a time loop, repeating that same Monday over and over except there's one difference. Everything he does changes the past present and future so while he repeats the same Monday over and over the things he has direct contact with can be affected by him. An example of this is the fire escape next to his apartment, early on in the game you use that to avoid your landlord and the whole thing collapses after it does every Monday from that point the fire escape remains broken.
I'll be the first to admit point and clicks are not my thing unless they have a great setting and story, their repetitive nature grinds on me very fast. In terms of mechanics Randal's Monday is no different that other point and clicks, throughout each location there is an array of objects and people to interact with. Usually this takes the form of a primary interaction and secondary interaction. Primary interactions are where Randal actually physically does something like initiating a conversation or stealing something. Secondary interactions are almost always where Randal will make an observation about the object or person while this can be as simple as stating what an item is sometimes these observations will contain clues as to what to do with that item or person. If your unsure of which objects are interact-able you can hold down spacebar which will light up all interact-able objects but not all of them will be important.
Movement between locations is done via the subway system. At locations you can walk between rooms or if your impatient you can double click the entrances to instantly load the location. One thing I really enjoyed about Randal's Monday was that the game self deprecating an example of this can be seen when using the subway on the load screen. When the load screen comes up you get helpful hints at the bottom of the screen and while there are some that pertain to the game often they are hints like 'upgrading your bases benefits all your troops' and other references to different video game genres. The game makes fun of being a point and click and it makes the whole game quite endearing in a way.
As with many point and clicks, Randal's Monday is filled with puzzles, these take the form of finding ways to acquire items and achieve your goals. Randal being a kleptomaniac will often have to steal items however usually someone is around watching you so you'll have to devise creative ways to distract them. This usually involves using other items you've 'acquired' sometimes you'll even need to combine items in your inventory to form new items which are often wacky and fun like the extendable duck hanger. One of my biggest dislikes of the game is the inventory. The inventory is done like a comic book which while it is aesthetically pleasing, in terms of functionality its a pain. To combine items you have to click on item on the inventory and then click the one you want to try and combine it with. However if it doesn't work both are then deselected, this means that say the item you want to experiment with is on the second page of the inventory and all your other items are on the first pages, you have to keep moving back and forth between sections to try and combine items. It makes the whole notion of trying ideas out laborious and its seriously not only a time drain but a drain on patience too.
The puzzles tended to annoy me as well. Now I understand I'm not great at point and clicks but I'm a pretty logical person. Yet there were a number of occasions where I literally had no idea what to do. The game doesn't really do a good job of giving you an idea about how to get things done which is fine most of the time but occasionally you have to do something where I thought I would never have guessed to do that with that item. Luckily there is a walk-through hint system in the game you can access which will tell you what to do step by step however it will not only make the game way too easy, it'll show up on your steam achievements that you used the help guide. In my opinion they should have had a decent hint system in the game but not the almost cheat sheet that they went for. After all it's good the game forces you to actually use your brain to think how to solve things but one thing I learned is that I myself have no ingenuity what so ever.
Where Randal's Monday shines is in it's character, humor and frequent references to video games, sci fi and general geek culture. There isn't one location or conversation in the game that isn't flooded with funny quotes and nods. The whole main story itself is a nod to several cult sci fi and fantasy films. While the game never made me laugh out loud, you cannot help but smile at the various references throughout and the characters in the game do give you cause to have a good chuckle to yourself. In conversations you have choices available to you and each often contains some funny joke that references some film or video game.
Speaking of the characters they are all pretty well thought out. Randal is a very dis-likable character however it's his very nature that requires him to be the protagonist of the game. It's because Randal is a sociopath and a kleptomaniac that its acceptable to steal the things you need and screw over people who get in your way. Narratively it not only would it not make sense for a decent guy to be doing these things but anyone with actually sanity would probably not be able to handle the events that take place. While the whole game is tongue in cheek in its humor and characters, it does have some important messages throughout.
The game looks great, its cartoon grimy appearance works really well and everything looks well drawn. Sound wise it also hits top marks, not only for the sound effects but the voice acting is surprisingly good throughout. Yes it's a little cheesy sometimes but that's usually because its supposed to be and I have to say that the writing of the game is very well done. Often Randal will break the forth wall in a funny way with one occasion telling the player that its their fault his life is getting worse and he often remarks at the player when your trying to do something that's not going to work by saying 'if you think that'll work you need to stop playing and take a rest'.
The characters, story, culture references and breaking of the fourth wall all make for a very enjoyable experience. Randal's Monday is certainly an enjoyable point and click adventure and its well written dialogue and nods to video games and movies alike make the play through well worth it. After installing the game, it will take you about half an hour to get past all of the EA login crap for the first time.  After that (and after you get used to the incredibly cheeky way that they swap the 'okay' and 'visit store' buttons all the time), you're confronted with an unskippable cutscene introducing you to Paradise City by the one female presence in the game; speaking in (what is supposed to be) a seductive voice whilst saying stuff like "here's the observatory".  It's ridiculous and cringe-worthy, and pretty much sums up EA's attitude towards women here.
Once you finally start playing, it's pretty much all good fun.  You can free drive around until you're in the mood to start a race by stopping at the traffic lights, and then you're dropped into either a A->B sprint, a 'takedown' contest where you've got to smash up as many cars as possible, the 'wanted man' event where two cars are trying to take you down whilst you try to get from A->B (my favourite), and finally the 'stunt' mission where you've got to jump and spin and do stuff to hit your target score.  After an ever-increasing number of these events, you unlock a new car - until there's no more missions left - at which point, I guess, you just free roam.
It's fun, but very repetitive, and I found myself having the most fun just by seeing how long I could go without crashing, and believe me- it's harder than it sounds.  This isn't a game that will entertain you for all that long; you'll have to make your own entertainment, so buy at the correct price-point accordingly.
Definitely not a wholehearted recommendation, but it's okay.  Pros outweigh the cons.

Bastion is a very unique game. The story line is extremely captivating, and it's easily one of the aspects I love most in this game.  The biggest thing that kept me playing this game was wanting to find out what happened next (I'm a huge story fan - A game with a good story is a game that I finished with love). The gameplay in this game is also something I haven't experienced before. The combat is very interesting, and there are a lot of small details in this game that I took for granted when I started playing this game (the automatic targeting system helps a lot more than I thought :p).
The Bastion area in the game is also new to me. Various buildings, all with unique purposes that all work together to make the gameplay more fun and interesting, and are all beneficial in their own special way. My favourite one easily being the Distillery, because I like being able to customize the bonuses I get for each level at any time, and always being able to unlock more and become even more powerful.
I really enjoyed being able to upgrade my weapons, and then choose from a pair of upgrades that you can go with. Differently from most games, you don't have to pick your way through an entire skill tree to get to cool abilities, and you also have the option of easily changing what you picked at any time. Though the normal skill tree is fun, and can easily change how you play a game, I always found it difficult to decide which tree to go with and worried about picking the one that I wouldn't like. What if I don't like freezing enemies, and I would rather burn them? What I like about this game is that you can easily switch between the weapon upgrade that you want to use. It may not affect gameplay as much, but I still found this to be more enjoyable.
Something I think this game lacks is replayability. When I first completed the game, I figured I would start again and continue trying to improve my character. I did it for a little while, and restarted the story, but it just didn't have the same effect. It wasn't quite the same after the first playthrough. It didn't have anything new, even in the new gametypes you unlock that allow you to continue with all your old gear. Another issue is that at that point, the game is pretty easy. You have all the best weapons, all with really good bonuses, and the difficulty is barely increased. It's possible that it gets more difficult farther in, because I didn't get far before I stopped the replay of the game.
*WARNING* WEAPON SPOILERS IN FOLLOWING PARAGRAPH
Another aspect I don't like about this game is that certain weapons are far better than others. I always found the fang repeater and the duel wielded guns (that I don't remember the name of) to be completely useless, having never used them outside of the practice zone for those weapons. For long range weapons, I used the bow until I got the Galleon cannon thing (that I also don't remember the proper name of) and then I used the calamity cannon once I got that. I never really had the need for anything else.
I also never used the skill associated with Q. It could be just me, but I was never particularly aware of it's existence and the only time I really used it was the occasional fight where that's what you were supposed to do. There's no particular emphasis to remind you to use it other than the constant finding of new abilities (which also never gives you the chance to use the old ones if you're like me), and there is no need to use it as I got through the game without too much trouble not using the Q skill.
I think the usage of Shrine Idols rather than an actual automatic difficulty increase is interesting, but I also never wanted to do it. I prefer a simple switch from Normal to Hard, rather than having to activate shrine idols and worry about which ones seem harder than others. This is probably just a personal thing, but the Shrine is always a building I avoided.
Overall, I don't think the game is worth $15. I wouldn't want to pay more than $7 for a game that I'm going to play less than 10 hours of, but when this game goes on sale (it seems to have some pretty big sales when it goes on sale too), I hope it gets into your Steam Library because you won't regret playing through this epic adventure.

So after checking the game and playing it completely,I think I can give a fair review of this game.
First of all, what you should expect when you play Foul Play:
You should like beat-em-ups with 2d sprites and all the cons that come with it (bad lineup,more "That should have hit"-moments).
You should like the general idea of a game having a theatre-like feeling.
However, you should not expect a hard game when playing. Elaboration on why later on.
Story: You control Sebastian Dashforth,who combined with his assistant Scampwick Steerpipe is presenting his life as a daemonologist on stage, re-enacting the main events of Dashforth's last 20 years. Not fearing to go into hand-on-hand combat he and Scampwick are fighting themselves through an lost city of egypt, cursed villages, underwater cities and a london in control of a cult.Fairly generous with the humor and honest (though you may not thank him for it) he will keep you interested to keep playing for a while.
Gameplay: You got six buttons that are important for playing, a weak,but fast attack,a stronger, slower attack which can bring enemies into the air or down from it, a jump, a button for improved abilities (which you learn at a higher level),a Showstopper ability granting you double the combo and double the audience approval when you activate it for a certain amount of time, a dodge and a block. The block is the most important of them,since you automatically counter blocked attacks from weaker enemies, letting you combo into them and from them. The enemies attacks have a clear indicator and you have a longer time to block or dodge an attack. You can play with someone else in Co-op and the only downside is that you have a combined health bar but seperated combo meters. You even get some upsides like a combo bonus if you activate showstopper at the same time. Enemies differ from higher health and exclusive gimmicks, like binding you if they hit on mummys.At the end of a level,you can get a charm if you did the challenges and a diary page if you collected enough stars.
Additional Pros:
-Replay value to 100% the game and to experiment on different gamestyles
-Unique Storyconcept and interesting Characters
-Soundtrack available with the game for no additional cost
-Attention to detail
Additional Cons:
-Low Playtime(any% about 3 hours, 100% 14 hours)
-Bugs like enemies thrown up into the air won't come down that easily at some points
-No Wiki
-No active lobby community,so no random multiplayer
All in all it is worth playing, and if you are a fan of unique concepts,than this game should be yours!

Sleeping Dogs is an open world action-adventure video game developed by United Front Games and Square Enix London. The game has you infiltrating the ranks of the Triads as undercover cop Wei Shen on an island off the mainland of Hong Kong.
Sleeping Dogs places a strong emphasis on hand to hand combat giving you the opportunity to unlock a wide range of different combos to be used while fighting. The combat very closely resembles that of Batman: Arkham City however doesn't feel as smooth, regardless anyone who enjoyed that series will probably enjoy this.
Every now and then you will be required to use a gun, personally I think they should have just focused on Melee combat either way the guns add some extra "action" to the game. A cover system is also included to allow you to avoid being shot and an interesting bullet-time mechanic allows you to vault over cover and take out enemies in slow-mo.
For those who like collecting stuff there is a large amount of collectable items in game to find while playing, you can also obtain several houses and dozens of clothing items, vehicles and furniture to customize your character.
Sleeping Dogs also features achievements which cover all aspects of the game including DLC content so I suggest, if you care for the achievements, you also pick up the DLC so you can 100% the game. I took roughly 35-40 hours to 100% the game and should a Steam sale come up I think you should play it too!
Pros
+ Fantastic graphics
+ Interesting story
+ Plenty of content
+ Enjoyable fighting
Cons
- Controls could be better
- Map could be bigger
- Achievements require DLC
Verdict: 8/10

Definitely one of the best open-world games I have played since GTA IV. Not only does it have a wonderful storyline but it really makes you feel like you are in HK. I was especially surprised how they were able to capture some elements such as the sound of the crosswalks (they make a different sound than the ones in America) and even the language people use (if I bumped into someone in an aggressive way, I would likely hear the same reaction as those that were made in the game).
If I had to nitpick at one thing though, it is that they did not include the MTR subway... arguably an identifying part of what Hong Kong is. EVERYONE uses the MTR and it is the main source of transportation here in HK. I don't mind the fact that not all the identifying land marks are shown and not every district is included, but the MTR is how everyone gets where they are and would have probably made amazing missions.
Nevertheless outstanding game. If you want a taste of what it feels like to be in HK, this is a good stepping point.

Kindred Spirits on the Roof benefits from a rather uncommon (in VNs at least) narrative structure, which positions the protagonist as a facilitator of other couples' relationships rather than one striving for her own. This allows players to get into the character's head as she tries to understand the intricacies and nuances of lesbian romance.
While the VN definitely delivers on feel-good high school yuri, it also reveals the difficulties it poses, especially in a conservative, collectivist society where presenting oneself as normal is paramount. It doesn't do so heavy-handedly, however, allowing the more intimate nature of the different stories to shine throug.
All in all, the different romances are quite engaging, and though some initially left me underwhelmed, I was rooting for all of them by the time the game drew to a close. With the vulnerabilities of first love compounded by what is frowned-upon, if not quite forbidden love, the story comes with emotional weight that can be surprising given its lighthearted mood.
All of this is supported by excellent sprites and a great soundtrack.

First and foremost; I genuinely enjoyed all aspects of this game. The art is nice and consistent throughout, the music is pleasant and I actually really like some of the songs, the story is nonsense at times but such is the nature of fiction so I think that the story actually culminates very well, and I really like some of the characters and the development of these characters throughout the story. It's a cute, yuri romance that I honestly feel could make a great anime. It has drama CDs and a spin-off manga, so why not?
Full disclosure; I am a fan of anime and I am a guy. A guilty pleasure of mine is Nekopara and I have Steins Gate for the Vita. I am a fan of visual novels because I watch a lot of anime that derives from them and I enjoy video games with a healthy amount of good narrative or visual novel-esque mechanics.
I heard about this game because I saw an article online about it being an "uncensored" visual novel on Steam. So I looked up some promotional images for the game and liked the art style. I'm no expert on visual novels, but I've seen images from visual novels where the art isn't consistent. This game has a very consistent manga-like art style that looks good against the game's backgrounds as well.
I went into the game thinking this would be another guilty pleasure like Nekopara but found that I was actually enjoying it for multiple reasons without the need of "ecchi" distractions. Right from the beginning the game grabs me with its openning song. I'm a sucker for some anime songs and there are a few songs with vocals in this game that I really enjoy. The lyrics are nice too and the vocalized songs are sung by one of the character's voice actors, which I think is nice. It's all a bit romantic in a shoujo-esque way, though I guess the game is yuri.
A major reason I was enjoying the game before the ecchi parts, and all-around regardless of anything ecchi; I really like the main protagonist. The protag's name is Toomi Yuna. She has a bit of a tomboy-ish, kuudere-ish vibe in that she is very self dependent and solemn with a "cool" or "cold" look to her character, which is why I found it adorable when she gets caught off guard occasionally and gets spooked or embarrassed, which shows that she is a complex character capable of feeling/showing natural emotions other than those typical of her apparant character. A fault that I hear about in many visual novels, or anime inspired by visual novels, or just anime in general is that the protagonist is unrelateable because they're a blank slate for you to imagine yourself in their shoes, or that the protag is just a terrible one-dimensional character whose involvement in the story boils down to plot for "PLOT"; as in they have all sorts of plot armor, plot hole inducing nonsense to make them important, and for some reason everyone then likes them or rivals them for some reason or another, so they are justified in all the "ecchi" stuff they get coming their way. But no. Kindred Spirits is way different from that nonsense. Toomi Yuna is a good protagonist. She has her own character which is developed and interesting and is part of a story within the game which is sort of seperate yet ties into her involvement with the other characters. What I mean by separate is that she isn't the focus of the game's ecchi story lines. Her own development stems more from her overcoming her own personal problems to become a stronger character that others rely on. Basically in a bad harem anime the protag gets unexplained plot power so that everyone is drawn to them. But in Yuna's case she isn't a harem protagonist, she's just trying to help other girls fall in love. This is difficult for Yuna because of her personal problems making her a bit of an introvert. But at her core she is a good person so she wants to help people when she knows she can. So she gets out of her comfort zone to help people. This makes her analyze herself and others and she comes to terms with why she was introverted in the first place so that she overcomes her problems. Basically she becomes a better character worthy of being relied on, capable of helping others, and therefore a justified protagonist.
So the focus of the plot is that Yuna helps girls who are lesbian find love. These girls have their own personalities told through their own narrative which explains how they feel about things, mainly their love interests. All the couples have their own quirks to them and whether or not you like the couples probably depends on the type of characters you like to see in a romance. People love shipping but tend to hate couples that don't meet their personal preferences. So obviously there were couples that I liked more than others for various reasons; some were cuter, some were more fun, some made more sense. But I liked the way the characters' narratives explained who they were and how they felt as characters. Regardless of what makes sense in the real world, I feel like all the couples are justified, more or less, by the characters' backstories, inner feelings, and interactions.
So this is an adult game in that it depicts relationships in a sexual way and shows implicit sex scenes that are more explained through narrative and vocals than the art itself. They do show boobs, but by todays anime standards it's fairly innocent. Even though it shows sex, it's not oversexualized. Some, if not most, anime today tends to be oversexualized even when it's not adult. Anime also tends to portray risque relationships. This game only really has one risque relationship. The entire game is "safe" in a vanilla sense. That's probably one of the reasons it wasn't censored by Steam. But I enjoy the art in general. I also just enjoy the development of the characters in the story. The sex scenes were "nice" but they were more like icing on the cake of the couples, sort of like a justification to the "ships" or a culmination of the romances naturally leading to intamacy.
So obviously I didn't explain the story too well as to avoid major spoilers. I just want to add that the voice acting helps define the characters along with the art and the narrative. Not everything is voiced, but you can sort of imagine how a character might say something in their voice as you're reading. The game also presents you with "choices" but they're very superficial and don't affect more than a sentence in the next line of dialogue. There is only one route that you simply read through, but visual novels offer more than manga and books because they have art, music, vocals, etc. The ghosts or "kindred spirits" are sort of a reason for the plot and a source for everything nonsensical that keeps reminding you this game is leading towards an ecchi finish line, but I still think that the writing in the lesbian relationships is done fairly well and keeps the relationships realistic or even relateable in most cases. I'm a guy, but I like romance too, so I don't even consider this a guilty pleasure; it's just a good romance story to me. So in all honesty you probably wont like all the characters but I'd say you should play it for the ones you will. Again, regardless of all the yuri romances that the other characters present you with, my favorite character is the protagonist Toomi Yuna. I'd play a non-ecchi game starring her, or watch a spin-off anime about her cooking (because she  likes to cook). If you're not sure whether you'll like the characters, just go to the game's official website, it has the rough bios on the characters. But if you're an anime fan who likes a bit of ecchi, likes a bit of romance, and likes "ships", this is the game for you.

Blackwake is an amazing cooperation oriented multiplayer game. COOPERATION is the KEY WORD. If you intend to play this game, you'll have to follow a few rules which i believe are mandatory to make sure everything goes fine.
1: LISTEN TO AND OBEY YOUR CAPTAIN.
2: DO NOT APPLY FOR CAPTAIN IF YOU DON'T KNOW HOW TO BE A CAPTAIN AND IF YOU DON'T HAVE A MICROPHONE. (You have several youtube tutorials available, and they will provide you with the knowledge necessary such as how to aim for an enemy ship and tactics. Also, microphone is absolutely mandatory to give orders.)
3: DO NOT SHOOT THE CANNONS UNLESS THE CAPTAIN TOLD YOU TO.
4: DO NOT TRY TO USE AN ALREADY MANNED CANNON. (Also, don't try to reload a cannon when someone is already doing it. You're getting in the way and that's annoying.)
5: IF ALL CANNONS ARE MANNED, DO SOMETHING ELSE. (There are other ways of getting points: running supplies, fixing the ship/sails, anti-sail swivels.)
6: IF YOU USE A CANNON, LEARN TO RELOAD IT QUICKLY.
7: IF YOU FIRE A CANNON, IT IS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY TO RELOAD IT IMMEDIATELY.
8: ON THE GALLEON, ONLY TWO (2) MEN TOPSIDE; EVERYONE ELSE ON THE BOTTOM DECK.
9: IF YOU CATCH FIRE, DO NOT RUN. (or you'll spread the fire to the whole ship.)
10: WHEN THE CAPTAIN SPEAKS, SHUT UP.
If you can't / don't want to follow these simple rules, you are not going to enjoy the game to it's full potential, and even worse: YOU'LL RUIN IT FOR EVERYONE ELSE. So please do not buy the game.
Now, if you're reading this, it most likely means you are not someone who is the target (=kids who don't / won't take the time to read / learn / listen about how this game is played) of my perhaps apparent frustration with the majority of the newcomers to Blackwake. I'll give you one last advice: AVOID THE GAME FOR A WEEK OR TWO AFTER A SALE. The majority of the players online are noobs who just bought the game, and a majority of these noobs are the kind of kids i told you about and it's very difficult to find a great captain with experience, making it even less likely to have an enjoyable game.
Once you've learned to be a part of a crew, you'll enjoy Blackwake very much. Have fun!

my point above is one of the many reasons why I say its very "real". the stress leading up to the confession, the worries about who is going to find out/maybe get mad, dealing with relationship issues/roadblocks, and most importantly, the trust and bond between two people is all covered in the game and written in extremely well.
Im giving this VN a 9.9 out of 10, the -.1 being that there isnt a way to forget about the whole story so id be able to read it again with genuine reactions from myself.

Two other minor annoyances for me were the menu structure (if you unlocked a new move during online play, you would have to go back all the way to the main menu - thus terminating your online game - to check what exactly you unlocked) and the fact that the game assumes you have a 360 gamepad. You can use your keyboard for it and it playes well with it, but all the tooltips etc. will only show the corresponding 360 pad key, not your keyboard key. If you can look besides those things, you will find Foul Play to be a very fun co-op experience.

If you like racing games, open worlds and totalling cars, this game is for you. However, If you don't like wasting your time trying to fix crashes, you might want to skip this one.
Once you fix the crashes, The game is fun. A HUGE city to drive around in, tons of races to compete in (Literally one on every street) and other fun little things to do like see how many innocent civilian's cars you can completely wreck in a minute.
About the crashes, They aren't too hard to fix. The fix(es) that worked for most people are:
-Disabling your webcam/selecting "none" under webcam in the game's config application.
-Setting the compatibility to something. It worked for me on Windows 95. Windows XP SP3 should work too.
-Disabling Anti-Aliasing(orhoweveryouspellit) You might not need to do this if the other options worked for you. (You can turn it off in the games config .exe too)
-Turning off the steam overlay, you might also not need to do this if the other options worked for you.
If none of the above worked, I hope you bought this game during a sale.

This was one of the original break-em and smash them racing games. My first introduction to the burnout series was Burnout : Revenge for the original xbox. Revenge was action packed and had very smooth game play. This game compared to it's predecessor is good but lacks fluidity and solid core mechanics. I would recommend Flatout Ultimate Carnage over this as it has more mini games, is less of a grind and for me was more engaging. Unlike Flatout, Burnout Paradise let's you explore the open world with some new vehicle types.
Paradise city is an open world crash-em-up racer. The
is pretty sound but can have some hiccups here and there regarding fluidity. You may drive around town freely and look and participate any event that is currently available to you. To start events, simply drive up to the event circle and press the gas and brake at the same time. These events come in the forms of Burnout Route/Burnout Ride (specifically for motorcycles) in which you race the clock for modified parts for your car, marked man which you race to a specific point while dodging enemy AI players trying to crash you, road rage mode where players are required to take out a certain amount of cars to proceed, stunt mode where air time, rolls and spins earn you points and finally Road Rules. There are two "modes" to road rules : time and showtime rules. Time is like a time attack whereas showtime requires the player to cause as much havoc to traffic as possible. The main sell point of this game is to do "take-downs", meaning taking out an opposing car. Hitting cars with a good momentum will send them on their way with a nice cinematic crash video effect.
Naturally, as you progress through the game, you are able to choose different cars in your garage given you've completed different events and tasks. There will be random race cars sometimes cruising through the streets waiting for you to take them down. There is no real set agenda regarding which car comes first or which car you see. Upon catching up to them taking these newly found cars out, these cars will be added to your garage. If you don't manage to take the car down or don't feel like it, chances are it will appear again (so don't panic)! There are quite a few car frames to choose from such as cars, vans, police cruisers, roadsters, classics, SUV's, F1, motorcycles and supercars. Cars have three criteria/ratings in regards to their performance. The three criterion's are speed, boost rating and strength. Different cars prefer different ways to acquire boost. Some vehicles rely on speed, others rely on aggressiveness to fill their meters while another category relies on stuns. There are other specific boost types but are very particular to a small amount of cars. Some cars have such good performance (I'm talking the special cars you acquire way after) that they do not have boost.
The
are actually quite good and some of the crash effects and visuals are really nice to watch. Although be it easy to knock some players out, it is still satisfying to see everything break apart. The
are pretty good and do a decent job immersing the player. Car sounds and crashes have a pretty good range and don't sound all the same.
The game like I said is nice to play (with different vehicles such as motorcycles) but in my personal opinion is missing that umph factor when hitting opponents. The damage scheme is great, however the impact engine doesn't let you feel how hard you are hitting another car. Not only that, every time you do get a hit off the game sort of stops for a scenematic. I like fluidity; the fact that Flatout gives you a chance to recover whereas Burnout doesn't is up to the gamer to choose the preferred style. For that reason I would have to recommend Flatout Ultimate Carnage over this game. If you like what you see then I recommend it, if you want a racing game with a bit more depth and challenges I'd go for Flatout. It's an average game in my opinion without a speedometer (unlike flatout)!
RATING : 7/10

I'm usually not to much fond of bashers. They tend to be repetitive and quickly boring, but Foul Play builds on the genre and manages to avoid most of the things the annoy me with other titles. It's theatrical structure is a perfect options that allows for a lot of different monsters, settings and situations. The writing is full of humour and wits. The game avoids the too obvious "save the princess" goal, which is a very good point.
The other thing I like about that theatrical structure is that it allows for a choice of gaming length depending on the time you have. Only a few minutes to play? Play an act and move on to other things. Wanna go for longer sessions? Do a full play in one run and you're good to go.
Overall a nice game, great universe and graphic style, good gameplay with some twists in the genre. Clearly worth its price anytime, an absolute best buy when on sale. Go get it!

Town of Salem is a game very similar to "Werewolf"
Like in Werewolf you are randomly assigned one of 33 unique roles at the start of a game. To help I will go over some of them! I would do all but these reviews got character limits.
Town (aka the Good Guys)
Investigator (Inves): The best detective force the town can muster. Despite this he is unable to tell the difference between a Doctor, a Serial Killer, and a Vampire.
Sheriff (Sher): Able to figure out who is a member of the Mafia, who is a Serial Killer, and who is a Werewolf. However, most of the time you will only visit town members and the leader of the Mafia who is "Not Suspicious".
Lookout (LO): You are the ultimate stalker. Each night you can see who dares to visit senpai. Of course it would be too hard to see if senpai actually went out of his house that night and where he went.
Spy (Spy): This guy is the nosiest character in the game. His special power is to see people's private messages. And see what mafia says at night. Of course mafia is aware of this and won't talk at night ever.
Doctor (Doc): Your job is to predict who the mafia and/or Serial Killer will attempt to kill at night. However, the Inves will inevitably accuse you of being a Serial Killer and you will die. Also don't forget that you can save evil people!
BodyGuard (BG): Simliar to the doctor but you are more about prevention than treatment. You wait outside senpai's house and if anyone ever visits him with murderous attmpts. At that point you take destiny into your own hands and kill senpai's assassin, but it comes with a cost, your own life. Of course, you likely just killed the vigilante and senpai was actually evil.
Jailor (Jailord): One of the most powerful Town members. You can detain one suspect every night and exectute them if you desire starting on the second night. If you detain a Serial Killer and don't execute them they will kill you. So naturally you will jail the Serial Killer in the first night before you can execute them.
Vigilante (Vigi): You take justice into your own hands. Starting Night 2 you can shoot anyone of your choice. Naturally anyone you shoot will be immune to your attack or a fellow ally. Eventually you will eventually go mad and just shoot people randomly, oddly enough this normally works, but please don't. If you shoot a fellow townie you will kill yourself the next night.
Veteran (Vet): You have the unique ability to prevent yourself from death for three nights. How so? Shoot everyone that dares step on your lawn. There are three ways to play vet. 1. Kill a town member and have everyone will hate you. 2. Kill an evil member and town will praise the very ground you stand on. 3. Get killed because you didn't alert everyone will think you are mentally handicapped.
Vampire Hunter (VH): You are the ultimate counter to Vampries. You are completely useless against Mafia, Serial Killers, Werewolves, and Arsonists. But hey if a vampire visits you or you visit them they are dead. Just be sure to do your work before you are outnumbered 10 to 1.
Medium (Med): You have the ability to talk to the dead at night. Of course this is irrelevant as you will die on the first night. What most n00bz don't know is you have the ability to talk to one of the living at night when you are dead, and inform that person of all the information the dead know, which is usually incorrect suspicions.
Escort (Esc): Described as a "Beautiful woman" in game, but despite this, you can still recieve this role even if your character is an old man. Your job is to "roleblock" people by "occupying" them during the night preventing them from doing anything at night. The downside with this role is you are the most likely to get AIDS along with the consort.
Retributionist (Ret): You can revive a people from the dead and are limited to one revive for whatever reason. Yes you heard me, you make zombies. The real question is why the town doesn't lynch you for witchcraft when this is vaguely based on the Salem witch trials. Either way you will either die before you can revive a half decent role or you revive a great role that secretly went afk when they died, wasting your revive. Congratz you are useless now.
Mayor (Mayor): You are the mayor of the Town of Salem. For some reason nobody knows that you are the Mayor of the town. Upon activating this you can ruin the fun for everyone by demanding everyone's roles and lynching everyone. You will be the target for assassination, but literally everyone who can protect you can so you basically are immortal and can get anyone you want killed, as long as there are more than 2 other townies to be your meatshield.
Transporter (Trans): Possibly the most disasterous role when put in the wrong hands. You can switch the position of two people, for example if you transport "Bill" and "Bob" anyone who wants to attack Bill will instead visit Bob. This does sound great, but you will inevitably get vigilante to shoot an ally, investigator to accuse the wrong person, and so much confusion nobody could get lynched.
Mafia (Bad Guys)
All mafia members know who the other mafia members are along with their roles.
GodFather (GF): You control who gets killed by mafia. This jerk will force you (the loyal mafioso) to visit the alerting veteran taking your life, despite all of your protesting. Feel free to report him for gamethrowing.
Framer (Frame): Your job is to visit somebody each night and the inves and sheriff will see them as members of the mafia. This is great unless there is a spy, in which case every person you frame is proven NOT to be mafia, meaning by doing anything you are actually making it more likely to lose. Good job.
Consigliere (Consig): You are the older brother of the inves. Unlike your counterpart you know the exact role of whoever you visit. However, because there just might be a spy you won't share any of the information because that would reveal that there is a consig. Of course the one time that you do tell mafia what people are there actually is a spy and you will get lynched just for claiming to be an investigator.
Blackmailer (BM): You have the ability to force people not to talk for the duration of one day, however they are allowed to vote to hang you for whatever reason. Oddly enough you are actually able to Blackmail yourself. You must be very convincing.
Disquiser (Disq): This character is interesting. You can choose to switch between your target if they die at night, making it appear that you died. You can do this if the town starts to suspect you for an easy escape. However, this strategy does have one counter. The victim writing his name on a piece of paper.
Forger (Fgr): Are you able to rewrite the wills of people who die. You could forge the investigators results and prove the mafia "innocent". That is assuming that you know that the person mafia is targetting is the investigator, he does actually die that night, and your ability to write a convincing fake will from scratch in the span of less than 20 seconds. Other than those "few barely noticable restrictions" you have a lot of "utility".
Janitor (Jan): Ironically enough Janitor is widely considered the most powerful non-killing mafia role. You visit someone who dies and then nothing is known about them, literally nothing. You also steal a copy of their will because that would be too hard for anyone without the Janitor's expertise. You are, however, countered by the one medium that mangaged not to die on the first night and he will tell the town everything you tried to hide, making your paper stealing expertise worthless.

Town of Salem is an excellent game for all the people that love communication, investigation, deception, deduction and decision making. Thanks to the high variability of roles and "All Any" game mode, every experience is different. The game itself is cool, new roles are added time to time as well as items and game balance.
The most important part of the game is the social factor and knowing exactly what can all the roles do and what loopholes do exist. Outside-the-box thinking and cold reading are the best metagaming tools you can master. And this is exactly what I love most about it. Although sometimes it can backfire or mislead you as well.
However, the most problematic part of the game are the players, since sometimes they are simply not smart or they are too indecisive. Vigilante is probably the most dangerous role to give to a bad player. But bad players are players too and one must simply know how to effectively interact with them.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who loves either to crack cases or manipulate others. It is also very useful to be both assertive and convincing, for some roles at least. There are also tonz of unspoken rules that one needs to learn to understand the social factor properly.
This game isn't just probability and statistics of various combinations, robotic thinking is ineffective here. It's game of trust, lies, predictions, emotions (although the best way of playing is not to care about them but they are awesome to use against people who do listen to them), tricks, manipulation and much much more.

The immersion of this game is unbelievable.
I own Saints Row and and GTA V, and I very much prefer this game over those.
Where the others try to win you over with high graphics and crazy missions, this game concentranted on solid, solid gameplay and immersion.
The controls of the cars are great.  The handbrake slows time slightly, giving you control around those tight curves and drifts.  When I do crash, I find myself saying, 'oh, I should have seen that', or, 'I took that turn too sharp', instead of 'Why don't these cars control better??'; the latter of I'm always thinking when playing GTA.
The immersion is amazing.  Walking through the nightmarkers, stall sellers try to call you over, trying to sell you their goods; if they are a food seller, the sounds of sizzling, rambuctiious kitchen float to you.  People walking around are varied.  You can catch snippets of conversation all around you, and everyone wears different clothes, hair, and even posture.  People are lighting cigarettes, carrying grocery bags, purses, talking on cell phones.  Bumping into them causes them to drop their things and yell at you, usually in cantonese.
One of the really small things I love is the snippets of Cantonese thrown into cutscenes, with subtitles so you can follow along.
Cutscenes blend into gameplay seamlessly.  And the COMBAT.  Completely envirnment/reaction based.  I would like it to Batman (reaction/timing based), but with the added effect of environment effects.  Throw enemies into walls and phone booths, throw them off piers, stuff them into air ducts.
I haven't put many hours into this game yet but I really LOVE this game.
If you are on the fence or maybe just thinking about it, I HIGHLY reccommend get this game, especially at the steam sale price.
I wouldn't reccommend the DLC pack though; most of it destroys the levelling system.  Save the cash and just grab the story missions.

Nearly all the negative reviews I'm seeing are from people complaining that they've been banned.  To them, I would suggest that perhaps they shouldn't have done whatever it is they got banned for.  The one that complains about getting banned repeatedly for trying to evade his original ban actually made me laugh, as did the review that says the game is dead because Three Rings "banned the entire player base" - which is quite simply a lie.  My account and main pirate are thirteen years old and I logged in today with no trouble.  I started playing YPP just after Beta and my characters, with all their ships and equipment, are still playable today because I behave myself.
Personally, I blame the decline of the game on the addition of some lame new content over the years.  They should have just stuck to pirates and not added Atlanteans and some of the other silliness, like pointless collectable trophies.  The game was better without such distractions.  They did add new puzzles over time until all the trade crafts had their own games, but much of the new content was a bit silly, in my opinion, and spoiled the simplistic beauty of what the game had been originally.
That being said, I would LOVE to see YPP reinvigorated.  My wife and I would certainly play again if they manage to breathe new life into this old ocean.
I still avow that Puzzle Pirates had the best game economy of any MMO I've ever played - and I've played a lot of them in my thirty-odd years of gaming.  On the surface, YPP appears almost childishly simple, but the economy was deeply complex and involved.  Shops needed to be supplied with materials that the ships brought to port.  Some commodities were only grown on distant islands, while others could only be had by pillaging - and to go pillaging, you needed to buy supplies from the shops, so there was a synergy to it unlike anything else I've seen before or since.  A real, working economy.  Simply brilliant - the true genius of this game.
From a social aspect too, YPP was great.  You could get deep into the politics as well as the economy when there were still crews with hundreds of active players roaming the seas every night, all chatting away and having a grand time.  Night after night of sailing with the same folk, you got to know each other and there was a real cameraderie, and even the occasional romance.  My wife and I met playing this game, in fact, now approaching our tenth anniversary!
Gone are the days when you'd see multiple Grand Frigates on the battle map, each with a crew of 100 players all hungry for plunder, but as far as cooperative puzzle games go, I would imagine you'll be hard pressed to find anything better than this, even now.  And you can still sail a sloop by yourself.
Woah, so good. I had loads of fun with it.

TL;DR It's an acquired taste.
Are you one of those people who think quaint is adorable and nurse a private curiosity for all the quirks in this world like it’s a badge of honour? Well, then! This may be the game for you. But then again it may not be, as I'm one of those people and yet I still failed to enjoy this game.
If you received
for free or in a random bundle, there isn't too much harm in trying it out. If that's not the case and for some crazy reason you're thinking of buying it, I desperately urge you to reconsider because I don't know what I've been doing for two hours listening to the horrendous singing in this point and click detective story.
I got my copy like a lot of others, through my Humble Bundle purchase. The content is exactly what you see in the game trailer above where you get to click on things and listen to the characters talk/give clues into the case you're on while you, as the player are immobilised while characters sing their hearts out with a monotonous atmosphere.
I played this for an hour on my own but then I closed it but when I tried to play it again the next day. It had failed to keep my progress so I spent the remainder of my time using a walkthrough to push through. I like to try and finish games but this one was more like, 'Come too far to turn back at this point...' I'd got stuck anyway as I hadn't thought to look under Devon's bed and was running around in circles. If you stick to reading/exhausting everything then you won't get stumped as easily as there is literally nothing that you can do wrong in this game to change an outcome. There is a choice at the very end but even that has little merit to game play so meh. This is still a preference of mine for point and click mystery titles as it keeps the experience pleasant (if a little boring) and away from unwarranted stress. I don't actually play this genre after becoming overly frustrated whilst playing
as a little girl (even though it's now a classic).
But with Pamplemousse it is akin to watching a tragic and horrific instalment of musical theatre and not being able to up and leave because you're lodged smack in the centre of a hot, stuffy hall along with all the other people who also are not enjoying themselves but ended up stuck there. I can only imagine how hard the creator worked to make this so I'm appalled at myself for having to leave such a negative review but as a game this feels more like those demo CDs you used to get for free in the 90s after buying some other popular game.
What's great is that you can multitask while in game, though. It opened in my Adobe Flash Player and so I could keep it running and minimise it while checking my email or I could keep focused on the story while eating dinner. You can also click to fast-forward/skip the talking in between though you have to put up with all the singing.
The story is all right and the characters are likeable. It was fantastic to see a genderqueer protagonist and also watch how the other characters started flailing at whether Dominique was "a girl or boy". It has light humour but you'll have to lower your expectations more and also find a way to get past the horrendous singing. I actually could take it no longer (though the voice acting was solid) and watched/played it like a black and white silent film by taking out my earphones and reading the subtitles for half of the game.
Though it is all right to play yourself if you're set on doing so and have the time as well as patience (the singing... it burns!!), the
is a good way to breeze through it in half an hour if you'd prefer.
Unfortunately, I dislike this game the most out of all the Steam games I've played so far. :( It's cute but I will not touch this game(?) ever again.

This review will be separated into three parts: TECHNICAL, WRITING, and OVERALL.
On a surface level, this visual novel is surprisingly well-constructed. The artwork is crisp and well-drawn (artist is peg and you can find more of their work
), the score is pleasing to the ears and never feels worn out or tiring, and the sound direction is very solid. The dialogue text display is easy on the eyes by default (you can change the opacity of the dialogue text box). I would've chosen a slightly better font, but that's minor and entirely preferential. The voice actors chosen for this game (side note: not all the dialogue is voiced) are very skilled as is apparent by their work here. Not a single character felt like the VA behind them was mismatched, and a few of them absolutely shone out above the rest. The localization of the actual dialogue is also an extreme selling point. The folks at MangaGamer show genuine care for the product they are localizing for stateside release and it shows in the (verified!) high translation quality and stellar editing of the dialogue which helped give the visual novel life.
Once you get past the fact that the game revolves around a pair of lesbian ghosts, the visual novel is...surprisingly grounded in reality. The characters, for the most part, are realistic without being uninteresting (a few of the characters, specifically Koba Youka, I've grown to be very fond of and am astonished at how especially good their characterization was), and the interpersonal relationships are plausible without being lackluster. I haven't read the original Japanese text, so I can't verify if it was originally written as such or if it was the (high-grade) localization that makes it seem this way, but engaging with the dialogue in this visual novel was very rewarding throughout. This all being said, there was one relationship in particular that drew some mixed reception; the teacher-student relationship. In all honesty, it was somewhat awkward and felt a bit rushed, but it was nowhere close to a dealbreaker for me.
I don't read many visual novels, but I do engage with plenty of yuri media. And Kindred Spirits on the Roof is one of the finest entries in both of those categories. Do I consider it worth the $34.99? Honestly, I don't know. It does seem to be a bit on the pricier side (especially since STEINS;GATE is the same price and that's longer and more comprehensive), so on the occasional chance that this visual novel goes on sale, please do get it. It's a truly fantastic work.

Highly recommended. Finishing the game 100% (including reading all the extras) took me 23 hours, and I read at a pretty fast pace. There were so many different couples with problems of varying levels of complexity, but all of it felt fresh and fun. I love how closely-acquainted the reader gets to feel with all of the girls through the eyes of Yuna, and I also love how more context and background is provided for characters (in the extras) in relationships that may have felt sudden or contrived in the main story.
There were only two things that really annoyed me:
1) The game slows down drastically every couple of minutes of gameplay--which I'm sure most reviews have already complained about. The solution for me was to save immediately and close the game before it froze completely.
2) Some of the voices for the girls were way too squeaky for my taste. This may not be as much of an issue for someone else, but I'll just put that out there. I got by by clicking and reading quickly, though I suppose it would have been easier to just mute.
Another thing, there IS a relationship that occurs between a student and a teacher if that sort of thing really squicks anyone out. However, the teacher is very considerate and never holds her status as an adult over the student to make her do sexual things.
Anyway, I love ONYS/KSOTR and all of the girls so so much. I'm ridiculously thankful that I got to live vicariously through these complex characters who struggled and overcame to share their love with their friends and girlfriends ♥

Over the past 2 weeks or so I have read this VN, read all of the extra scenes afterwards and listened to all of the audio dramas...and I still want more. It took me a quite a bit put into words what I love so much about this game, and I'm not going to be comprehensive here. Lets just be clear that this VN touched me deeply and I won't ever forget it. I'm going to just ramble about the things I love about it.
I love the painted art, both the character designs and backgrounds. There are so many great/cute CGs that are perfectly used throughout the game. Aika petting Youka on the head, Umi braiding Sasa's hair, the Kindred Spirits and Yuna drinking coke on the roof...many more.
I love the frank way the story handles homosexuality, how it doesn't ignore the closeminded people who think this love is just a phase between 2 girlfriends, but it also completely debunks that silliness. Throughout the 30 hours of content, this story is all about legitimizing yuri romance as equal to any other kind of romance. It does this naturally too, through its characters and dialog. The sparse "h-scenes" also do a good job of supporting that, and they aren't explicit or too long. These scenes are used for character development rather than just titilation, and their inclusion is very important to the arc of each couple.
And I love those couples, Youka and Aki are my favorite... all of them are sweet and wonderful though. Throughout the game there's a real sense that these folks love each other from the way they talk and think, it's so heartwarming. The drama is smart and never overblown, and the resolution is always satisfying. Not just the romantic couples, the friend couples are a treat to listen to as well. Yuna and Ano have a wonderful discussion towards the end of the game that is pretty much exactly what I needed to hear in a game like this. Everything regarding the characters and dialog work perfectly.
There are some presentation problems, the music is good but there's too little of it. The art is unfortunately low res and sparse sound effects are sometimes very bad. Even with those misgivings and the rather high price point, this yuritopia is highly recommended. It is worth your money.

Hey!  You you like Castle Crashers?  Do you like games with really unique premises and art styles?  Then get Foul Play!
Foul Play plays out like the best of the side-scrolling brawlers of yesterday and today.  Anyone who's played Castle Crashers or the Scott Pilgrim game will feel right at home.  The key difference here is the atmosphere and art style.
The entire game plays out on one huge stage, with all of the characters being actors in a play.  When defeated, enemies will crawl offstage once the spotlight leaves them.  The scenery moves around between stages, complete with stage crew running back and forth.  The audience will respond to your performance, complete with heckling for poor fighting.
All in all, this is a solid game all-around, and highly recommended.

The fighting engine is one of the better ones for 2d fighting games in a long time. Single player modes aside, it was clear from all the previews and promos before the game was launched that this was going to be a multiplayer focused title, as a fighting game should be.
There's in-game tools to let anybody #riseup to competitive levels.
The training mode is great, letting you set up post-grounded and blocking responses from the dummy, and lets you queue up for matches (with the option to set in rank, casual, connection settings) while you practice, so there's never any real down time.
The biggest tool the game provides though, is the replay mode. The CFN system tracks -every- recent batch of replay for every player online. That means you can download and watch all the top-ranking players and learn from them, as well as watching your own wins and losses to see what part of your game you need to work on. This is a very under utilized feature that beginners tend to ignore, but when used properly will let any beginner see what the next step of progression would be.
That and the continual free updates for modes, characters, and balance changes will continue to add value to this title.
Casuals beware, this isn't worth full sticker price for someone who don't want to invest time and effort to enjoy gameplay, but for anybody else that wants to challenge themselves against others I would suggest this title to anybody who wants to get into the vast and deep world of competitive fighting games.
The amount of skill you can gain, the setups with all the unique cast of characters, the way the game works allowing for freestyle ways of playing... this itself would last anybody years for 60$.
Edit: 3/28/16 - The game also now have a very nice demo mode where they will guide you through the entire system of the game, along with trials to better understand each character.

I spent my whole weekend playing this game. I have to say, it must be pleasant for anyone to see a familiar topic been transplanted into games. Indeed, there's been no hesitation for me to buy it since I found this game. But after the whole weekend of playing, I felt a little contradictory for this game. The good parts and bad parts are all very obvious.
If you start your game with Issac Newton, that would be the only correct way to experience the whole story. Start learning in Optics, then turn to Astronomy and Mathematics. Finally, you could hit the finishing line by writing
. The story is coherent and pleasant. Starting from Cambridge, strengthening the power of the Royal Society of London, and finally competing with Hooke in Physics and Leibniz in Mathematics. There always been something to do in every period of the game. Finally, you would become an authority in more than 8 areas, which hit the demand of the final job, writing the Principia.
But what if you’re not playing as Issac Newton, that would become strange. For me, I choose to play as Leibniz in my second round. Leibniz’s initial properties are set to be master of Math, jack of none. That makes me very hard to hit the 8 authorities demand the final topic. What’s more, the only competitor to Leibniz seems to be Issac Newton, which would only happen in the later stage of the game. It would be very boring in the first 3 to 4 hours of gaming. When I finally hit the 8 topics I need, I found that the final topic for Leibniz is still the
. That seems really ridiculous. If you’re not choosing either Newton or Leibniz, the other roles seem to be too old when the game starts. So…choose Newton is the only way to experience this game. One other ridiculous point is that, what if you choose to retire, the game would still count your achievements, and provide you a picture of the
with your name on. So what’s the motivation for me to do my final work?
The gameplay is easy. Researching, Writing papers, Gaining money for the bonus. The game seems to provide some functions to interfere your competitors. But in most cases, there’s no need to do so, because the AI is too weak, you may be ahead of them at all times. The balance of the game, for now, is totally a mess. As it’s still in the Early Access, it may be fixed later. I think if this could become a multiplayer game, it would strengthen the competition a lot.
The System also has a lot to be improved. The UI looks like kind of Paradox, but the game actually is not that complex. The simulation process seems to be too slow. A player’s operation time may be even shorter than the time spent by AI thinking. There still be some crash problems exist now, but fortunately, with the autosave system, it would not affect a lot. One other serious problem is that the game writes the save file in the default location of the Cocos2d engine provided, which is ~/Documents/jsb.sqlite in macOS. That was not a good place to store the save file, cause it may be overwritten by other developing games using the Cocos2d engine.
One spotlight is the Chinese Translation, mistakes are seldom seen. For games with large paragraphs of text to read, it would be a huge improvement to provide a translated version for other language users. I hope the game could conquer the above problems, and provide a much plentiful gaming experience and better system when the game formally be sold. It would be a very interesting and original experience on strategy game with topics on science and researching history.

This compelling game will take you on a journey of scientific progress as you seek an understanding of the world around you. It will teach you the history of science by making you one of the individuals responsible for discovering that science, slowly contemplating the nature of reality while comparing it to your observations (often assisted by tools, some of them invented (and built) by yourself).
It will also introduce you to the political side of science, the competition around the publishing of scientific ideas and the general struggle to advance scientific understanding, including all the dead-ends that can be arrived at (and advanced) before complete understanding is finally achieved.
Though incomplete (at time of review), what is already on offer is fun and compelling. My only wish is for the game to be complete, so I might plow through all of the content at once. This is a game that makes you want to play for hours on end.
In any case, what content is present is enough to satisfy. Very fun, and you'll learn while playing it. I'd recommend it to anyone who loves science and wants to understand it a bit better (and have fun while doing it).
